3.q: A software firm moves its new payroll product from a project into agile product management. Which statement best describes how the product roadmap is treated in agile product management?
o: It is fixed when the product is launched so that development effort stays aligned with the original product vision
It is owned by the delivery team and replaces the product vision as the main guide for development decisions
It supports a high-level product vision and is adjusted as feedback from stakeholders, customers and the market arrives
It sets out every feature in detail with committed release dates for the coming year to give stakeholders certainty
3.w: Agile product managers keep a high-level product vision and align development with it through a flexible roadmap that is continually adjusted from stakeholder, customer and market feedback (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.2.1).

n.0: The roadmap in agile product management is flexible, not fixed at launch; it changes as feedback and market conditions change (book 14.2.2.1).
n.1: The roadmap serves the product vision rather than replacing it, and the product manager maintains them with the team (book 14.2.2.1).
n.3: Detailed long-range commitments contradict the flexible, continually adjusted roadmap described for agile product management (book 14.2.2.1).

3.q: What is the purpose of the communication management approach in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: To describe the agile behaviours and ways of working expected of the teams
To describe how changes to the project backlog will be controlled
To set out the reports that the project manager sends to the project board
To define how and how often information and feedback flow across the ecosystem
3.w: The communication management approach defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, everyone across the project ecosystem (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4, Table 4.1).

n.0: Agile behaviours and ways of working are described in the quality management approach, not the communication management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 4.1, quality practice).
n.1: Controlling changes to the project backlog is set out in the issue management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, issues practice).
n.2: Reports to the board are part of communication, but the approach covers communication and feedback with the whole ecosystem, not one reporting line (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).

3.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, in which process and activity does the project manager first create the daily log?
o: Initiating a project, in the 'agree the management approaches' activity
Controlling a stage, in the 'capture issues and risks' activity
Starting up a project, in 'appoint the project executive and project manager'
Directing a project, in the board's 'authorize initiation' activity
3.w: The project manager creates the daily log in starting up a project, during 'appoint the project executive and project manager', so it is available from the very start (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.1).

n.0: By initiation the daily log already exists; this activity agrees the management approaches for the PID (book Table 13.6, Table 13.1).
n.1: Capturing issues and risks in controlling a stage uses the daily log, which was created earlier, in starting up (book Table 13.1, Table 13.9).
n.3: Authorizing initiation is a board activity in directing a project; the daily log is a project manager's product created in starting up (book Table 13.4, Table 13.1).

3.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
PRINCE2 Agile recommends that personas are written in a cross-functional workshop and kept [?], because the abstraction leaves more room for innovation.
o: fictional
demographic
individual
permanent
3.w: Personas should be fictional: the abstraction from real people widens the room for innovative solutions (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.1: Personas are based on user needs, not demographics such as age, occupation or income (book 6.4.1).
n.2: Describing real individuals removes the abstraction that the book says supports innovation (book 6.4.1).
n.3: Personas are refined as understanding of users grows; the book's point here is that they are fictional (book 6.4.1).

3.q: As a stage draws to a close, who defines the participants for the release planning workshop, sets its dates and invites everyone, and in which process does this take place?
o: The project executive, in directing a project
The team coach, in managing product delivery
The chief product owner, in controlling a stage
The project manager, in managing a stage boundary
3.w: In managing a stage boundary the project manager defines the participants for the release planning workshop (for initiation or for subsequent stages), sets dates and invites all participants (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.3).

n.0: The executive makes decisions in directing a project; arranging the release planning workshop is the project manager's task in managing a stage boundary (book 13.7.3).
n.1: The team coach facilitates team-level workshops in managing product delivery; the release planning workshop belongs to the stage boundary (book 13.7.3).
n.2: The CPO takes part in planning, but the workshop belongs to managing a stage boundary and is arranged by the project manager (book 13.7.3).

3.q:
Which two statements about burn charts in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?

1. A burn-down chart typically shows story points remaining over the days of an iteration.
2. A burn-up chart is mainly a team-level chart of hours spent each day.
3. Burn charts are used in place of budget tracking because cost is the aspect that flexes.
4. An updated burn chart can reveal that a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 3
3 and 4
1 and 4
3.w: Statement 1 describes the team-level burn-down chart (book 12.4.3). Statement 4 is correct because an exception can be triggered by an updated burn chart at iteration or release level (book Table 12.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: a burn-up chart shows completed work against a deadline, usually at project or product level, in story points rather than hours (book 12.4.3).
n.1: Both are wrong: a burn-up chart is not an hours chart (book 12.4.3), and cost has zero tolerance in PRINCE2 Agile, so it does not flex (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Statement 4 is correct, but statement 3 is wrong: what flexes is what is delivered, while cost is fixed with zero tolerance (book 12.3.1, Table 3.1).

3.q: Which principle means a project is planned, monitored and controlled stage by stage, with the project board authorizing one stage at a time?
o: Manage by exception
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Ensure continued business justification
Manage by stages
3.w: Manage by stages: the project is planned, monitored and controlled stage by stage, and the board authorizes one stage at a time, delegating day-to-day control within tolerances to the project manager (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 5.2.1.4).

n.0: Manage by exception sets tolerances for the seven performance aspects so authority can be delegated; authorizing one stage at a time is manage by stages (book 5.2.1.5).
n.1: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships concerns clear roles and engaged stakeholders, not stage-by-stage control (book 5.2.1.3).
n.2: Ensure continued business justification concerns keeping a valid justification, not authorizing the project one stage at a time (book 5.2.1.1).

3.q: At a stage boundary, the release map for the next stage is being updated. Which of the following should NOT be done at this point?
o: Plan the next stage at a high level in the release planning workshop
Break key activities into user stories and update the release map
Define or update the team OKRs for the coming stage
Break each iteration of the next stage into detailed tasks
3.w: At a stage boundary the release map is planned at a high level; the next iterations can be outlined but not at task level, because plans are made just in time. Task-level plans are produced by the team for each iteration in managing product delivery (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.5, Table 13.16).

n.0: This should be done: the release planning workshop plans the next stage and reviews the release map at a high level (book Table 13.16).
n.1: This should be done: the release planning topic breaks key activities into user stories and updates the release map (book Table 13.16).
n.2: This should be done: OKR definition is a topic of the release planning workshop (book Table 13.16).

3.q: Which principle establishes governance by delegating responsibilities and setting tolerances for the seven performance aspects, such as cost, time and scope?
o: Manage by stages
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Manage by exception
Tailor to suit the project
3.w: Manage by exception establishes governance by delegating responsibilities and setting tolerances for benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 5.2.1.5).

n.0: Manage by stages is about authorizing and controlling the project one stage at a time; setting tolerances for the seven aspects is manage by exception (book 5.2.1.4).
n.1: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships concerns clear roles and engaged stakeholders, not tolerances on performance aspects (book 5.2.1.3).
n.3: Tailor to suit the project concerns adapting the method to size, complexity, risk and context, not setting tolerances (book 5.2.1.7).

3.q: At a progress review for a council housing project, the board asks whether the combined level of the project's tracked risks has been falling over the last six iterations. Which technique is designed to show this?
o: Risk register and its status history
Burn-up chart for the release
Trend of project Agilometer readings
Cumulative risk burn-down chart
3.w: The cumulative risk burn-down chart tracks the total risk level across iterations and shows the trend in exposure, ideally falling (book 10.4.2, Figure 10.4).

n.0: The risk register gives the status and history of each risk, not a picture of total exposure across iterations (book Table 10.1).
n.1: A burn-up chart shows completed work against a deadline to forecast completion; it does not track risk exposure (book 12.4.3).
n.2: The Agilometer assesses the risks of agile working through its sliders, not the combined exposure of the project's tracked risks per iteration (book 10.3.1).

3.q: How does PRINCE2 Project Management, on which PRINCE2 Agile builds, define culture?
o: The formal structure of authority and reporting lines in an organization
The set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices of a group
The agreed ways of working recorded in the project's management approaches
The policies and standards an organization requires its projects to follow
3.w: Culture is the set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices; PRINCE2 Agile builds on this when it asks how the evolving culture will be handled in organizational change (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2.3, PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1).

n.0: Authority and reporting lines describe organizational structure, which is only one thing a change may alter; it is not the definition of culture (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2.3).
n.2: Agreed ways of working are written down in the management approaches; culture is how people actually think and behave, and the two can drift apart (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2.3).
n.3: Policies and standards are formal requirements set by the organization; culture is the shared attitudes, values, goals and practices behind behaviour (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2.3).

3.q: Which statement about Kanban is correct?
o: Iterations are optional, because work is pulled when there is capacity
Work is pushed to the team in fixed batches at the start of each sprint
Work in progress is left unlimited so that the team stays fully busy
Each Kanban team appoints a Scrum master to manage its board
3.w: Kanban is a pull system with limits on work in progress; iterations are optional (book Glossary, 14.2.2.1; Kanban Guide).

n.1: Kanban pulls work as capacity frees up; pushing batches per sprint is not how it works (Glossary).
n.2: Limiting work in progress is central to Kanban (Glossary).
n.3: Scrum master is a Scrum accountability, not part of Kanban.

3.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile urge care when applying software testing practices to other kinds of product?
o: Products such as a campaign may not be rebuilt and retested quickly or by automation
Non-software products are tested by project assurance instead of testers
Testing practices are owned by suppliers and cannot be shared with users
Products that are not software do not need acceptance criteria or a Definition of Done
3.w: Software can be built and tested with automation in days, hours or minutes, but a product such as a marketing campaign may not be built that quickly or automatically, so the transfer needs care (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.4.3).

n.1: Testers design and run tests for any product; project assurance monitors governance (book Table 7.2).
n.2: Supplier testing methods are documented in the quality management approach; ownership is not the concern (book Table 9.1, 9.4.3).
n.3: Every product needs acceptance criteria and a DoD; the caution is about speed and automation of testing (book 9.3.2.2, 9.4.3).

3.q: PRINCE2 Agile links each practice to a question it helps the project to answer. Which question is linked to the business case practice?
o: What is acceptable to the users, and how can this be measured?
What now, when a product deviates from what was agreed?
What if something unexpected happens, and how should responses be planned?
Why does the project exist, and what should it stay aligned to?
3.w: The business case practice answers why the project exists and what it must stay aligned to, which is why it underpins every decision on continued investment (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 5.2, 6.1).

n.0: What is acceptable to users and how to measure it is the question for the quality practice (book Table 5.2).
n.1: What to do when a product deviates from what was agreed is the question for the issues practice (book Table 5.2).
n.2: What happens if something unexpected occurs and how to respond is the question for the risk practice (book Table 5.2).

3.q: A delivery team's product owner is preparing the backlog that the team will work from. Which statement describes a product backlog in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: A project-level list of high-level epics that names who will accept the project product
A team-level backlog of detailed user stories that includes or links to the team Definition of Done
A one-page visual summary of the project vision, benefits, costs, users, scope and major risks
A visual plan showing how many releases there will be, when they occur and what each contains
3.w: A product backlog has everything a regular backlog has, plus it includes or links to the team Definition of Done; it holds the detailed stories and is used at team level by the person responsible for the team's outputs (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.1).

n.0: High-level epics and naming who accepts the project product describe the project backlog (book 8.3.2.1).
n.2: A one-page summary of vision, benefits, costs and risks is the project canvas (book 6.3.2.1).
n.3: Showing how many releases, when, and their features describes the release map (book 8.4.4).

3.q: Near the end of a stage, the board of a hospital trust's scheduling project wants to review how the stage went, see the updated release map for the next stage, and confirm that the business justification and risks are still acceptable. Which process has the purpose of providing the board with this information?
o: Controlling a stage
Managing a stage boundary
Directing a project
Managing product delivery
3.w: Managing a stage boundary gives the board enough information to review the success of the current stage, review the updated release map, approve the next stage plan and confirm continued business justification and acceptability of the risks (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.1).

n.0: Controlling a stage keeps the current stage on track and reports progress; preparing the information for the stage-end review is managing a stage boundary (book 13.5.1, 13.7.1).
n.2: Directing a project is where the board makes the decision, but the process whose purpose is to supply the information for that decision is managing a stage boundary (book 13.3.1, 13.7.1).
n.3: Managing product delivery controls the link between the project manager and the delivery team for work packages; it does not prepare the board's stage-end review (book 13.6.1).

3.q: Before each progress review, someone on a PRINCE2 Agile project updates the project and team dashboards and pulls information from them to meet reporting needs. Which role normally does this?
o: Project assurance
Project support
The team coach
The chief product owner
3.w: Project support provides administrative support tailored to iterations and workshops, including updating and pulling information from the project and team dashboards to meet reporting needs (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Project assurance monitors adherence and advises the board and PM; maintaining dashboards is an administrative support task.
n.2: The team coach supports a team's self-management and workshops; reporting from dashboards is done by project support.
n.3: The CPO represents users and owns the project backlog; dashboard administration is not part of that role.

3.q:
Which two statements about how PRINCE2 Project Management addresses people are correct?
1. People is one of the five integrated elements of the method.
2. People guidance starts to apply once the project board has approved the PID.
3. Projects should involve key people critical to success even if they hold no formal role.
4. The people element replaces the need for defined roles and responsibilities.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
3.w: People is one of the five integrated elements (statement 1), and projects must involve key people who are impacted or critical to success even when they hold no formal role (statement 3) (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2 and 3.1, PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: people factors are addressed throughout the lifecycle, from pre-project onwards, not from PID approval (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.5.1).
n.1: Statements 2 and 4 are both wrong: people guidance applies throughout, and the 'define roles, responsibilities and relationships' principle still applies (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.5.1).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: defined roles, responsibilities and relationships remain a principle; the people element works alongside them (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.5.1).

3.q: Which principle states that PRINCE2 should be adapted to suit the project's size, complexity, risk and organizational context?
o: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Tailor to suit the project
Manage by exception
Learn from experience
3.w: Tailor to suit the project: PRINCE2 is flexible and should be adapted to the project's size, complexity, risk and organizational context (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 5.2.1.7).

n.0: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships concerns clear roles and stakeholder engagement, not adapting the method to the project (book 5.2.1.3).
n.2: Manage by exception concerns tolerances and delegation, not adapting the method to the project's size and context (book 5.2.1.5).
n.3: Learn from experience concerns lessons; tailoring decisions may draw on lessons, but adapting the method is the tailoring principle (book 5.2.1.7).

3.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, what is the likely result when an organization does agile without being agile?
o: Short-term efficiency gains that lack a lasting, sustainable impact
A cultural shift that builds long-term resilience across the organization
Lower efficiency at first, followed by a lasting change in culture
Strong adaptability, as the framework's events require critical thinking
3.w: In the 'long-term impact versus short-term mechanics' contrast, doing agile alone can bring short-term efficiency gains but not a sustainable impact; being agile creates the cultural shift (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1).

n.1: A cultural shift and long-term resilience come from being agile, not from doing agile alone (book 2.3.1).
n.2: This reverses the contrast: doing agile alone tends to give short-term efficiency, not a lasting cultural change (book 2.3.1).
n.3: Doing agile alone may mean following a framework rigidly without knowing why, which limits adaptability (book 2.3.1).

3.q: Three delivery teams are each building screens for a new customer portal, and users complain that the teams style their screens differently. Which role is responsible for setting a consistent priority on branding across all three teams?
o: The product owner of each delivery team
The project manager
The agile coach
The chief product owner
3.w: The CPO sets priorities across the delivery teams, for example making sure branding is consistent across every team's products, and ensures user requirements are met (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Each product owner manages one team's product backlog; priorities that cut across teams belong to the CPO.
n.1: The project manager runs the project day to day but does not prioritize the product content across teams.
n.2: The agile coach supports agile adoption at organization level; prioritizing user requirements is not part of the role.

3.q: Significant technical debt means that a team can no longer deliver the remaining Must-have stories in the current stage. Which statement is correct?
o: It is a detail change, handled informally by the team with the product owner
It is an exception, so the project manager prepares an exception report for the board
It is best captured in a lessons report so that other teams can avoid the same debt
It is recorded in an issue report as it affects one product, and the team carries on
3.w: If the Must-haves cannot all be delivered, the scope tolerance is forecast to be breached, which is an exception; the project manager sets out options and a recommendation for the board in an exception report (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.4.2, Table 12.1).

n.0: Losing Must-haves breaches the fixed scope for Must-haves, so this cannot be absorbed informally at team level (book Table 3.1, 11.3.2).
n.2: A lessons report shares lessons to embed them in ways of working; it does not escalate a forecast tolerance breach (book Table 12.1).
n.3: An issue report covers one issue's impact and options; a forecast breach of stage tolerance needs an exception report to the board (book 9.4.2, Table 12.1).

3.q: In a PRINCE2 Agile project with several delivery teams, which role sets priorities across the teams?
o: Chief product owner
Product owner of each team
Team coach of each team
Agile coach for the organization
3.w: The chief product owner represents the user community, owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams, such as consistent branding for every team's output (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 7.2, 7.3).

n.1: A product owner owns one team's product backlog and does not prioritize across teams (book Table 7.2).
n.2: A team coach works with one or two teams on self-management and workshops, not cross-team priorities (book Table 7.2).
n.3: The agile coach works across the organization on systemic blockers to adoption, not on product priorities (book Table 7.2).

3.q:
Which two statements about the team planning workshop are correct?

1. It reviews Agilometer results with the project board and agile coaches.
2. It defines team OKRs and updates the release map for the next stage.
3. Its purpose is to prepare the delivery team for the next iteration.
4. Its iteration planning topic selects stories by priority and estimate to form a realistic team plan.
o: 3 and 4
1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3.w: Statement 3 gives the purpose of the team planning workshop and statement 4 describes its iteration planning topic (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.6.4.1, Table 13.13).

n.1: Both are wrong: Agilometer reviews with the board belong to the agile enablement workshop, and team OKRs to the release planning workshop (book 13.3.3, Table 13.16).
n.2: Statement 1 is wrong: Agilometer reviews with the board and agile coaches take place in the agile enablement workshop (book 13.3.3).
n.3: Statement 2 is wrong: team OKRs and release map updates for the next stage belong to the release planning workshop (book Table 13.16).

3.q: Which two kinds of content does an agile transformation plan combine?
o: Release dates for each product increment, plus a burn-up chart of finished work
Risks to agile adoption, plus the probability and impact of each one
Skills of each team member, plus the training needed to close any gaps
High-level goals aligned to strategy, plus short-term objectives for implementation
3.w: The plan aligns new target states with the organization's mission and vision through high-level goals and adds short-term objectives for practical implementation (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.7.1).

n.0: Release dates and burn charts belong to the release map and progress reporting (book 8.3.2.5, 12.4.3).
n.1: Assessing agile adoption risks is done with the Agilometer and in the agile enablement workshop (Table 13.5).
n.2: Mapping skills and gaps is the team skill matrix; training and coaching plans support maturity (book 7.4.1, 2.7.3).

3.q: How is a cumulative risk burn-down chart kept up to date in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: The team sets the likelihood of each tracked risk at its first planning meeting and updates it in each later planning session
The project manager recalculates it at each stage boundary from the risk register and adds it to the end stage report
Project support updates it every day from the stand-up notes and publishes it on the project dashboard for the board
The project board updates it whenever an exception report is approved and the release map has been revised
3.w: The team defines the risk likelihood for each tracked risk in its first planning meeting and updates the probability in every following planning session, so the chart shows how total exposure changes (book 10.4.2, Figure 10.4).

n.1: The chart is maintained by the team in its planning sessions, not recalculated by the project manager at stage boundaries (book 10.4.2).
n.2: The likelihood of each tracked risk is updated by the team in each planning session, not daily by project support (book 10.4.2).
n.3: The board does not maintain the chart; the team sets and updates risk likelihoods in its planning sessions (book 10.4.2).

3.q: An organization already has its own established procedures for designing, developing and testing products. How does PRINCE2 Agile suggest these are handled?
o: They are raised as a request for change for the change authority to approve
They are recorded in the quality register as planned quality activities
They are replaced by the testing practices in each team's product backlog
They may be used, with this recorded as a tailoring decision in the PID
3.w: PRINCE2 Agile allows an organization's own product design, development and testing procedures to be used instead, recording this as a tailoring decision in the PID (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.3.1).

n.0: Choosing to use the organization's procedures is a tailoring decision agreed in initiation, not a change to an approved baseline (book 9.3.1).
n.1: The quality register records individual planned and completed quality activities, not a decision about which procedures the project follows (book Table 9.1).
n.2: There is no requirement to replace existing procedures; the book allows them to be used and the decision to be recorded in the PID (book 9.3.1).

3.q: Mid-iteration, a team hits a technical blocker. The whole team swarms on it, clears it within the iteration, and none of the team's tolerances are affected. How should this be treated?
o: As an exception, because the iteration plan was disrupted
As a team-level matter, because no tolerance is forecast to be exceeded
As an issue for the project board to decide on at the next progress review
As an Agilometer risk to be rated at the next agile enablement workshop
3.w: A blocker resolved at team level, for example by swarming, is not an exception because no tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; it would go to the project manager as an issue if the team could not resolve it (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 11.4.2, Table 12.1).

n.0: Disruption in itself does not create an exception; an exception needs a forecast breach of tolerance (book Table 12.1).
n.2: The team resolved the blocker itself; had it failed, the next step would be raising it with the project manager as an issue, not taking it straight to the board (book 11.4.2).
n.3: The Agilometer assesses the risks of agile working, such as the level of collaboration; it is not a record of resolved technical blockers (book 10.3.2).

3.q: Which integrated element covers aspects of project management, such as risk, quality and progress, that must be applied consistently and continually throughout the project lifecycle?
o: Practices
Processes
Principles
People
3.w: The practices are the seven aspects of project management (business case, organization, plans, quality, risk, issues and progress) that are applied continually throughout the lifecycle (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.3; chapters 6 to 12).

n.1: Processes set out activities in sequence through the lifecycle, from pre-project to closure; risk, quality and progress are practices (book 1.3.3).
n.2: Principles are the guiding obligations, such as manage by exception; risk, quality and progress are practices (book 1.3.3).
n.3: People concerns those involved in and affected by the project; risk, quality and progress are practices (book 1.3.3).

3.q: An organization brings together people from several functional divisions, and from a partner organization, to work as one team on a new product. Which characteristic of a project does this BEST illustrate?
o: Cross-functional
Temporary
Introduces change
Repetitive and ongoing
3.w: Projects are cross-functional: their teams span functional divisions and sometimes more than one organization (book 1.3.1).

n.1: Temporary refers to the project having a start and an end, which the case does not describe (1.3.1).
n.2: Introducing change into BAU is a project characteristic, but it is not what this case illustrates (1.3.1).
n.3: Repetitive, ongoing work is a feature of BAU, not a characteristic of a project (1.3.1).

3.q: The user group for a hospital's patient portal asks for a new Must have epic, covering repeat prescriptions, that is not in the agreed project backlog. How should this change be handled?
o: Informally, by the team trading it against an existing story of similar effort
Formally, as a baseline change decided by the board or a delegated change authority
By adding it directly to the team's next iteration because it is classed as a Must have
Through an Agilometer reassessment of the flexibility on what is delivered slider
3.w: A new Must have epic would change the project backlog, which forms part of the project baseline, so formal handling is essential and the decision lies with the board or whoever holds delegated change authority (book 11.3.2).

n.0: Adding a new Must have epic changes the project backlog, so it is a baseline change; trading is for detail changes at team level (book 11.3.2, 11.4.1).
n.2: Being a Must have does not let the team bypass formal handling; the change alters the baseline and needs a formal decision (book 11.3.2).
n.3: The Agilometer assesses the risks of agile working; it is not used to deal with baseline changes (book 10.3.1, 11.3.2).

3.q: Identify the missing words in the following Agile Manifesto value. Customer collaboration over [?].
o: comprehensive documentation
following a plan
processes and tools
contract negotiation
3.w: The third Manifesto value prefers customer collaboration to contract negotiation (Agile Manifesto, 2001; book Table 2.1).

n.0: Comprehensive documentation is the right-hand item of the working software value.
n.1: Following a plan is the right-hand item of the responding to change value.
n.2: Processes and tools is the right-hand item of the individuals and interactions value.

3.q: In the quality practice in agile, how is acceptance of products by the users normally obtained?
o: Once, when the complete project product is handed over at the end of the project
Frequently, as completed increments are shown and accepted against agreed criteria
By project assurance signing off each product on behalf of the users
By the project manager confirming that the product register is complete
3.w: Agile seeks frequent acceptance: completed features are demonstrated, for example in the product demo of a progress review, to gather user acceptance and feedback against acceptance criteria and the DoD (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.3.1, Table 13.10).

n.0: Waiting until the end for a single acceptance is the traditional pattern; agile obtains acceptance increment by increment (book 9.3.1, Table 13.10).
n.2: Project assurance monitors adherence to principles and governance; it does not accept products in place of the users (book Table 7.2).
n.3: The product register records product status and acceptance dates; updating it records acceptance, it does not obtain it from users (book Table 9.1).

3.q: On a project's burn-up chart, the completed-work line is rising steadily, but the total scope line has stepped upwards twice during the stage. What do the steps in the scope line show?
o: The delivery teams' velocity has fallen
Work has been completed faster than forecast
Work has been added to the scope being delivered
The cost tolerance for the stage has been exceeded
3.w: A burn-up chart shows completed work against a separate line for total scope; when the scope line rises, work has been added, which moves the forecast finish (book 12.4.3).

n.0: Velocity shows in the slope of the completed-work line, which is rising steadily here, not in the scope line (book 12.4.3).
n.1: Faster completion would show as a steeper completed-work line; the scope line measures the total to be delivered (book 12.4.3).
n.3: A burn-up chart tracks work delivered, not money, and cost has zero tolerance in PRINCE2 Agile (book 12.4.3, Table 3.1).

3.q: Which workshop, held during starting up a project, has topics including user group definition, business option selection, benefits analysis and cost definition?
o: Starting up workshop
Project initiation workshop
Project canvas workshop
Release planning workshop
3.w: The project canvas workshop builds a shared understanding of the project's core elements; its topics include user group definition, business option selection, project vision, benefits, risk, scope, cost and business value definition (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.2.4.1, Table 13.2).

n.0: The starting up workshop covers project roles, lessons review, initiation stage planning, risk analysis and refine planning (book Table 13.3).
n.1: The project initiation workshop, in initiating a project, covers the Agilometer, management approaches, project DoR and DoD, personas, release planning and canvas refinement (book Table 13.7).
n.3: The release planning workshop covers introduction, OKR definition, release planning and wrap-up (book Table 13.16).

3.q: Two delivery teams work on the same project. Team A delivers about 30 points per iteration and team B about 18. The project manager wants to forecast when team B will finish its backlog. What should the forecast be based on?
o: Team A's velocity, as it is the higher and more ambitious rate
The average of both teams' rates, about 24 points per iteration
Team B's own velocity of about 18 points per iteration
The product owner's estimate of the hours left on each story
3.w: Empirical forecasting uses the measured rate of the team doing the work: PRINCE2 Agile says to use your own team's velocity, not another person's or team's, so team B's 18 points is the basis (book 8.3, 12.4.3).

n.0: Team A is a different team; PRINCE2 Agile warns against forecasting with another team's velocity (book 8.3).
n.1: Blending two teams' rates still brings in another team's data; the forecast should use the team doing the work (book 8.3).
n.3: Converting stories to hours returns to actual estimates; agile forecasting divides remaining points by the team's velocity (book 8.4.3, 12.4.3).

3.q:
Which two statements about agile are correct according to PRINCE2 Agile?
1. Agile favours experimentation and quick pivots in response to feedback.
2. Adopting a recognized framework is enough to secure agile benefits.
3. Agile aims to deliver user-focused solutions with less waste and delay.
4. Agile depends on following one prescribed framework rigidly.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
3.w: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: agile favours experimentation, feedback and quick pivots, and aims to cut waste and delay while delivering user-focused solutions (book 2.3).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: adopting a framework does not by itself secure the benefits; mindset and culture must change (2.3).
n.2: Statements 2 and 4 are both wrong: a framework alone does not secure benefits, and agile is less about rigid adherence to a framework (2.3).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: agile is less about rigid adherence to any framework (2.3).

3.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes the project executive from the chief product owner (CPO) in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The executive is accountable for the project; the CPO represents users and sets priorities
The executive owns the project backlog; the CPO approves tolerances for agile decisions
The executive sets priorities across the teams; the CPO owns the business justification
The executive manages day to day; the CPO gives independent assurance to the board
3.w: The executive is accountable for the project and approves tolerances for agile decision-making; the CPO represents the user community, owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: The responsibilities are reversed: the CPO owns the project backlog and the executive approves the tolerances.
n.2: Setting priorities across teams is the CPO's job, and business justification sits with the executive.
n.3: Day-to-day management is the PM's job and independent assurance belongs to project assurance.

3.q: A release review at Ashdown Libraries shows that users struggle with a new search feature, so the team reworks its plan for the next iteration. Which key characteristic of the agile mindset does this show?
o: Adaptability
Empowerment
Respect
Self-organization
3.w: Inspecting what happened and adapting the plan in response is adaptability (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.2).

n.1: Empowerment is about the team's autonomy to decide; the behaviour here is inspecting results and adapting the plan (book 2.6.2).
n.2: Respect is about empathy and open-mindedness towards people (book 2.6.2).
n.3: Self-organization was a Version 1 behaviour; V2 lists key mindset characteristics and uses self-management (under empowerment) (book 2.6.2).

3.q: Why is the release map kept at a high level at a stage boundary, rather than being planned at task level for every iteration in the stage?
o: Plans are made just in time, because planning too early has its own risks
Task-level detail for each iteration is held in the project backlog instead
The project board approves each task directly in the progress review workshop
Iterations are planned once the release they belong to has been completed
3.w: Plans are made just in time to avoid planning too early and its inherent risks; the team plans the next iteration at task level in managing product delivery (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.5).

n.1: The project backlog holds high-level requirements, mostly epics, not task-level detail (book 8.3.2.1).
n.2: The progress review workshop reviews dashboard metrics, risks and demos; the board does not approve tasks (book Table 13.10).
n.3: Each iteration is planned by the team at its start, in the team planning workshop, not after the release ends (book Table 13.13).

4.q: PRINCE2 Agile's fix and flex defaults include a row for benefits. What does that row say about minimum viability?
o: Benefits are flexed below minimum viability and fixed above it
Benefits have zero tolerance at every level of plan, like time
Benefits are fixed for Could haves and flexed for Must haves
Benefits are fixed for minimum viability and flexed above it
4.w: Table 3.1 fixes benefits at minimum viability and allows them to flex above it, in the same way that sustainability is fixed at its minimum criteria (book Table 3.1).

n.0: This reverses the rule: minimum viability is the floor that is fixed, and benefits above it may flex (book Table 3.1).
n.1: Zero tolerance on all levels of plan is the default for time and cost, not benefits (book Table 3.1).
n.2: MoSCoW categories drive the scope row (fixed for Musts, flexed for Shoulds and Coulds), and even there the Musts are fixed, not flexed (book Table 3.1).

4.q: PRINCE2 Agile sets a default position for each aspect of project performance. What is the default tolerance for time?
o: Fixed for Must haves and flexed for Should and Could haves
Fixed for minimum viability and flexed above it
Flexed at team level and fixed at project level
Zero tolerance for extra time on all levels of plan
4.w: By default PRINCE2 Agile sets zero tolerance for extra time on all levels of plan, so deadlines are kept and what is delivered flexes instead (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1).

n.0: Fixed for Must haves and flexed for Should and Could haves is the default for scope, not time (book Table 3.1).
n.1: Fixed for minimum viability and flexed above it is the default for benefits, not time (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Time has zero tolerance on all levels of plan, including team and project levels (book Table 3.1).

4.q:
Which two statements about the PRINCE2 principles are correct?
1. All seven principles must be applied for a project to be a PRINCE2 project.
2. A small, simple project may leave out the 'manage by stages' principle.
3. The principles are not tailored; tailoring adapts how the method is applied.
4. 'Learn from experience' applies at project closure rather than throughout.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
4.w: Statement 1 is correct: all seven principles must be applied for a project to be PRINCE2. Statement 3 is correct: the principles themselves are not tailored; tailoring adapts the way the method is applied (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 5.2; PRINCE2 7 manual ch 2).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: even a simple project applies manage by stages, with at least an initiation stage and one further stage (PRINCE2 7 manual 2.4).
n.1: Both statements are wrong: no principle may be left out, and lessons are sought and applied throughout the project, not only at closure (PRINCE2 7 manual ch 2, 2.2).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: lessons are sought, recorded and acted on from the start and throughout the project as well as at closure (PRINCE2 7 manual 2.2).

4.q: A project board wants independent feedback on whether the delivery teams are balancing agility with control. Which statement describes the role that provides this in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Project assurance monitors adherence to agile practices and governance checks
Project support gives administrative help with iterations, workshops and data
The chief product owner sets priorities so that user requirements are met
The agile coach mentors the organization and removes blockers across teams
4.w: Project assurance monitors adherence to the PRINCE2 Agile principles and agile practices, builds quality and governance checks into iterative delivery and gives feedback on balancing agility with control (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: Project support is administrative support and tools advice; it does not provide independent assurance to the board.
n.2: The CPO represents users and sets priorities; independent monitoring of governance is not part of that role.
n.3: The agile coach helps the organization adopt agile; independent monitoring for the board is the role of project assurance.

4.q: When a customer asks for a change, the supplier works with the customer to agree new priorities instead of reopening the terms of their agreement. Which Agile Manifesto value does this BEST reflect?
o: Responding to change over following a plan
Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Working software over comprehensive documentation
Customer collaboration over contract negotiation
4.w: Working with the customer on priorities rather than renegotiating the agreement reflects customer collaboration over contract negotiation (Agile Manifesto, 2001; book Table 2.1).

n.0: Responding to change is involved, but the key contrast in the case is collaboration versus reopening the contract.
n.1: The case does not set people against processes or tools; it concerns the customer agreement.
n.2: The case is not about documentation versus working output.

4.q:
Which two statements about why organizations need agile are correct?
1. Agile removes uncertainty from complex projects.
2. Complexity creates ambiguity, so one perfect solution is rare.
3. Traditional projects tend to assess quality early in the life cycle.
4. Traditional projects can focus on time and cost at the expense of benefits.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
4.w: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: complexity creates ambiguity so there is rarely one perfect solution, and traditional projects can over-focus on time and cost at the expense of benefits and value (book 2.4, Table 2.2).

n.0: Statement 1 is wrong: agile helps teams cope with uncertainty by adapting; it does not remove it (2.4).
n.1: Statements 1 and 3 are both wrong: agile does not remove uncertainty, and traditional projects assess quality late (2.4, Table 2.2).
n.3: Statement 3 is wrong: a problem of traditional projects is that quality is assessed late, not early (Table 2.2).

4.q: What is the main purpose of a minimum viable product (MVP) in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: To provide the complete, fully tested product that is handed over at project closure
To define the lowest quality standard that the users will accept for every product
To build a basic version of the product cheaply and quickly to gather early feedback
To set the largest scope that can be delivered within the agreed project budget
4.w: An MVP is a basic version built with minimal cost and time so that core features and assumptions can be tested and feedback gathered early; it is then refined from that feedback (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.0: An MVP is not a finished product; it is an early version that is refined from user feedback (book 6.3.1).
n.1: Quality criteria are set through the quality practice and the DoD; the MVP is about testing core features cheaply, not about a quality floor (book 6.3.1, 9.3.2).
n.3: The MVP is the smallest useful version of the product, not the largest scope affordable within the budget (book 6.3.1).

4.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile recommend combining theoretical training with practical coaching on the job?
o: Coaching on the job removes the need for formal training courses during an agile change
Training must be completed before a person may join a delivery team in PRINCE2 Agile
People must understand how to apply the change, not just be told, which reduces frustration
Coaching lets the project manager direct each team member's daily tasks more closely
4.w: People must understand how to apply proposed changes through theoretical training and practical coaching on the job. This combats frustration, a leading cause of demotivation and resistance to change (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.7.3).

n.0: The book asks for both theoretical training and practical coaching, not coaching in place of training (book 2.7.3).
n.1: PRINCE2 Agile does not set training as an entry condition for teams; it uses training and coaching to build understanding (book 2.7.3).
n.3: Directing daily tasks conflicts with self-management; coaching helps people apply the change (book 2.7.3, 2.6.2).

4.q:
Which two statements about the project backlog in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?

1. It usually holds high-level requirements in the form of epic user stories.
2. It includes or links to the team Definition of Done for each delivery team.
3. It shows or links to the project Definition of Ready and Definition of Done.
4. It is owned by the product owner of the largest delivery team.
o: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
4.w: The project backlog usually contains high-level epics (statement 1) and shows or links to the project DoR and DoD from the quality management approach (statement 3) (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.1).

n.1: Statement 2 is wrong: the team Definition of Done is included in or linked from each team's product backlog (book 8.3.2.1).
n.2: Both are wrong: the team DoD belongs with the product backlog, and the project backlog is owned by the chief product owner (book 8.3.2.1, Table 7.2).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the chief product owner owns the project backlog, not a product owner (book Table 7.2).

4.q: In the project closure workshop, which agenda topic can draw on trends from psychological safety assessments?
o: Final handover planning
Lessons report
Final product demo
Progress review
4.w: The lessons report topic of the project closure workshop defines actionable lessons and can include insights and trends from the Agilometer and psychological safety assessments (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.19).

n.0: Final handover planning covers support responsibilities, operational requirements and benefits actions (Table 13.19).
n.2: The final product demo confirms user acceptance and readiness for handover (Table 13.19).
n.3: The progress review topic updates the PID, logs, project dashboard and Agilometer (Table 13.19).

4.q: A delivery team completed 24, 18 and 21 story points in its last three iterations, and 105 points remain in its backlog. If conditions stay the same, about how many more iterations will it need?
o: Four iterations
Five iterations
Six iterations
Seven iterations
4.w: Velocity is the average rate of story points delivered per timebox: (24 + 18 + 21) / 3 = 21 points. 105 / 21 = 5 more iterations, assuming conditions stay the same (book 12.4.3).

n.0: Four iterations would need about 26 points per iteration, above every iteration the team has delivered so far (book 12.4.3).
n.2: Six iterations implies a velocity of about 18 points, which is the team's lowest iteration rather than its average (book 12.4.3).
n.3: Seven iterations implies a velocity of 15 points, below anything the team has recorded (book 12.4.3).

4.q: At a theatre group, two things happen in one iteration: (a) users ask for a small new feature within an existing epic, more valuable than a planned story of similar effort; (b) a story is stuck on a problem that one developer cannot solve alone. Which techniques fit (a) and (b)?
o: (a) swarming, (b) trading
(a) trading, (b) swarming
(a) baseline change, (b) exception
(a) refactoring, (b) swarming
4.w: A valuable detail change is absorbed by trading it for a lower-priority item of similar effort, agreed with the product owner; a stuck story is tackled by the team swarming on it (book 11.4.1, 11.4.2).

n.0: The techniques are reversed: trading absorbs a valuable change by swapping similar-effort items, and swarming tackles a blocker (book 11.4.1, 11.4.2).
n.2: The new feature stays within an existing epic, so the project backlog is unchanged; and a blocker is not an exception unless tolerances are forecast to be exceeded (book 11.3.2, Table 12.1).
n.3: Refactoring improves internal structure without changing behaviour; it does not absorb a new user feature (book 9.4.1, 11.4.1).

4.q: Which role in a PRINCE2 Agile project is accountable for the project and approves the project brief, the management approaches and the project management team structure?
o: The chief product owner
The project executive
The project manager
Project assurance
4.w: The project executive is accountable for the project and approves the project brief, the management approaches and the project management team structure (book Table B.1).

n.0: The CPO represents users and owns the project backlog; approval of these products rests with the executive.
n.2: The project manager prepares these products but does not approve them.
n.3: Project assurance may advise on these products but does not approve them.

4.q: Testing at a leisure-centre chain shows that the new online booking screen will not meet the accessibility standard set out in its agreed quality criteria. Which type of issue has been found?
o: Request for change
Business opportunity
Off-specification
Problem
4.w: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications. A screen that will fail its agreed accessibility criteria fits this type (book 11.3.1).

n.0: A request for change proposes changing a baseline; here the product fails to meet what was already agreed (book 11.3.1).
n.1: A business opportunity is an unanticipated positive consequence; a product failing its quality criteria is negative (book 11.3.1).
n.3: Problem is the general type for an immediate negative impact; a product that will not meet its quality specification is defined separately as an off-specification (book 11.3.1).

4.q: In a release planning workshop for a rail operator's timetable project, each team defines or updates the objectives and measurable key results that will guide its work in the next stage. Which topic of the workshop is this?
o: Release planning
Introduction
OKR definition
Wrap-up
4.w: The OKR definition topic of the release planning workshop defines or updates team OKRs (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.16).

n.0: The release planning topic breaks key activities into user stories and updates the release map, rather than setting objectives and key results (book Table 13.16).
n.1: The introduction opens the workshop and sets the context for the session; OKRs are set under OKR definition (book Table 13.16).
n.3: Wrap-up closes the workshop by confirming outcomes; it is not where OKRs are defined (book Table 13.16).

4.q: What is the goal of agreeing a project Definition of Done in the project initiation workshop?
o: A shared understanding of the quality needed before work is handed to the users or CPO
A shared view of the effort and complexity involved in each user story
A shared map of the skills, gaps and overlaps within each delivery team
A shared understanding of the quality needed before work is handed to development
4.w: The project DoD topic lists product-overarching criteria for work to be acceptable to users, so that everyone shares an understanding of the quality needed before work is handed to the users or CPO (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).

n.1: Sharing a view of effort per story is the effort estimation topic of the team planning workshop (book Table 13.13).
n.2: Mapping skills, gaps and overlaps is the team skill matrix topic of the project kickoff workshop (book Table 13.8).
n.3: That is the goal of the project Definition of Ready topic, which covers what must be in place before development starts (book Table 13.7).

4.q:
Which two statements about progress control in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?

1. Baseline metrics can be set through assessments and then checked regularly using the same metrics.
2. Progress reporting is mainly formal and written, so workshops play little part in it.
3. Progress information is often shared visually, for example through burn charts and dashboards.
4. The team retrospective is the main way to track progress during an iteration.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
4.w: The book describes setting baseline metrics through assessments and checking them regularly (statement 1), and reporting that is often informal and visual, using workshops, burn charts and dashboards (statement 3) (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.2).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: agile progress reporting is often informal and takes place in workshops such as planning, review and retrospectives (book 12.2).
n.2: Both are wrong: reporting is often informal and workshop-based, and retrospectives happen at the end of an iteration rather than to track progress during it (book 12.2, 4.2.4).
n.3: Statement 3 is correct, but statement 4 is wrong: retrospectives are held at the end of an iteration to learn and improve, not to track progress during it (book 4.2.4).

4.q: An IT operations team improves its service desk every week as part of its normal work, using a backlog and short iterations. Which feature would show that a new piece of work should instead be run as a project?
o: It will be carried out by people from within the IT operations team
It will use agile techniques such as product backlogs and iterations
It has a defined end, after which operations takes over the new capability
It will repeat on a regular cycle whenever demand from service users rises
4.w: A project is temporary: it has a start and an end, after which BAU adopts the change. Agile techniques are also used in BAU, so they do not by themselves make work a project (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.1, 1.1).

n.0: Work done within one functional team is typical of BAU; project teams are cross-functional, so this does not point to a project (book 1.3.1).
n.1: Agile ways of working are used in business as usual as well as in projects, so backlogs and iterations do not distinguish a project (book 1.1).
n.3: Repetitive, ongoing work that recurs with demand is a feature of BAU, not of a project, which is unique and temporary (book 1.3.1).

4.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.

In the 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity, the project board reviews the updated [?] and approves the updated release map, or instructs the project manager to close the project prematurely.
o: team dashboard
product backlog
end project report
project dashboard
4.w: When authorizing a stage or exception plan, the board reviews the updated project dashboard and approves the updated release map (and PID), or instructs premature closure (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.4).

n.0: Team dashboards report a team's progress to the project manager; the board works from the project dashboard (book Table 12.1).
n.1: The product backlog holds one team's user stories and is owned by the product owner; it is not what the board reviews to authorize a stage (book Table 13.4).
n.2: The end project report is approved by the board in 'authorize project closure', not when authorizing a stage or exception plan (book Table 13.4).

4.q: After receiving an exception report, the project board carries out the 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity. What does this involve in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Re-planning the team's iterations and assigning new user stories to each developer
Running a team retrospective to agree the delivery team's improvement actions
Approving the team dashboard layout that every delivery team must then use
Reviewing the updated project dashboard and approving the updated release map
4.w: In this directing activity the board reviews the updated project dashboard and approves the updated release map (and updated PID), or instructs premature closure (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.4).

n.0: Detailed iteration planning happens in managing product delivery, in the team planning workshop, not in directing a project (book Table 13.13).
n.1: Team retrospectives belong to managing product delivery and are held by the team, not by the board (book Table 13.14).
n.2: Team dashboards are co-created within each team rather than dictated, and approving their layout is not part of this activity (book 13.4.4.2).

4.q: A project manager wants to set out, for each role used on a PRINCE2 Agile project, the specific responsibilities that the person filling it will carry. Which product should be used?
o: Commercial management approach
Team delegation matrix
Role descriptions
Team skill matrix
4.w: Role descriptions record the roles in the project management team and their specific responsibilities, such as a note that the PM will be mentored by the agile coach (book 7.3.2, Table 7.3).

n.0: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracting, not the responsibilities of each project role.
n.1: A delegation matrix shows who decides and who is involved per decision area; it does not describe each role's full responsibilities.
n.3: A team skill matrix maps team capabilities and gaps, not role responsibilities.

4.q: In managing product delivery, a delivery team refines its backlog, clarifies acceptance criteria, estimates effort and then selects stories by priority to agree what it can realistically deliver next. Which workshop is this?
o: Team planning workshop
Release planning workshop
Project kickoff workshop
Team retrospective workshop
4.w: The team planning workshop prepares the next iteration: product backlog refinement, user story refinement, effort estimation and iteration planning to build a realistic team plan (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.6.4.1, Table 13.13).

n.1: The release planning workshop is held at stage boundaries to define OKRs and update the release map (book Table 13.16).
n.2: The project kickoff workshop in initiation covers team intro, values, skill and delegation matrices and dashboards (book Table 13.8).
n.3: The team retrospective reflects on the last iteration (the good, the bad, the learning, team building) rather than planning the next (book Table 13.14).

4.q: Which PRINCE2 Agile role reviews products against the acceptance criteria and the team Definition of Done?
o: Project assurance
The developer
The team coach
The tester
4.w: The tester designs, runs and possibly automates tests and quality reviews, checking products against acceptance or quality criteria and the team DoD (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 7.2).

n.0: Project assurance monitors adherence to principles, practices and governance; it does not review each product against the team DoD (book Table 7.2).
n.1: The developer designs, builds and maintains increments of the product; reviewing them against the criteria and DoD is the tester's role (book Table 7.2).
n.2: The team coach helps one or two teams self-manage and facilitates their workshops; reviewing products against the criteria and team DoD is the tester's role (book Table 7.2).

4.q: At a stage boundary, the project manager runs a workshop whose topics include OKR definition and breaking key activities into user stories to plan the next stage. Which workshop is this?
o: Team planning workshop
Release planning workshop
Progress review workshop
Agile enablement workshop
4.w: The release planning workshop, held for initiation and for later stages, covers an introduction, OKR definition, release planning (breaking activities into stories and updating the release map) and wrap-up (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.4.1, Table 13.16).

n.0: The team planning workshop is held in managing product delivery to prepare the next iteration and the team plan (book Table 13.13).
n.2: The progress review workshop in controlling a stage reviews project dashboard metrics, risks and a product demo (book Table 13.10).
n.3: The agile enablement workshop in directing a project reviews Agilometer assessments and agile adoption risks (book Table 13.5).

4.q: A team is developing a highly innovative product whose success rests on several untested assumptions. How should it approach its MVP?
o: Use the MVP to explore the key assumptions and validate them as quickly as possible
Delay the MVP until detailed upfront design has removed the main uncertainties
Define the MVP once during starting up and keep it unchanged to protect the benefits
Treat the MVP as the full project scope and extend the timescale to deliver it
4.w: How an MVP is defined depends on uncertainty; in highly innovative contexts it often means exploring key assumptions and validating them as fast as possible (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.1: Waiting for upfront design defeats the purpose of an MVP, which tests assumptions early with minimal investment (book 6.3.1).
n.2: An MVP is refined using feedback; freezing it ignores what is learned from testing the assumptions (book 6.3.1).
n.3: An MVP is a minimal version, not the full scope, and time has zero tolerance by default, so the timescale is not extended (book 6.3.1, Table 3.1).

4.q: A request for change on a school-admissions project needs formal handling. The project manager wants to record it so that its status can be tracked until it is closed. Where should it be recorded?
o: Issue register
Daily log
Lessons log
Risk register
4.w: The issue register captures and maintains the formal issues on the project, including their status, so the request for change is tracked there (book 11.3.4, Table 11.1; PRINCE2 7 manual chapter 10).

n.1: The daily log holds informal issues, required actions and significant events; an issue needing formal handling goes in the issue register (book Table 12.1; PRINCE2 7 manual chapter 10).
n.2: The lessons log records lessons that can be applied to this or future projects, not formal issues awaiting a decision (book Table 12.1).
n.3: The risk register records uncertain events; a request for change is an issue and is tracked in the issue register (book Table 10.1, 11.3.1).

4.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile treat culture as important in organizational change management (OCM), rather than focusing on new processes and tools alone?
o: Culture sets the tolerances within which the project board can approve change
Culture is recorded in the project canvas and stays fixed for the whole project
New ways of working last when the culture evolves to support them
Culture determines which agile framework the delivery teams must use
4.w: Processes and tools can be introduced quickly, but new ways of working only stick when the culture evolves with them, which is why the change management approach considers the evolving culture and how to stop changes being rolled back (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1, 4.2.3).

n.0: Tolerances are set by the business layer and project board; they are not set by culture (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, progress practice).
n.1: The project canvas summarizes the project and its business case; culture evolves over time rather than being fixed in a document (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2.3).
n.3: The choice of agile approach is a tailoring decision made for the project, not something culture prescribes (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, tailoring).

4.q: Early in an agile transformation at Pennant Bank, staff are emailed a guide to the new ways of working and then left to apply it themselves. According to PRINCE2 Agile, what is the most likely result?
o: Frustration, leading to demotivation and resistance to the change
Rapid adoption, as written guidance gives everyone the same understanding
Higher psychological safety, as people can learn at their own pace
Stronger agile sustainability, as no reliance on coaches is created
4.w: PRINCE2 Agile warns that informing people and leaving them to cope undermines change; without training and on-the-job coaching, frustration grows, a leading cause of demotivation and resistance (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.7.3).

n.1: Being informed is not the same as understanding how to apply the change; the book warns this causes frustration (book 2.7.3).
n.2: Leaving people unsupported does not build psychological safety; it breeds frustration (book 2.7.3, 2.7.4).
n.3: Without training and coaching the change is resisted, which works against agility lasting (book 2.7.3).

4.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile describe psychological safety as essential in an agile organization?
o: It lets the project board remove tolerances, since teams will report every problem
Rapid feedback, collaboration and continual learning rely on people being willing to speak up
It means fewer defects reach the product, so testing can be reduced in each iteration
It is a contract term in the commercial management approach for agile suppliers
4.w: Where rapid feedback, collaboration and continual learning are key, people need to feel safe to express themselves, take risks and challenge ideas; this makes psychological safety essential for a productive, innovative agile environment (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.7.4).

n.0: Tolerances remain part of governance under manage by exception in PRINCE2 Agile; psychological safety does not replace them (book 5.2.1.5).
n.2: Testing and quality checks stay part of every iteration; the book links safety to feedback and learning (book 2.7.4, 9.3.2).
n.3: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracts, not psychological safety (book Table 7.3).

4.q: A charity's delivery team holds demos with volunteers at each progress review and releases new features every month. Which pair of organizational change management effects does PRINCE2 Agile link to these two practices?
o: Demos engage users and speed adoption; frequent releases allow smooth, incremental adoption
Demos replace user acceptance; frequent releases remove the need for training volunteers
Demos let the board approve each stage; frequent releases fix the full scope early
Demos record lessons in the lessons log; frequent releases reduce the testing needed
4.w: Progress reviews with demos enable user engagement and faster adoption, and frequent releases allow incremental and smooth adoption of change (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).

n.1: Demos engage users but do not replace acceptance, and frequent releases do not remove the need to prepare people for the change (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).
n.2: Stage approval is a project board decision, and agile projects flex scope below the Must haves rather than fixing it all early (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1).
n.3: Lessons are linked to retrospectives, and frequent releases go with frequent testing rather than less of it (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).

4.q: In managing product delivery, what does the team do about quality while executing a work package?
o: Tells the project manager of completed quality activities and gets products approved
Raises an exception report for each product that fails a quality check in the iteration
Sends a checkpoint report to the project board listing each quality check performed
Updates the project canvas with the results of every quality check carried out
4.w: Executing a work package includes notifying the project manager of completed quality activities and products and obtaining approvals for completed products (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.12).

n.1: A failed check is normal work for the team; exception reports are for forecast breaches of tolerance, raised by the project manager (book Table 12.1).
n.2: In PRINCE2 Agile the team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report, and team-level reporting goes to the project manager, not the board (book Table 12.1).
n.3: The project canvas holds the business justification; quality results go in the quality register (book 6.3.2, Table 9.1).

4.q: A project manager is preparing the operational procedures that will be handed over with a new warehouse system. Which content does PRINCE2 Agile suggest these step-by-step procedures cover?
o: The project canvas, the personas, the team OKRs and the latest Agilometer assessment
Burn-down charts, velocity history and the team plans from each completed iteration
The lessons log, the daily log and the issue register from the project's final stage
Configuration management, maintenance schedules, SLAs and troubleshooting guides
4.w: Operational procedures in an explicit, step-by-step format cover configuration management, maintenance schedules, applicable SLAs and troubleshooting guides, giving smooth, consistent maintenance (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.1).

n.0: These are project-level artifacts used to justify, plan and steer the project; they are not operational maintenance procedures (book 14.2.1).
n.1: Burn charts, velocity and team plans track project delivery; they do not tell operations staff how to run and maintain the product (book 14.2.1).
n.2: Logs and registers record the project's own management; they are not the step-by-step procedures for operations (book 14.2.1).

4.q: In the 'accept a work package' activity of managing product delivery, who produces the team plan showing what can be completed within the agreed constraints?
o: The delivery team
The project manager
The chief product owner
Project support
4.w: In 'accept a work package' the delivery team reviews the work package description or user stories, produces a team plan of what can be completed within the constraints, reviews risks, advises the project manager and agrees to deliver (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.12).

n.1: The project manager agrees the work package with the product owner and team but does not produce the team plan; detailed planning is the team's (book Table 13.9, Table 13.12).
n.2: The CPO prioritizes across teams at project level; the team plan for a work package is produced by the delivery team (book Table 13.12).
n.3: Project support provides administrative help; it does not produce team plans (book Table 13.12).

4.q: A project board at a regional airport wants to see the project's burn charts between progress reviews. Where would the board normally find them?
o: On the project dashboard, from which the board pulls information
In the team plan, which the product owner sends to the board
In the quality register, which records each completed story
In the daily log, which project support sends to the board
4.w: The project dashboard replaces the highlight and end stage reports and shows items such as release status, burn charts, current risks and issues; the board pulls information from it (book 12.3.2.1, Table 12.1).

n.1: The team plan is the delivery team's task-level plan for the next iteration; it is not a reporting tool for the board (book 8.3.2).
n.2: The quality register records planned and completed quality activities and their results, not burn charts (book 9.3.2).
n.3: The daily log is the project manager's own working record, created in starting up; it is not where the board finds burn charts (book Table 12.1).

4.q: How does the Agile Manifesto regard the items on the right-hand side of its value statements, such as comprehensive documentation and following a plan?
o: They still have value, but the items on the left are valued more
They belong to traditional projects and are dropped once agile is adopted
They are valued equally with the items on the left in every agile team
They are valued more than the items on the left on large or regulated work
4.w: The Manifesto states that while there is value in the items on the right, the items on the left are valued more (Agile Manifesto, 2001; book Table 2.1).

n.1: The Manifesto keeps value in the right-hand items; agile teams still plan and document, just with less emphasis.
n.2: The Manifesto is a statement of preference: the left-hand items are valued more.
n.3: The Manifesto does not reverse its preference for larger or regulated work.

4.q:
Which two statements about the PRINCE2 Agile fix and flex defaults are correct?
1. There is zero tolerance for extra cost on all levels of plan.
2. Time may be extended to protect Should have features.
3. Must have requirements are fixed.
4. Benefits may be flexed below minimum viability.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
4.w: Statement 1 is correct: cost has zero tolerance on all levels of plan. Statement 3 is correct: scope is fixed for Must haves and flexed for Should and Could haves (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: time has zero tolerance, so Should haves are flexed to protect the date, not the other way round (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Both statements are wrong: time is not extended to protect Should haves, and benefits are fixed for minimum viability, flexing only above it (book Table 3.1).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: benefits are fixed for minimum viability and are flexed above it, not below it (book Table 3.1).

4.q: Why does a PRINCE2 Agile project keep checking its business case as releases are delivered, rather than checking it once at the start?
o: The chief product owner must re-approve every user story against the project canvas before it is built
Feedback and releases can change the costs, value and benefits, so the project must stay worthwhile throughout
Time and cost tolerances are reset at every iteration, so the business case must be rewritten to match
The project canvas is replaced by the product backlog after the first release, so it needs a final check
4.w: The business case is checked to confirm that the project remains worthwhile as new information emerges, in line with ensuring continued business justification (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.0: The CPO prioritizes the project backlog; repeated checks of the business case are about justification, not approving each story (book Table 7.2, 6.3.1).
n.2: Time and cost have zero tolerance by default at all levels of plan; they are not reset each iteration (book Table 3.1).
n.3: The project canvas remains the business case for the whole project and is confirmed at closure (book 6.3.2.1, Table 13.4).

4.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile relate to agile frameworks such as Scrum and Kanban?
o: It replaces them with its own delivery techniques so that they are not used
It requires Scrum for project delivery and allows Kanban for BAU work
It adds direction and management around them, and the project chooses which to use
It treats them as alternatives to the PRINCE2 processes, chosen stage by stage
4.w: PRINCE2 Agile covers project direction and management as well as delivery, and under 'tailor to suit the project' the project decides which agile frameworks, artifacts and workshops to use (book 3.1, 5.2.1.7).

n.0: PRINCE2 Agile works with agile frameworks rather than replacing them (3.1).
n.1: PRINCE2 Agile does not mandate Scrum; the choice of framework is part of tailoring (5.2.1.7).
n.3: The PRINCE2 processes stay in place; agile frameworks are used for product delivery within them (3.1).

4.q: Which management approach, agreed in initiating a project, describes how data and information will be created, used and managed across the project and afterwards, including security and privacy?
o: Communication management approach
Digital and data management approach
Issue management approach
Quality management approach
4.w: The digital and data management approach covers how data and information are created, used and managed through the project lifecycle and afterwards, including security and privacy; it is one of the progress practice's artifacts (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1, Table 13.6).

n.0: The communication management approach covers two-way communication and tailored messaging with stakeholders, not how project data is managed and protected (book chapter 4).
n.2: The issue management approach covers how issues are captured and reported and how changes to the baseline are controlled (book Table 11.1).
n.3: The quality management approach covers quality methods, agile ways of working and testing, not data handling (book chapter 9).

4.q: A health board's project manager plans to identify key influencers in each clinic early in the project. Why is this useful, according to PRINCE2 Agile and PRINCE2 Project Management?
o: They approve each release before it goes into operational use
They replace the chief product owner in prioritizing the project backlog
They can help co-create products and messages that drive adoption
They hold the authority to set the project's time and cost tolerances
4.w: Users and key influencers can be involved in co-creating products and ways of working, and messaging works better when shaped with key influencers, both of which help the change to be adopted (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3, PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.2, 4.4).
