n.0: Release and acceptance decisions follow the agreed acceptance arrangements in the project backlog and Definition of Done, not approval by key influencers (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, quality practice).
n.1: The CPO owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams; key influencers do not replace that role (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, roles).
n.3: Project tolerances are set by the business layer and the project board, not by key influencers (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, progress practice).

5.q:
Which two statements about the key characteristics of the agile mindset are correct?

1. Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management within teams.
2. Respect refers to inspection and adaptation in response to change.
3. Collaboration builds shared ownership and co-creation of solutions.
4. Adaptability is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
5.w: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management (1) and collaboration builds shared ownership and co-created solutions (3) (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.2). Statements 2 and 4 swap the meanings of respect and adaptability.

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: inspection and adaptation describe adaptability, not respect (book 2.6.2).
n.1: Both are wrong: statements 2 and 4 swap respect (empathy, open-mindedness) and adaptability (inspection and adaptation) (book 2.6.2).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: empathy and open-mindedness are the roots of respect, not adaptability (book 2.6.2).

5.q: Which benefit does a delegation matrix bring to a PRINCE2 Agile delivery team?
o: It fixes the scope of each iteration before any work begins
It reduces confusion and duplicated effort over who decides
It records the velocity that each team member contributes
It lists the user stories that the team has agreed to deliver
5.w: By making decision authority transparent, a delegation matrix improves alignment, reduces confusion, streamlines communication and avoids duplicated effort (book 7.4.3).

n.0: Iteration scope is agreed in team planning; the delegation matrix is about decision authority.
n.2: Velocity is a team-level planning measure; the delegation matrix does not record it.
n.3: Agreed user stories sit in the product backlog and work package, not in the delegation matrix.

5.q: A building society has authorized initiation of its mortgage portal project. Which two named workshops does PRINCE2 Agile describe for the 'initiating a project' process?
o: The project initiation workshop and the project kickoff workshop
The project canvas workshop and the starting up workshop
The agile enablement workshop and the progress review workshop
The release planning workshop and the team planning workshop
5.w: In initiating a project the project manager defines participants for the project initiation workshop and the project kickoff workshop, sets dates and invites everyone (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.4.3, 13.4.4.1, 13.4.4.2).

n.1: The project canvas and starting up workshops support starting up a project, before initiation is authorized (book 13.2.3).
n.2: The agile enablement workshop supports directing a project and the progress review workshop supports controlling a stage (book 13.3.3, 13.5.4.1).
n.3: The release planning workshop supports managing a stage boundary and the team planning workshop supports managing product delivery (book 13.7.4.1, 13.6.4.1).

5.q: A pilot project at Hollins Water produces an agile transformation plan for the wider organization. How should the plan be described in terms of the business case?
o: As a benefit, because it is a measurable improvement in agility
As an output, because it is a deliverable the project produces
As an outcome, because it is the change in ways of working
As a tolerance, because it limits how far teams may change
5.w: An agile transformation plan created by a project is a deliverable, so it is an output (part of scope), not a benefit (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Glossary; official V2 sample rationale).

n.0: A benefit is a measurable improvement resulting from an outcome; a plan the project produces is an output, never a benefit (book Glossary).
n.2: An outcome is the result of the change once outputs are used; the plan itself is a deliverable, an output (book Glossary).
n.3: Tolerances are permitted deviations set on performance targets such as time and cost under manage by exception; a plan the project produces is an output (book 5.2.1.5, Glossary).

5.q: Teams commonly size user stories in story points. What does a story point value represent?
o: A fixed number of hours agreed for each user story
A measure of the business value a story will deliver
A size that means something relative to another story
A score of how far a story meets the Definition of Done
5.w: Story points are the most common form of agile estimate: a points value that means something relative to another story (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.4.3).

n.0: Story points are relative estimates, not actual hours (book 8.4.3).
n.1: Business value is set out in the project canvas and used in prioritization; story points estimate size or effort (book 6.3.2.1, 8.4.3).
n.3: The Definition of Done is a set of criteria that work either meets or does not; story points do not score it (book 9.3.2.2).

5.q: In which workshop are the project Definition of Ready and the project Definition of Done agreed?
o: The project initiation workshop
The project canvas workshop in starting up
The project kickoff workshop
The team planning workshop
5.w: Project DoR and project DoD are agenda topics of the project initiation workshop in initiating a project (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.4.4.1, Table 13.7).

n.1: The project canvas workshop shapes the canvas, scope and user groups; DoR and DoD come later, in initiation (book Table 13.2, Table 13.7).
n.2: The kickoff workshop builds teamwork (values and norms, skill and delegation matrices, dashboards); it has no project DoR or DoD topic (book Table 13.8).
n.3: Team planning refines stories and their acceptance criteria for the next iteration; the project-level DoR and DoD are set in initiation (book Table 13.13, Table 13.7).

5.q: When a delivery team accepts a work package, a detailed plan of what it will do in the next iteration is created. Who produces this team plan?
o: The project manager
The delivery team
The chief product owner
Project support
5.w: The team plan is produced by the delivery team when it accepts a work package; it is a detailed task-level plan for the next iteration (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 8.1, Table 13.12).

n.0: The project manager reviews the team plan when authorizing the work package but does not produce it (book Table 13.9).
n.2: The chief product owner owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams; team plans are made by the teams (book Table 7.2).
n.3: Project support gives administrative and planning help but does not produce the team's plan (book Table 7.2).

5.q: The project backlog shows or links to the project Definition of Ready and Definition of Done. Which management product do these come from?
o: The commercial management approach
The team plan
The quality management approach
The project canvas
5.w: The project backlog should show or link to the project DoR and DoD taken from the quality management approach, and name who accepts the project product (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.1).

n.0: The commercial management approach can support agile contracts, but it is not the source of the project DoR and DoD (book Table 7.3, 8.3.2.1).
n.1: A team plan covers one iteration's tasks; the project-level DoR and DoD come from the quality management approach (book 8.3.2, 8.3.2.1).
n.3: The project canvas sets out the business justification and scenarios; quality criteria come from the quality management approach (book 6.3.2, 8.3.2.1).

5.q: How do frequent releases support organizational change management, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
o: They allow the change to be adopted incrementally and smoothly
They let the teams postpone testing until the final release
They remove the need for a benefits management approach
They let the project board leave out stage boundaries
5.w: Frequent releases support OCM by allowing incremental and smooth adoption of the change (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).

n.1: Agile projects test frequently, and frequent testing is itself listed as an OCM enabler because it increases user engagement (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).
n.2: Frequent releases bring benefits earlier, which the benefits management approach still plans and reviews (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, business case practice).
n.3: Management stages and their boundaries remain part of PRINCE2 Agile governance whatever the release frequency (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, processes).

5.q: A garden-centre chain is planning an agile project for an online ordering service. How does PRINCE2 Agile describe a minimum viable product (MVP)?
o: A basic version built with minimal cost and time to gather early feedback
The finished product with every Must, Should and Could have delivered
The lowest-cost business option chosen when the project canvas is drafted
The set of products that must be handed over at project closure
5.w: An MVP is a basic version of the product, built with minimal cost and time, so the team can gather early feedback and test core features; it is refined using that feedback (book 6.3.1).

n.1: An MVP is deliberately not a finished product; delivering every Must, Should and Could have describes a complete product (book 6.3.1).
n.2: Business options are compared in the project canvas to choose a way forward; an MVP is an early version of the product itself (book 6.3.2.1, 6.3.1).
n.3: Handover at closure concerns the final project product; the MVP comes early, to learn from real use (book 6.3.1, Table 13.18).

5.q: A product owner says the MVP and the first full release are the same thing. Which statement about an MVP compared with a full first release is correct?
o: An MVP contains all the Must, Should and Could haves, so it is a full release
An MVP is built after the full product, as a cut-down version for user training
An MVP and a full first release are the same product under different names
An MVP holds just enough to learn from real use, so it is less than a full release
5.w: An MVP is a basic version built with minimal cost and time to gather early feedback and test core features, so it holds less than a complete release (book 6.3.1).

n.0: Delivering every Must, Should and Could have is a full product; the MVP is deliberately minimal (book 6.3.1).
n.1: The MVP comes early, before the full product, so feedback can shape what is built next (book 6.3.1).
n.2: They differ in purpose and size: the MVP exists to test core features and learn, not to deliver the full set of features (book 6.3.1).

5.q: A department lets its cross-functional teams decide how to organize their own work. Staff report a stronger sense of ownership and purpose, and morale and productivity rise. Which benefit of agile is this?
o: Organizational resilience and alignment
Responsiveness and innovation
Stronger contract control with suppliers
More efficient teams and engaged people
5.w: Collaboration and transparent communication in cross-functional teams, with teams empowered to self-manage, build trust, ownership, purpose, morale and productivity (book 2.4).

n.0: Resilience and alignment concern adapting to change while serving organizational objectives, not team morale (2.4).
n.1: Responsiveness and innovation come from feedback loops and continual improvement (2.4).
n.2: Contract control is not an agile benefit named in the book, and the case says nothing about suppliers (2.4).

5.q: A project team is deciding whether to build its product through a series of sequential phases or through repeated cycles that each add new features. Which project context covers this choice?
o: Scale
Commercial
Delivery method
Organizational
5.w: The delivery method context concerns the way project work is delivered, such as linear-sequential or iterative-incremental (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.4).

n.0: Scale concerns how simple or large and complex the project is, which affects the formality of control, not how the work is sequenced (book 1.3.4).
n.1: The commercial context concerns suppliers that may be external to the sponsoring organization, not the way the work is delivered (book 1.3.4).
n.3: The organizational context concerns whether the project is standalone or part of a programme or portfolio (book 1.3.4).

5.q: A team is writing personas for a new mobile banking service. On what does PRINCE2 Agile recommend the personas are based?
o: Age, occupation and income data about the users
The job titles of the sponsoring managers
The defects recorded in the issue register
The needs that the users have in common
5.w: Demographics such as age, occupation and income no longer predict what users share, so personas are based on user needs (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: Age, occupation and income are demographics, which the book says no longer predict shared needs (book 6.4.1).
n.1: Sponsoring managers are stakeholders, not the users the personas represent; personas are based on user needs (book 6.4.1).
n.2: The issue register records issues raised during the project; personas start from user needs (book Table 11.1, 6.4.1).

5.q: A retailer's store managers report that customers want to collect online orders in store. The retailer then sets up a project to introduce a click-and-collect service. Which project characteristic is shown by the link between the store managers' report and the project?
o: Change, because BAU spotted the need and the project introduces it
Unique, because the retailer has not offered this service before
Temporary, because the service will be handed to stores after launch
Cross-functional, because store and online teams will work together
5.w: Change: BAU identifies a need for change and projects are the means by which that change is introduced. Here the store managers (BAU) spotted the need and the project brings in the new service (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.1).

n.1: Unique is about how a project differs from other projects (team, supplier, location, timeframe); it does not describe BAU raising a need that a project then meets (book 1.3.1).
n.2: Temporary is about the project ending and BAU adopting the change; the stem asks about the link between BAU identifying the need and the project, which is change (book 1.3.1).
n.3: Cross-functional is about the make-up of the project team; the stem does not describe the team, and the link it asks about is BAU identifying a need for change (book 1.3.1).

5.q:
Identify the missing word(s) in the following sentence.
In PRINCE2 Agile, timeboxed releases and iterations sit within management stages, and the project board authorizes one stage at a time. This reflects the '[?]' principle.
o: manage by exception
manage by stages
focus on products
tailor to suit the project
5.w: Manage by stages: the board authorizes one stage at a time, and in PRINCE2 Agile each stage contains timeboxed releases and iterations (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 5.2.1.4; Glossary, timebox).

n.0: Manage by exception concerns tolerances and delegation; authorizing one stage at a time with iterations inside stages reflects manage by stages (book 5.2.1.5).
n.2: Focus on products concerns delivering well-defined outputs, not the stage-by-stage structure of authorization (book 5.2.1.6).
n.3: Tailor to suit the project concerns adapting the method to the project; the stage-by-stage authorization described is manage by stages (book 5.2.1.7).

5.q: Six weeks after a new case management system goes into operational use, the service manager wants evidence of what users find difficult so that the product can keep improving. Which transition measure in PRINCE2 Agile is intended for this?
o: Step-by-step operational procedures covering configuration and maintenance
Regular feedback loops such as user surveys, retrospectives and structured check-ins
Escalation pathways that name the contacts and timelines for resolving issues
Tailored training sessions supported by manuals and short video tutorials
5.w: Regular feedback loops, such as user surveys, retrospectives and structured check-ins, collect actionable insights that drive ongoing improvement and allow adjustments after transition (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.1).

n.0: Operational procedures support smooth, consistent maintenance and set expectations; they do not gather user insights (book 14.2.1).
n.2: Escalation pathways help resolve operational issues and transfer knowledge; they are not designed to collect improvement insights (book 14.2.1).
n.3: Training, manuals and videos help users adopt the product; they do not collect feedback on what users find difficult (book 14.2.1).

5.q: Where would the project board expect to see trends from Agilometer and other agile assessments while a stage is in progress?
o: On the project dashboard
On each delivery team's dashboard
In the daily log
On the release map
5.w: The project dashboard can show release status, burn charts, current risks and issues, the communication plan and Agilometer or agile assessment trends, and the board pulls information from it (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.3.2.1).

n.1: A team dashboard reports from its team to the project manager and replaces the checkpoint report; the board pulls from the project dashboard (book Table 12.1).
n.2: The daily log records informal issues, actions and events for the project manager; it is not the board's status view (book Table 12.1).
n.3: The release map is the visual project and stage plan clustering user stories into releases, not a record of assessment trends (book 8.3.2.5).

5.q: At a museum's digital project, the team's accessibility tester has resigned and leaves on Friday, which will affect the next iteration. The project manager records this as an issue rather than as a risk. Why is this correct?
o: Staffing matters belong to the issues practice, while the risk practice covers technical uncertainty
It has already happened and needs management attention, whereas a risk is an uncertain event
It was raised during an iteration rather than in a planning session or a retrospective
It affects time, which has zero tolerance, so it has to be escalated to the board as an issue
5.w: An issue is a relevant event that has happened and needs project management consideration; a risk is an uncertain event that may happen. The resignation has already occurred, so it is an issue (PRINCE2 7 manual 10.1, which PRINCE2 Agile builds on; book 11.3.1).

n.0: Both practices can cover any subject; the difference is whether the event is uncertain (risk) or has occurred (issue) (PRINCE2 7 manual chapter 9 and 10.1).
n.2: When or where something is raised does not decide whether it is an issue or a risk; risks can also be raised at any time (book 10.3.1).
n.3: Recording an issue does not mean escalating it; the reason it is an issue is that the event has already occurred (book 11.3.2; PRINCE2 7 manual 10.1).

5.q: What is the recommended maximum number of personas for an agile pilot project or a new product?
o: Three
Seven
Five
Ten
5.w: More than five personas is not recommended for agile pilots or new products; a larger set is possible only when agile maturity is high (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: Three echoes the one to three key user groups prioritized in the project canvas workshop; the persona limit is five (book Table 13.2, 6.4.1).
n.1: Seven is above the recommended maximum of five for pilots and new products (book 6.4.1).
n.3: Ten is well above the recommended maximum of five for pilots and new products (book 6.4.1).

5.q: Which option correctly states the purpose of the risk practice AND how PRINCE2 Agile applies it?
o: To collect and assess issues and control changes to the baseline, by trading backlog items of similar effort
To monitor actual achievement against the plan and control deviations, by updating burn charts at every level
To document the users' requirements and the means to meet them, by checking stories against the Definition of Done
To identify, assess and control uncertainties affecting the objectives, by weaving the five risk steps into the iterations
5.w: The risk practice exists to identify, assess and control uncertainties that would affect the project's objectives, improving its chance of success. PRINCE2 Agile adapts the five-step technique and builds it into planning sessions, retrospectives and iteration cycles (book Table 10.1, 10.3.1).

n.0: Collecting and assessing issues and controlling baseline changes is the purpose of the issues practice, and trading is an issues technique (book 11.1, 11.4.1).
n.1: Monitoring achievement against plan and controlling deviations that cause an exception is the purpose of the progress practice (book 12.1, 12.3.1).
n.2: Documenting user requirements and how they will be met is the purpose of the quality practice (book Table 9.1, 9.3.2.2).

5.q: A water company is deciding how much detail to put in the change management approach for its move to agile working. Which consideration does PRINCE2 Agile highlight as key to making the changes last?
o: The size of the budget set aside for external training courses
The number of delivery teams that will work in parallel
The reporting frequency agreed for the project dashboards
The evolving culture and ways to stop changes being rolled back
5.w: Among the points that shape the approach's level of detail, the evolving culture and ways to make sure changes are not rolled back after the transformation are what make the change last (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1).

n.0: Learning and upskilling needs are a consideration, but the size of a training budget is not what the book highlights for making change last (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1).
n.1: The number of delivery teams affects the organization practice and scaling, not how the change management approach secures lasting change (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.3.1).
n.2: Dashboard frequency is a progress control; it does not stop new ways of working being rolled back (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1).

5.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile recommend that personas are created?
o: By the chief product owner, working from market research before initiation
By project support, using the stakeholder analysis in the communication approach
By the project executive, as part of the project mandate from the business
By a cross-functional group in a workshop that includes development team members
5.w: Personas should be written collaboratively in a cross-functional workshop with development team members, so the people building the product share the understanding of users (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: The CPO represents users, but the book recommends writing personas together in a cross-functional workshop, not by one role from research (book 6.4.1).
n.1: Project support assists with stakeholder analysis, but personas are created in a cross-functional workshop with the development team (book 6.4.1, Table 7.2).
n.2: The mandate triggers starting up; personas are defined collaboratively later, for example in the project initiation workshop (book 6.4.1, Table 13.7).

5.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile describe the agile mindset?
o: Formal processes that guide teams on when to deliver value and how to manage work
Techniques and activities, such as prioritization and workshops, used in frameworks
A way of thinking about work that fosters adaptability and continual learning
Guidelines drawn from the Agile Manifesto that explain why agile behaviour matters
5.w: The agile mindset is a way of thinking and approaching work that fosters adaptability and encourages continual learning, improvement and flexibility (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.1).

n.0: This describes the processes layer of the Agile Onion, which gives structure but does not guarantee agility (book 2.6.1).
n.1: This describes the practices layer of the Agile Onion, the most visible part of adoption (book 2.6.1).
n.3: This describes the principles layer of the Agile Onion (book 2.6.1).

5.q: PRINCE2 Agile prefers tolerance to be set mainly on one area so that teams can absorb variation without causing an exception. Where does it place most of that tolerance?
o: On the length of each iteration, which the team may extend if needed
On the project budget, through a contingency held by the PM
On what is delivered, such as Should-have and Could-have features
On the release dates, which the product owner may move back
5.w: PRINCE2 Agile allows tolerance on what is delivered and restricts tolerance on time and cost: scope is fixed for Must-haves and flexed for Should-haves and Could-haves (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1, Table 5.1).

n.0: Iterations are timeboxes and time has zero tolerance on all levels of plan, so iteration length is not where variation is absorbed (book Table 3.1).
n.1: Cost has zero tolerance on all levels of plan in PRINCE2 Agile, so variation is absorbed in scope rather than budget (book Table 3.1).
n.3: Moving release dates would flex time, which has zero tolerance on all levels of plan (book Table 3.1).

5.q: A PRINCE2 Agile project brings in external specialist advisers to work alongside its own staff. Which technique helps make clear which matters the advisers decide and which they advise on?
o: A team skill matrix
A cumulative flow diagram
A delegation matrix
The Agilometer
5.w: When working across organizations, PRINCE2 Agile suggests setting clear boundaries within which people can flex, for example a delegation matrix showing what external advisers decide or advise on (book 4.3.1, 7.4.3).

n.0: A skill matrix shows capabilities and gaps, not decision authority.
n.1: A cumulative flow diagram shows work moving through workflow states, not who decides.
n.3: The Agilometer assesses the risk of working in an agile way, not decision authority.

5.q: What is the purpose of the project closure workshop in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: To review the current stage, update the release map and plan the work of the next stage with OKRs
To formally conclude the project by confirming the product meets requirements and preparing handover
To review the Agilometer with the board so that the risks of agile working can be reassessed
To demonstrate new features and celebrate achievements before the next set of iterations begins
5.w: The project closure workshop formally concludes the project: it confirms the final product meets requirements, reflects on lessons, finalizes documentation and prepares the handover to operations (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.8.4).

n.0: Planning the next stage with OKRs and the release map is the purpose of the release planning workshop at a stage boundary (book 13.7.4.1).
n.2: Reviewing the Agilometer with the board is the focus of the agile enablement workshop in directing a project (book 13.3.3).
n.3: Demonstrating features and celebrating achievements during a stage describes the progress review workshop (book 13.5.4.1).

5.q: In a workshop at Corvan Engineering, the team coach makes sure quieter members and new joiners are heard, and that differing views are explored rather than dismissed. Which key characteristic of the agile mindset does this BEST show?
o: Empowerment
Respect
Adaptability
Transparency and rich communication
5.w: Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness: every voice is valued and diverse perspectives are embraced (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.2).

n.0: Empowerment is about autonomy and self-management in decisions, not about valuing every voice (book 2.6.2).
n.2: Adaptability is about responding to change through inspection and adaptation (book 2.6.2).
n.3: Transparency is about open information flow and visible work; hearing and valuing differing views is respect (book 2.6.2).

5.q: On a traditional project, defects in a new billing system are found in the final testing phase, months after the code was written, and are expensive to fix. Which problem of traditional delivery does this illustrate?
o: Quality is assessed late, so early chances to fix it are missed
Progress is hard to measure without complicated metrics
Too much focus is placed on benefits rather than on time and cost
Teams self-manage too much, so quality checks are skipped
5.w: One problem of traditional projects is that quality is assessed late, so opportunities to put things right early are missed (book Table 2.2).

n.1: This is a real problem of traditional delivery, but the case is about late discovery of defects, not measuring progress (Table 2.2).
n.2: Traditional projects tend to focus too much on time and cost and too little on benefits, the reverse of this option (Table 2.2).
n.3: Self-management is an agile feature, not a problem of traditional delivery, and nothing in the case suggests it (2.3).

5.q: A new company builds a minimum viable product, measures how customers use it, and then decides whether to pivot or persevere. Which approach is it following?
o: Kanban
Lean Startup
Scrum
eXtreme Programming (XP)
5.w: Build, measure, learn, then pivot or persevere using a minimum viable product is the Lean Startup approach, aimed at getting products to customers quickly (book Glossary; Ries, The Lean Startup).

n.0: Kanban manages flow with WIP limits; it does not centre on MVPs and pivot decisions (Glossary).
n.2: Scrum organizes work in sprints with set events; the build-measure-learn loop is Lean Startup's.
n.3: XP centres on engineering practices such as test-first programming (Glossary).

5.q: A project manager is preparing workshop agendas. In which PRINCE2 Agile workshop is 'OKR definition', where team OKRs are defined or updated, an agenda topic?
o: Release planning workshop
Team planning workshop
Project kickoff workshop
Agile enablement workshop
5.w: OKR definition is a topic of the release planning workshop: OKRs are introduced as a link between high-level goals and measurable outcomes, and team OKRs are defined or updated (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.16).

n.1: The team planning workshop covers backlog and story refinement, effort estimation and iteration planning (book Table 13.13).
n.2: The project kickoff workshop covers introductions, psychological safety, team values, skill and delegation matrices and dashboards (book Table 13.8).
n.3: The agile enablement workshop is for the board and agile coaches to review Agilometer assessments and agile-adoption risks (book Table 13.5).

5.q: A project manager says: 'Our method has four elements: principles, themes, processes and tailoring to the project environment.' Why is this out of date for PRINCE2 Agile Version 2?
o: Version 2 has six elements, adding agile workshops and artifacts to the original four
Version 2 keeps the four elements but renames the themes as agile focus areas
Version 2 drops processes as an element, because agile delivery teams self-manage
Version 2 builds on five elements, adding people and using practices and project context
5.w: PRINCE2 Agile V2 builds on PRINCE2 Project Management's five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes and the project context. Themes became practices and people is a new named element (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.3).

n.0: There are five elements, not six; workshops and artifacts are agile tailoring, not integrated elements (book 1.3.3).
n.1: Focus areas were a Version 1 heading that no longer appears; the themes became practices within five elements (book 1.3.3).
n.2: Processes remain one of the five integrated elements; self-managing teams work within them (book 1.3.3).

5.q: PRINCE2 Agile lists regular feedback as one way agile working supports organizational change management. At which points does it say this feedback can be incorporated?
o: At stage boundaries and in the project closure workshop
In the project initiation workshop and at project closure
In end stage reports and in the end project report
During iterations and after a release
5.w: Regular feedback can be incorporated both during iterations and after a release, so the change is shaped while it is being delivered (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).

n.0: Stage boundaries and closure are governance points; the OCM enabler is feedback built into iterations and after releases (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).
n.1: Initiation and closure are too far apart to give the regular feedback the book describes (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).
n.2: End stage and end project reports are progress reports to the board, not the user feedback loops the book links to OCM (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).

5.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.

When an iteration is running late, the team protects the deadline by dropping lower-priority work, starting with the [?] haves.
o: Must
Won't
Could
Should
5.w: Could haves are desirable but less important and are the first to be dropped when time is short; scope flexes so that time and cost do not (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1; DSDM MoSCoW guidance).

n.0: Must haves are fixed in scope; they are the minimum that has to be delivered (book Table 3.1).
n.1: Won't have items are already agreed not to be delivered this time, so there is nothing to drop (book 9.3.2).
n.3: Should haves are important and are flexed after the Could haves have gone (book Table 3.1; DSDM).

5.q: A team at a broadband provider has swarmed on an integration blocker for a day but still cannot resolve it within the team. What should happen next?
o: The project manager raises an exception report to the project board
The team trades the blocked story for another of similar effort and closes it
The board reassesses the Agilometer at the next agile enablement workshop
The team escalates the blocker as an issue to the project manager
5.w: Swarming is tried first at team level; if the team still cannot handle the blocker, it is escalated as an issue to the project manager. An exception follows only if tolerances are forecast to be exceeded (book 11.4.2, Table 12.1).

n.0: An exception arises only when tolerances are forecast to be exceeded; nothing here says that, so the next step is escalation as an issue (book Table 12.1, 11.4.2).
n.1: Trading absorbs change; it is not a way to resolve or close a blocker (book 11.4.1).
n.2: The Agilometer assesses the risks of agile working; it does not resolve a team-level blocker (book 10.3.1, Table 13.5).

5.q: A product owner asks the team to give each user story a number of story points. In PRINCE2 Agile, what does a story point value represent?
o: A fixed number of working hours agreed for one user story
The size of a story relative to other stories in the backlog
A priority rating showing whether a story is a Must or a Should
A mark awarded when a story passes all its acceptance tests
5.w: Story points are the most common form of relative estimation: a story gets a points value that means something in relation to another story or requirement (book 8.4.3).

n.0: Story points are not hours; they express relative size, which is why they are a relative rather than an actual estimate (book 8.4.3).
n.2: Priority is set with MoSCoW (Must, Should, Could, Won't have this time), which is separate from estimating size (book 9.3.2, 8.4.3).
n.3: Passing acceptance tests relates to the Definition of Done; points are assigned before the work, as an estimate (book 9.3.2.2, 8.4.3).

5.q: A team coach suggests using delegation poker at the start of a PRINCE2 Agile project. What is delegation poker?
o: A technique for estimating the relative size of user stories
A way for the team to rank risks by probability and impact
A collaborative technique for defining decision-making in teams
A game used in retrospectives to rate the team's morale
5.w: Delegation poker is a collaborative technique for defining how decisions are made within teams (book 7.4.2).

n.0: Sizing user stories is done with estimation techniques such as story points or magic estimation, not delegation poker.
n.1: Ranking risks by probability and impact is a risk assessment technique, not delegation poker.
n.3: Delegation poker concerns decision-making authority, not measuring morale in retrospectives.

5.q: In the 'report highlights' activity, the project manager assembles the team dashboards, the project log and changes to the release map. What does the project manager then update so that the board can pull the information it needs?
o: The team dashboard
The team's product backlog
The project canvas
The project dashboard
5.w: In 'report highlights' the project manager updates the project dashboard so that the board can pull information; the project dashboard replaces the highlight report (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.9, Table 12.1).

n.0: Team dashboards are one of the sources the project manager assembles; they report team progress to the project manager, not to the board (book Table 12.1).
n.1: The product backlog holds a team's user stories and is maintained by the product owner; in 'report highlights' the project manager updates the project dashboard, not a backlog (book Table 13.9).
n.2: The project canvas is the agile form of the business case; it is not updated as the regular progress report for the board (book 6.3.2.1, Table 13.9).

5.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, agile ways of working aim to deliver user-focused solutions while keeping which two things to a minimum?
o: Stakeholder involvement and feedback
Change and experimentation
Team autonomy and decision-making
Waste and delays
5.w: Agile favours adaptation, collaboration, experimentation and feedback in order to minimise waste and delays and deliver user-focused solutions (book 2.3).

n.0: Agile seeks more stakeholder involvement and feedback, not less (2.3).
n.1: Agile embraces change and favours experimentation rather than minimising them (2.3).
n.2: Agile empowers teams to self-manage and decide, so autonomy is encouraged (2.3).

5.q: Why does the project manager in PRINCE2 Agile agree work package descriptions with the product owner rather than directly with the developers?
o: The product owner prioritizes stories across every delivery team on the project
The PM has direct authority over the product owner, a version of the team manager
The developers are appointed by the project board and report to the executive
The product owner is accountable for the project's continued business justification
5.w: The project manager is the only role with direct authority over the product owner, who is a version of the team manager role; the product owner then has direct authority over the delivery team members (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.3.1).

n.0: Prioritizing across teams is the chief product owner's responsibility, not a product owner's (book Table 7.2).
n.2: Developers sit in the delivery team under the product owner; they do not report to the executive (book 7.3.1).
n.3: The project executive is accountable for the project and its business justification, not the product owner (book Table 7.2).

6.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, which artifact tailors the PRINCE2 project product description?
o: Product backlog
Project canvas
Project backlog
Release map
6.w: The project backlog replaces the project product description: it holds high-level, mostly epic, user stories and shows or links to the project DoR and DoD (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.1).

n.0: The product backlog is the team-level backlog that tailors product descriptions and links to the team DoD (book 8.3.2.1).
n.1: The project canvas tailors the business case, not the project product description (book 6.3.2.1).
n.3: The release map tailors the project and stage plans (book 8.3.2.5).

6.q: A product owner at a travel insurer hears the team talk about 'trading' when a new requirement arrives mid-iteration. What is trading (or swapping) in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Moving a developer between teams so that the velocity of each team stays roughly equal
Replacing one or more backlog items with new ones of similar effort to absorb emerging change
The whole team working together on one blocked story until it can move forward again
Swapping the order of iterations in the release map so that a release arrives sooner
6.w: Trading, or swapping, handles emerging change by replacing one or more requirements, features or user stories with others of a similar size in terms of effort (book 11.4.1).

n.0: Trading swaps requirements, features or stories, not people between teams (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 11.4.1).
n.2: The whole team focusing on a blocked story is swarming, not trading (book 11.4.2).
n.3: Trading works on backlog items within the planned work, not on the sequence of iterations in the release map (book 11.4.1, 8.3.2.5).

6.q: In which process is the project backlog first created in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Initiating a project, when the project Definition of Ready and Done are agreed in the project initiation workshop
Managing product delivery, when each team refines its backlog in the team planning workshop
Directing a project, when the board authorizes initiation and approves the project brief
Starting up a project, when the project manager works with the CPO, senior supplier and executive on what is to be delivered
6.w: In starting up a project, while the executive leads the project canvas, the project manager works with the CPO, senior supplier and executive to define what is to be delivered and creates the project backlog with its epics (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.1).

n.0: The project DoR and DoD are agreed in the project initiation workshop, and the project backlog is reviewed and updated if needed in initiation, but it already exists from starting up (book Tables 13.6, 13.7).
n.1: Teams refine their own product backlogs in the team planning workshop; the project backlog has existed since starting up (book Table 13.13).
n.2: Authorizing initiation approves the project brief and the release map for initiation; it does not create the project backlog (book Table 13.4).

6.q:
Which two statements about the Definition of Ready are correct?

1. It helps prevent delays by making sure the team has what it needs before starting work.
2. A user story can be ready when it states who, what and why and has measurable, prioritized acceptance criteria.
3. It sets out the checks a product must pass before it is handed to the users.
4. It is agreed by the project board at each stage boundary for the next stage.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 4
2 and 3
3 and 4
6.w: The DoR makes sure items are fully prepared so work can start without delays, and a story is ready when it has who, what and why plus measurable, prioritized acceptance criteria (book 9.3.2.1). Checks before handover to users belong to the DoD (9.3.2.2), and the DoR is a team agreement, with the project DoR set in the project initiation workshop (Table 13.7).

n.1: Statement 4 is false: the DoR is a shared team agreement and the project DoR is set in the project initiation workshop, not by the board at each boundary (book 9.3.2.1, Table 13.7).
n.2: Statement 3 is false: the checks a product must pass before handover to users are the Definition of Done (book 9.3.2.2).
n.3: Both are false: handover checks belong to the DoD (9.3.2.2), and the DoR is not a board decision at stage boundaries (9.3.2.1, Table 13.7).

6.q: At Fernlea Housing, the delivery team keeps its work status visible on a shared board, raises obstacles openly at regular meetings and explains ideas with sketches as well as written notes. Which key characteristic of the agile mindset is the team showing?
o: Empowerment of a self-managing team
Respect for every team member's view
Adaptability through inspection
Transparency and rich communication
6.w: Transparency and rich communication mean information flows openly and is richer than text alone; regular meetings, open documentation and visible work status build trust and alignment (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.2).

n.0: Empowerment is about autonomy and self-management; the behaviours described are about open, rich information flow (book 2.6.2).
n.1: Respect is about empathy and open-mindedness towards others' views (book 2.6.2).
n.2: Adaptability is about inspecting and adapting to change, not about how openly information is shared (book 2.6.2).

6.q: A delivery team in a PRINCE2 Agile project keeps its user stories in a product backlog. Which role owns this team's product backlog?
o: The chief product owner
The project manager
The team coach
The product owner
6.w: The product owner owns the team's product backlog and keeps it aligned with the project backlog, continued business justification and tolerances (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: The CPO owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams, not each team's product backlog.
n.1: The project manager consults on product backlogs but does not own them.
n.2: The team coach helps the team write user stories but does not own the backlog.

6.q: Near the end of an iteration, a team realises it cannot finish every user story it planned. Following the PRINCE2 Agile default for time, what should normally happen?
o: The iteration ends on time and the unfinished lower-priority work is reprioritised
The iteration is extended until all of the planned user stories are finished
The project board is asked to approve extra time for this iteration
The iteration is cancelled and replanned from the start with a longer duration
6.w: Time has zero tolerance at all levels of plan, including the iteration timebox, while Should and Could haves can flex. The timebox ends as planned and unfinished work goes back for prioritisation (book Table 3.1, Glossary).

n.1: Extending the iteration breaks the fixed timebox; time has zero tolerance by default (Table 3.1).
n.2: Iterations are timeboxes with zero time tolerance; the board does not grant extra time for an iteration (Table 3.1).
n.3: Cancelling and lengthening the timebox flexes time, which is fixed by default (Table 3.1).

6.q: Which responsibility belongs to the tester role in a PRINCE2 Agile delivery team?
o: Designing, building and maintaining the increments of the team's product
Reviewing products against acceptance criteria and the team Definition of Done
Preparing user stories and keeping the product backlog aligned to the project
Helping the team to self-manage, refine its processes and resolve conflicts
6.w: The tester designs, runs and possibly automates tests and quality reviews and reviews products against acceptance or quality criteria and the team Definition of Done (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Designing, building and maintaining increments is the developer's responsibility.
n.2: Preparing user stories and aligning the product backlog is the product owner's responsibility.
n.3: Supporting self-management, process refinement and conflict resolution is the team coach's role.

6.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile pair MoSCoW prioritization with zero tolerance on time and cost?
o: So the deadline can move when Must haves take longer than estimated
So every feature in the backlog is delivered by the agreed end date
So extra budget can be released for Should haves at each stage end
So lower-priority features can flex to protect the agreed time and cost
6.w: Agile allows tolerance on what is delivered while restricting time and cost; MoSCoW shows which features can flex (Should and Could haves) when time or cost is under pressure (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1, Table 5.1).

n.0: Time has zero tolerance on all levels of plan; the response to pressure is to flex lower-priority scope (book Table 3.1).
n.1: MoSCoW assumes not everything will be delivered; Should and Could haves may be dropped (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Cost also has zero tolerance; Should haves flex rather than attracting extra money (book Table 3.1).

6.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.

The purpose of the [?] process is to provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed.
o: managing a stage boundary
directing a project
controlling a stage
closing a project
6.w: Closing a project provides a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed and the achievement of objectives recognized (PRINCE2 7 manual 19.1; PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.18 'confirm project acceptance').

n.0: Managing a stage boundary prepares information for the board's review of a stage and the next stage plan; it is not the final acceptance point (book 13.7.1).
n.1: Directing a project includes the board authorizing closure, but the process whose purpose is the fixed point for confirming acceptance is closing a project (book 13.3.1).
n.2: Controlling a stage keeps the work of a stage within tolerances; it does not provide the project's acceptance point (book 13.5.1).

6.q: Which statement about the 'controlling a stage' process in PRINCE2 Agile is correct?
o: It begins with the first delivery stage, so the work of the initiation stage is controlled by directing a project
It is the process in which the board approves each release map update and confirms continued business justification
It is normally first used once the project is authorized, but it can be used during initiation for large or complex projects
It is the process in which the delivery team produces a team plan and agrees to deliver each work package
6.w: Controlling a stage assigns and monitors work, handles issues, reports progress and takes corrective action to keep the stage within tolerances. It is normally first used after authorization but may be used in initiation for large or complex projects (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.5.1).

n.0: The book allows controlling a stage to be used during initiation for large or complex projects; directing a project is the board's process, not day-to-day control (book 13.5.1, 13.3.1).
n.1: Approving the next stage plan and confirming business justification happen at stage boundaries, supported by managing a stage boundary and directing a project (book 13.7.1).
n.3: Producing a team plan and agreeing to deliver work belong to the 'accept a work package' activity in managing product delivery (book Table 13.12).

6.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.

In an OKR, the [?] are specific, measurable outcomes that show how far a team has moved towards its clear, aspirational goal.
o: objectives
acceptance criteria
key results
story points
6.w: Key results are the specific, measurable outcomes that show progress towards the objective, which is the clear, aspirational goal (PRINCE2 Agile V2 Glossary, book 12.3.2.3).

n.0: Objectives are the clear, aspirational goals themselves, not the measures of progress towards them (Glossary).
n.1: Acceptance criteria state what a user story must satisfy to be accepted; they are not part of an OKR (book Table 13.13).
n.3: Story points are relative estimates for user stories, not outcomes set in an OKR (book 8.4.3).

6.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile describe the 'manage by exception' principle as being at the heart of empowering people to self-manage?
o: Clear tolerances let teams make their own decisions while the board stays in control
Exceptions are raised by teams directly to the board, bypassing the project manager
Teams agree their own tolerances each iteration without reference to the board
The board reviews every user story, so teams know exactly what to build next
6.w: Manage by exception lets people self-manage within agreed tolerances while the project keeps the right level of governance; decisions inside the limits stay with the team, and only forecast breaches are escalated (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 5.1, 5.2.1.5).

n.1: Escalation follows the governance structure: deviations beyond tolerance go through the project manager to the board, not around the project manager (book 5.2.1.5, Table 12.1).
n.2: Tolerances are set by the level above (the board sets project and stage tolerances); teams work within them rather than setting their own (book 5.2.1.5).
n.3: A board reviewing every user story would be the opposite of management by exception, which delegates day-to-day decisions (book 5.2.1.5).

6.q: Under the 'manage by exception' principle, a project board sets tolerances so it can delegate authority. Against which aspects of project performance can these tolerances be set?
o: The six aspects: time, cost, quality, scope, benefits and risk
The seven aspects: benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk
The three aspects of time, cost and quality, as the classic project triangle
The four aspects of time, cost, scope and benefits, with quality left to teams
6.w: Manage by exception sets tolerances for the seven performance aspects: benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 5.2.1.5, 1.3.2).

n.0: This is the older six-aspect set without sustainability; PRINCE2 7 and PRINCE2 Agile V2 use seven aspects (book 1.3.2, 5.2.1.5).
n.2: The time, cost and quality triangle is not the PRINCE2 set; tolerances cover all seven aspects, including scope, benefits, sustainability and risk (book 5.2.1.5).
n.3: Quality is one of the seven aspects with tolerances set through governance, and sustainability and risk are also included (book 5.2.1.5).

6.q: What does PRINCE2 Agile mean by rich communication?
o: Sharing emotions, body language and visuals as well as words
The belief that any person can learn, adapt to change and grow
A leader serving the team and putting members' needs first
Combining theoretical training with practical coaching on the job
6.w: Rich communication conveys not just words but emotions, body language, visuals and graphics, to reduce misunderstandings in short agile iterations (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.7.3).

n.1: This is the growth mindset, often seen as the core of the agile mindset (book 2.7.3).
n.2: This is servant leadership, credited to Robert Greenleaf (book 2.7.3).
n.3: This is training and coaching, which helps people apply the changes (book 2.7.3).

6.q: At the project kickoff workshop, a project manager presents one fixed team dashboard design that every delivery team must adopt. Why does this conflict with PRINCE2 Agile guidance?
o: Team dashboards should be co-created within each team to support self-management
Team dashboards are designed by the board during the agile enablement workshop
Team dashboards are not created until the first release planning workshop
Team dashboards should be designed by project assurance to keep them independent
6.w: In the project kickoff workshop each team co-creates its own dashboard for transparency, accountability and quick insight into progress; dictating one design works against self-management (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.4.4.2, Table 13.8).

n.1: The agile enablement workshop is where the board and agile coaches review Agilometer assessments, not where team dashboards are designed (book Table 13.5).
n.2: Team dashboards are a topic of the project kickoff workshop in initiating a project, earlier than release planning (book Table 13.8).
n.3: Project assurance monitors adherence to principles and practices; designing team dashboards is the teams' own work (book Table 7.2, 13.4.4.2).

6.q: Which statement about the people element of PRINCE2 Project Management is correct?
o: It covers the project board members and leaves out the users affected by the change
It covers both the people working on the project and the people affected by it
It was one of the four integrated elements in earlier editions of PRINCE2
It replaces the organization practice in projects that use agile delivery
6.w: The people element covers the needs, capabilities and motivations of everyone involved, including those working on the project and those affected by it (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2; PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.3, chapter 4).

n.0: People is not limited to the board: it includes those working on the project and those affected by the change (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2).
n.2: The older four elements were principles, themes, processes and tailoring to the project environment; people became a named element in PRINCE2 7 (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2).
n.3: The organization practice remains one of the seven practices in PRINCE2 Agile; the people element does not replace it (book chapter 7).

6.q: Which statement best describes the difference between the story map and the release map in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The story map is the project plan; the release map is the team's task-level plan for the next iteration
The story map is part of the business case; the release map is part of the quality management approach
The story map breaks the products into user stories; the release map groups them into releases over time
The story map sets the order of priority; the release map shows the products as a component hierarchy
6.w: The story map is the breakdown (products into user stories), and the release map is the plan built from it, clustering stories into releases with deadlines (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.4, 8.3.2.5).

n.0: The release map, not the story map, represents the project plan, and task-level detail sits in team plans (book 8.4.4, Table 8.1).
n.1: Both maps are plans practice artifacts; the business case uses the project canvas (book 8.3.2, 6.3.2.1).
n.3: A component hierarchy is what a product breakdown structure shows; the release map shows releases over time (book 8.4.1, 8.4.4).

6.q: A team notices that work keeps piling up in its 'testing' state while items move steadily through the other states. Which technique is designed to make this kind of bottleneck visible over time?
o: Burn-down chart
Agile maturity assessment
Cumulative flow diagram
Risk-adjusted product backlog
6.w: A cumulative flow diagram shows tasks in each workflow state over time and helps identify bottlenecks, such as work collecting in one state (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.4.2).

n.0: A burn-down chart shows total outstanding work over time, not where work collects between workflow states (book 12.4.3).
n.1: Agile maturity assessments measure psychological safety, agile maturity and agile sustainability, not workflow bottlenecks (book 12.4.1).
n.3: A risk-adjusted product backlog holds risk responses alongside user stories; it does not show flow between states (book 10.4.1).

6.q: Lindqvist Logistics adopts an agile framework, renames its meetings with agile terms and trains every team in the new vocabulary. Team leaders still approve every task before work starts. Which explanation fits PRINCE2 Agile guidance?
o: The organization is being agile, but it has not yet adopted enough agile frameworks, processes and terms
The organization has not yet scaled agile, so the framework should first be extended to more teams
The organization is doing agile, but people are not yet free to apply an agile mindset through self-management
The organization lacks a project canvas, so the value of the change has not been summarized on one page
6.w: Frameworks, processes and terminology are doing agile. Being agile also needs people to be allowed to apply the mindset within appropriate self-management, which task-by-task approval prevents (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1).

n.0: The teams have adopted a framework, processes and terminology, which is doing agile; what is missing is the freedom to self-manage, which is being agile (book 2.3.1).
n.1: Scaling extends agile across many teams and products (book 3.2); it does not address leaders approving every task within a team.
n.3: The project canvas is the one-page business justification for a project (book 6.3.2.1); it does not explain the missing freedom to self-manage.

6.q: The release map serves as the plan for a PRINCE2 Agile project. Which other plan elements should it include or refer to?
o: The budget, tolerances and assumptions for the plan
The team skill matrix, delegation matrix and team values
The Definition of Ready, Definition of Done and test results
The daily log, lessons log and issue register entries
6.w: As the agile form of a plan, the release map includes or refers to the budget, tolerances and assumptions (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 8.1).

n.1: Skill and delegation matrices and team values are organization and people topics set up in the project kickoff workshop, not plan elements (book Table 13.8).
n.2: Definitions of Ready and Done belong to the quality practice and the backlogs; test results are quality records (book 9.3.2).
n.3: Logs and registers are progress and issues records, not elements of the plan (book Table 12.1).

6.q: A PRINCE2 Agile project needs one role to represent the user community, own the project backlog and keep it refined with input from users. Which role is this?
o: The product owner of the lead delivery team
The project executive on the project board
The chief product owner
The senior supplier on the project board
6.w: The chief product owner represents the user community, owns the project backlog and keeps it refined with user input and aligned with the teams' product backlogs (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: A product owner owns one team's product backlog, not the project backlog, and does not represent the whole user community.
n.1: The project executive is accountable for the project and its strategic alignment; the CPO represents the users.
n.3: The senior supplier represents the supplier side, those who design and build the products, not the users.

6.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, what is meant by a growth mindset?
o: A leader serving the team and putting members' needs first
Sharing emotions, body language and visuals as well as words
Combining theoretical training with practical coaching on the job
The belief that any person can learn, adapt to change and grow
6.w: The growth mindset is the fundamental belief that anyone can learn, adapt to change and grow; it is often seen as the core of the agile mindset (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.1, 2.7.3).

n.0: This is servant leadership, credited to Robert Greenleaf (book 2.7.3).
n.1: This is rich communication, which reduces misunderstandings in short iterations (book 2.7.3).
n.2: This is training and coaching, which helps people apply the changes (book 2.7.3).

6.q: A charity's donor app project is approaching the end of its initiation stage, and the project manager is preparing for the next stage. Which named workshop supports the 'managing a stage boundary' process?
o: The team planning workshop
The progress review workshop
The project closure workshop
The release planning workshop
6.w: Managing a stage boundary is supported by the release planning workshop, held for initiation and for subsequent stages, which plans the next stage (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.3, 13.7.4.1).

n.0: The team planning workshop supports managing product delivery and prepares the next iteration, not the next stage (book 13.6.4.1).
n.1: The progress review workshop supports controlling a stage by assessing the current status (book 13.5.4.1).
n.2: The project closure workshop supports closing a project in the final stage (book 13.8.4).

6.q: How does a well-designed communication management approach help with risk, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Listening to stakeholders can surface concerns before they become risks
It replaces the risk register as the record of stakeholder threats
It sets the risk appetite that the board agrees with the business
It removes the need for Agilometer assessments during initiation
6.w: Because the approach is as much about listening as broadcasting, it helps surface concerns before they turn into risks (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).

n.1: Identified risks are still recorded in the risk register; the communication approach does not replace it (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, risk practice).
n.2: Risk appetite is the amount of risk the business is willing to take; it is set by the business and applied by the project board, not set through the communication management approach (PRINCE2 7 manual ch 9).
n.3: The Agilometer is still assessed in the project initiation workshop; communication does not remove that need (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).

6.q:
Which two statements about dashboards in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?

1. The team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report.
2. The project dashboard replaces the work package description.
3. The project dashboard replaces the highlight report and the end stage report.
4. The team dashboard is reviewed mainly in progress review workshops.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
6.w: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report, and the project dashboard replaces both the highlight report and the end stage report (book Table 12.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the work package description becomes a set of user stories agreed between the project manager and product owner, not a dashboard (book 8.3.2).
n.1: Both are wrong: the work package description is not replaced by a dashboard, and the team dashboard is reviewed in team planning and retrospective workshops, while progress review workshops use the project dashboard (book Table 12.1).
n.3: Statement 3 is correct, but statement 4 is wrong: progress review workshops review the project dashboard, while the team dashboard is reviewed in team planning and retrospective workshops (book Table 12.1).

6.q:
Which two statements about communication in a PRINCE2 Agile project are correct?
1. The communication management approach describes the agile behaviours the teams will follow.
2. Working with key influencers from user, supplier and business groups helps to tailor messages.
3. Communication should be as much about listening as about broadcasting.
4. Periodic reports give a full and unbiased picture of how people feel about the change.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 3
3 and 4
1 and 4
6.w: Working with key influencers from user, supplier and business groups helps tailor messages (statement 2), and communication is as much about listening as broadcasting (statement 3) (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).

n.0: Statement 1 is wrong: agile behaviours belong in the quality management approach, not the communication management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 4.1).
n.2: Statement 4 is wrong: periodic reporting alone is not enough and can be biased (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).
n.3: Both statements are wrong: agile behaviours sit in the quality management approach, and periodic reports can be biased (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4, Table 4.1).

6.q:
Which two statements about PRINCE2 Agile Version 2 are correct?
1. Project performance is managed across seven aspects, including sustainability.
2. The former 'change' theme is now covered by the issues practice.
3. The five 'focus areas' remain a separate syllabus heading.
4. The Scrum master is one of the named PRINCE2 Agile roles.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
6.w: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: V2 judges performance across seven aspects, with sustainability added, and the old 'change' theme is now the issues practice (book 1.3.2, Table 3.1; issues practice, chapter 11).

n.1: Statement 3 is wrong: the focus areas heading has gone in V2, with its content moved into practices and people (e.g. the Agilometer into risk).
n.2: Statement 4 is wrong: 'Scrum master' is not one of the 11 named V2 roles; the V2 role set includes a team coach instead.
n.3: Both are wrong: focus areas are no longer a heading, and the Scrum master is not a named V2 role.

6.q: Which artifacts are reviewed in the release planning workshop when the next stage is being planned?
o: The project canvas, the project backlog and the release map
The team dashboards, the iteration team plans and the skill matrix
The personas, the project Definition of Ready and the delegation matrix
The final product demo, the lessons report and the handover plan
6.w: The release planning workshop reviews the project canvas, the project backlog and the release map to plan the next stage (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.4.1).

n.1: Team dashboards and team plans are reviewed at team level in managing product delivery, and the skill matrix is a kickoff topic (book Table 12.1, Table 13.8).
n.2: Personas and the project Definition of Ready are project initiation workshop topics, and the delegation matrix is a kickoff topic (book Table 13.7, Table 13.8).
n.3: The final product demo, lessons report and handover planning are topics of the project closure workshop (book Table 13.19).

6.q: A team uses agile techniques to maintain and improve a company's customer app. The work has no planned end date and new requests arrive continually. How should this work be classified?
o: As a project, because the team uses agile techniques to do the work
As a project, because the stream of new requests keeps changing the product
As BAU, because it is ongoing product work with no defined end
As BAU, because agile techniques are not used within projects
6.w: Work that is ongoing and repetitive, with no defined end, is BAU; agile is used in BAU as well as in projects, so using agile does not make it a project (book 1.1, 1.3.1).

n.0: Using agile does not make work a project; agile is also used in BAU (1.1).
n.1: Continual change requests to a live product are typical of ongoing BAU product work; a project is temporary (1.3.1).
n.3: Agile techniques are used in projects too; PRINCE2 Agile exists for exactly that (1.1, 3.1).

6.q: User stories are a popular way of expressing requirements in a PRINCE2 Agile project. Which three elements does the user story format capture?
o: Who needs it, when it is due and how much it will cost
What is needed, how it will be built and where it will be used
Who wants it, what they want and why they want it
Why it is needed, when it is due and who will approve it
6.w: A user story describes who wants something, what they want and why, typically written as 'As a ... I want ... so that ...' (book 8.3.2.3).

n.0: Due dates and cost are planning information held elsewhere, such as the release map and budget; the story format captures the user, the need and the reason (book 8.3.2.3).
n.1: How a feature will be built is left to the delivery team; the story format deliberately states the user's need and its value, not the design (book 8.3.2.3).
n.3: Due dates and approvers are not part of the story format; it names the user (who), the need (what) and the value (why) (book 8.3.2.3).

6.q: Which statement BEST describes agile as PRINCE2 Agile presents it?
o: A set of prescribed processes that every team follows in the same way on each project
A delivery approach based on detailed upfront planning and formal sign-off of each phase
A set of software tools that track team tasks and report progress to managers
A way of thinking and working that favours adaptation, collaboration and learning from feedback
6.w: The book presents agile as a way of thinking and working that favours adaptation, collaboration, experimentation, learning from feedback and quick pivots, to cut waste and delay and deliver user-focused solutions (book 2.3).

n.0: Agile is not a fixed set of prescribed processes; the book stresses that it is less about rigid adherence to a framework (2.3).
n.1: Detailed upfront planning with sequential sign-off describes the waterfall approach (2.2).
n.2: Tools can support agile working, but agile is a way of thinking and working, not a tool set (2.3).

6.q: How can the business case practice keep the work of an agile project focused on value?
o: By delivering every feature in one final release, so that the full benefits arrive together at closure
By assigning a value to each user story and prioritizing the work by its value against the objective
By replacing the business case with the product backlog once the first iteration has started
By measuring the velocity of each team and directing the most funding to the fastest team
6.w: PRINCE2 Agile asks that every effort contributes to meaningful outcomes; a practical way is to give each user story a value and prioritize by value against the objective (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.0: Agile delivers incrementally and plans frequent releases so benefits arrive early; holding everything for one final release works against the value focus (book 6.3.1, Table 6.1).
n.2: All projects still need business justification; the business case is tailored (for example into a project canvas), not replaced by a backlog (book 6.3.1, 6.3.2).
n.3: Velocity is a planning measure of how much a team completes; it does not express the value of the work to the business (book 8.3, 6.3.1).

6.q: In the 'prepare the outline business case' activity of starting up a project, who leads the team in developing the project canvas from the project mandate?
o: The project manager
The chief product owner
The project executive
The senior supplier
6.w: The project executive leads development of the project canvas from the mandate; the project manager, consulting the CPO, senior supplier and executive, then defines what is to be delivered and creates the project backlog (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.1).

n.0: The project manager creates the project backlog in this activity, but the executive leads the project canvas (book Table 13.1).
n.1: The CPO is consulted on what is to be delivered and owns the project backlog; the executive leads the canvas (book Table 13.1, Table 7.2).
n.3: The senior supplier is consulted when the project backlog is defined; the executive leads the canvas (book Table 13.1).

6.q: A trainer who learned PRINCE2 Agile from the 2015 guide describes the Agilometer as part of a 'focus area'. In PRINCE2 Agile Version 2, which practice includes the Agilometer among its artifacts?
o: Progress
Quality
Organization
Risk
6.w: Version 2 dropped the focus areas heading. The Agilometer is now listed with the risk management approach and risk register as an artifact of the risk practice (book 10.3.2, Table 10.1).

n.0: The progress practice uses dashboards, burn charts and OKRs; the project dashboard may show Agilometer trends, but the Agilometer itself belongs to the risk practice (book Table 12.1, Table 10.1).
n.1: The quality practice covers requirements, the Definition of Done and testing; it does not hold the Agilometer (book Table 9.1, Table 10.1).
n.2: The organization practice covers roles, team structure and the commercial management approach, not the Agilometer (book Table 7.3, Table 10.1).

6.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile combine PRINCE2 Project Management with agile ways of working?
o: Each is strong where the other is light, so together they cover direction, management and delivery
Agile teams need PRINCE2 reports in order to calculate their velocity for each new iteration
PRINCE2 needs agile in order to replace its stage boundaries with continuous release cycles
Combining them lets the project board take over product prioritization from the teams
6.w: Project management is strong on governance and control but light on product delivery, while agile is strong on delivery and responding to change but light on direction and management. PRINCE2 Agile brings them together so all three areas are covered with governance throughout (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 3.1).

n.1: Velocity comes from the team's own record of delivered work, not from PRINCE2 reports, and this is not the reason for the blend (book 8.3, 12.4.3).
n.2: Stage boundaries remain in PRINCE2 Agile: in managing a stage boundary the project manager gives the board the information it needs to review the stage and approve the next stage plan (updated release map); stages are not replaced by continuous release cycles (book 13.7.1).
n.3: Prioritizing work stays with the product owner and chief product owner; the board directs through stages and tolerances (book Table 7.2, 5.2.1.5).

6.q: A team coach tells the project manager about a minor problem with access to a test environment, which the team expects to sort out informally within a day. Where should the project manager record it?
o: Issue register
Daily log
Issue report
Exception report
6.w: The daily log records informal issues, required actions and significant events, so a minor problem being handled informally is recorded there (book Table 12.1).

n.0: The issue register is for formal issues; a minor matter handled informally belongs in the daily log (book Table 12.1; PRINCE2 7 manual chapter 10).
n.2: An issue report analyses one formal issue's impact and recommends a decision, which this minor matter does not need (book Table 11.1).
n.3: An exception report is for a forecast breach of tolerance; a minor problem expected to be fixed in a day is not that (book Table 12.1).

6.q: At the end of an iteration, only part of a user story meets the Definition of Done. What does PRINCE2 Agile suggest?
o: Report the whole story as done and finish the rest in the next iteration
Split it: the finished part is done and the rest returns to the backlog
Extend the iteration by a few days so the whole story can be finished
Raise an exception report because the story was not completed in time
6.w: A partly completed story is split: the part meeting the DoD is done, and the remainder goes back to the backlog to be reprioritized (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.3.2.2).

n.0: Work that does not meet the DoD is not done; reporting it as done hides the true position (book 9.3.2.2).
n.2: Iterations are timeboxes with fixed time; the unfinished part is returned to the backlog instead (book 9.3.2.2, Table 3.1).
n.3: One unfinished story is handled by splitting it; exceptions are for forecast breaches of tolerance (book 9.3.2.2, Table 12.1).

6.q: A delivery team at a ferry operator has agreed its own team Definition of Done. In which artifact should it be included or linked?
o: The project canvas
The risk register
The product backlog
The project dashboard
6.w: A product backlog is a regular backlog that also includes, or links to, the team Definition of Done (book 8.3.2.1).

n.0: The project canvas is the one-page business justification; it does not hold team quality criteria (book 6.3.2.1).
n.1: The risk register records risks and their status, not completion criteria (book 10.3.2).
n.3: The project dashboard shows progress for the board; the team DoD sits with the team's product backlog (book 12.3.2.1, 8.3.2.1).

6.q: A project manager notices that most news about the project spreads through informal chats and messaging groups rather than formal channels. What does PRINCE2 Agile recommend in response?
o: Restrict project information to formal reports so that messages stay consistent
Ask project assurance to monitor informal conversations between the teams
Accept it, and give people shareable formats and several feedback paths
Hold a weekly briefing to replace informal exchanges between team members
6.w: Most communication happens outside formal channels; the book advises accepting this, providing information in formats people can share, and offering multiple feedback paths (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).

n.0: Trying to restrict information to formal reports fights how people actually communicate; the book says to accept informal channels (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).
n.1: Project assurance provides independent assurance to the board; monitoring informal conversations is not its role (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, roles).
n.3: A briefing can help, but replacing informal exchanges is not the aim; the book says to work with them (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).

7.q: What happens to the business case in the 'prepare the full business case' activity of initiating a project?
o: The project manager seeks lessons on business case development and creates a more detailed project canvas
The chief product owner converts the outline project canvas into epics in the project backlog
The project board confirms that the expected benefits have been realized by the first release
The project canvas is baselined in the PID so that it is not updated again until project closure
7.w: In initiation the project manager, with the project team, draws on lessons about business case development and produces a more detailed project canvas for the board's authorization (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.6).
