n.1: The project backlog of epics is created in starting up; it does not replace the business case (book Table 13.1, 6.3.1).
n.2: Nothing has been released during initiation, so there are no realized benefits to confirm (book 6.3.1).
n.3: The canvas continues to be updated, for example at stage boundaries, so that business justification is checked throughout (book 6.3.1, 13.7.4.1).

7.q: A project includes physical products as well as software. How do the product breakdown structure (PBS) and product flow diagram (PFD) relate in planning?
o: The PFD is drawn first, and the PBS then orders the products by priority for each release
The PBS shows the order of delivery, and the PFD lists the requirements of each component
Building the PBS helps identify dependencies, which the PFD then shows as a sequence
Both are replaced by the project backlog, which holds the products and their sequence
7.w: A PBS divides each product hierarchically into components and collects their requirements; developing it helps identify dependencies, which the PFD describes as the sequence of development (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.4.1, 8.4.2).

n.0: The PBS comes first and is a hierarchy, not a priority order; the PFD follows from it (book 8.4.1, 8.4.2).
n.1: This swaps the two: the PBS holds the components and their requirements, while the PFD shows the order and dependencies (book 8.4.1, 8.4.2).
n.3: The project backlog replaces the project product description; the PBS and PFD remain plans practice techniques (book 8.3.2.1, 8.4).

7.q: A team at Brightwell Insurance holds daily stand-ups and retrospectives and uses MoSCoW prioritization, yet its managers say it looks agile but does not respond well to change. Which Agile Onion layer has the team adopted without going deeper?
o: Practices
Principles
Values
Mindset
7.w: Events such as stand-ups and techniques such as prioritization are practices, the most visible layer. Teams that stop there can look agile but lack the depth needed for long-term success (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.1).

n.1: Principles explain the why; a team that had internalized them would understand why responding to change matters (book 2.6.1).
n.2: Values shift the focus to people, collaboration and user value; they are part of what the team is missing (book 2.6.1).
n.3: The mindset of adaptability is exactly what is missing; it is the deepest layer (book 2.6.1).

7.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of the project executive in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Keeping each team's product backlog aligned with the project backlog
Monitoring adherence to the PRINCE2 Agile principles and agile practices
Removing systemic blockers to agile adoption across the organization
Approving the tolerances within which agile decision-making takes place
7.w: The project executive is accountable for the project and approves the tolerances for agile decision-making, as well as the project brief, management approaches and team structure (book Table B.1).

n.0: Keeping a team's product backlog aligned with the project backlog is the product owner's responsibility.
n.1: Monitoring adherence to principles and agile practices is the role of project assurance.
n.2: Removing organization-wide blockers to agile adoption is the agile coach's responsibility.

7.q: In validation and verification, what does validation confirm?
o: That the product has been signed off by project assurance
That the right product is being built to meet the users' needs
That the product has passed every automated unit test
That the product is being built correctly to its specification
7.w: Validation is building the right thing; verification is building the thing right (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.4.3).

n.0: Project assurance monitors governance and adherence to principles; it does not validate products for users (book Table 7.2).
n.2: Passing unit tests shows the code works as written; it does not show the right product is being built (book 9.4.3).
n.3: Building the product correctly to its specification is verification, building the thing right (book 9.4.3).

7.q: During the project initiation workshop for a new citizen-services app, the project manager introduces the Agilometer. How is it used in this workshop?
o: Everyone assesses the sliders, individually or in groups, and the views are combined into one project Agilometer
The project executive completes it before the workshop on behalf of everyone and presents it to the board
The agile coach sets each slider after the workshop and records the readings as entries in the risk register
The project manager sets each slider to match the targets in the project canvas and shares it with the team
7.w: In the project initiation workshop the Agilometer and its purpose are introduced, all participants assess it (anonymously or in groups) and the individual assessments are combined into one project Agilometer (book Table 13.7).

n.1: The initiation workshop involves all participants in the assessment; it is not a single executive's view presented for approval (book Table 13.7).
n.2: The assessment is made by all participants during the workshop and combined; the sliders are not set by one person afterwards (book Table 13.7, 10.3.2).
n.3: The sliders reflect participants' views of the environment, not targets copied from the project canvas (book Table 13.7, 10.3.2.2).

7.q: A water company has upgraded pumping stations before. The next upgrade, however, uses a new supplier, a different site and a newly formed team. Which characteristic of a project does this illustrate?
o: Temporary
Unique
Cross-functional
Change
7.w: Unique: every project differs from others in some way, for example in its team, customer, supplier, location or timeframe, even when similar work has been done before. BAU, by contrast, is repetitive and ongoing (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.1).

n.0: Temporary is about the project having a start and an end; the stem stresses how this upgrade differs from earlier ones, not its duration (book 1.3.1).
n.2: Cross-functional is about the team spanning functional divisions or organizations; the stem does not describe the mix of functions in the team (book 1.3.1).
n.3: Change is about BAU identifying a need and the project introducing it; the stem focuses on what makes this upgrade different (book 1.3.1).

7.q: A project manager plans to report each week how much of the time and cost tolerance has been used. Why is this of little value in a PRINCE2 Agile project using the default tolerances?
o: Time and cost are tracked by the delivery team, so the board does not need them
Time and cost tolerances are reviewed at stage end, so weekly reports duplicate them
Time and cost have zero tolerance, so the useful measure is what is being delivered
Time and cost are flexed by default, so their tolerances change every iteration
7.w: With zero tolerance for extra time and cost on all levels of plan, there is no tolerance to use up; progress is better shown by what is being delivered, for example in burn charts (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.3.1, Table 3.1).

n.0: The board does govern time and cost, which are fixed; the reason the report adds little is that their tolerance is zero (book Table 3.1, 12.3.1).
n.1: The issue is not duplication: with zero tolerance there is nothing to measure against, so flexing what is delivered is tracked instead (book 12.3.1).
n.3: Time and cost are fixed, not flexed, by default in PRINCE2 Agile (book Table 3.1).

7.q: Which statement describes what trading allows a delivery team to do?
o: Adapt to new priorities without increasing the overall scope of work or disrupting the current iteration
Extend the current iteration so that both the new and the existing items can still be delivered
Accept small changes from users directly, so the product owner does not need to be involved
Increase scope within the cost tolerance by bringing extra developers into the team for a while
7.w: Trading lets the team stay flexible and adapt to new priorities without increasing overall scope or disrupting the current iteration, because a lower-priority item is traded out for the new one (book 11.4.1).

n.1: Trading keeps the iteration intact by removing lower-priority work; it does not extend the timebox (book 11.4.1).
n.2: Trading relies on close communication with the product owner to agree priorities, not on bypassing the PO (book 11.4.1).
n.3: Trading keeps overall scope the same; cost has zero tolerance by default and adding people is not trading (book 11.4.1, Table 3.1).

7.q: The team for a new product has drafted nine personas. Why does PRINCE2 Agile advise against having this many?
o: Each persona above five must be approved by the project board as a baseline change to the canvas
Too many user needs shift focus from key users, make prioritizing harder and take too long to meet
Each persona needs its own product owner and delivery team, which adds to the cost of the project
Story points cannot be estimated reliably once a project has more than five personas to satisfy
7.w: Above five personas, for pilots and new products, focus moves away from key users, prioritizing requirements becomes harder and meeting all the needs takes too long for the deadlines (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: The book gives no board approval rule for personas; the concern is loss of focus, harder prioritization and time (book 6.4.1).
n.2: Personas describe users, not teams; delivery teams are organized around products and backlogs (book 6.4.1, 7.3.1).
n.3: Estimation is relative sizing of stories by the team; the persona limit is about focus and prioritization (book 8.4.3, 6.4.1).

7.q: A team coach asks how the lessons report differs from other progress products. Which statement describes the purpose of the lessons report?
o: To provide a repository for lessons that apply to this or future projects
To share lessons and trigger actions that embed them in ways of working
To review how the project performed against the PID used to authorize it
To tell the board that a stage plan is forecast to exceed its tolerance
7.w: The lessons report shares lessons and triggers actions so that they become embedded in the relevant organization's ways of working (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1).

n.0: This describes the lessons log, where lessons are recorded as they arise (book Table 12.1).
n.2: This describes the end project report, prepared when evaluating the project during closure (book Table 12.1).
n.3: This describes the exception report, used when a plan is forecast to exceed tolerance (book Table 12.1).

7.q: What level of detail does a team plan contain in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: A high-level plan of all releases in the current stage
A summary of epics for the whole of the project
A forecast of benefits for each of the planned releases
A detailed, task-level plan covering the next iteration
7.w: A team plan is a detailed task-level plan for the next iteration, produced when the team accepts a work package (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 8.1).

n.0: Releases across a stage are shown on the release map used as the stage plan (book 8.4.4).
n.1: A summary of epics for the whole project is the project backlog (book 8.3.2.1).
n.2: Benefits are forecast in the business case artifacts and the benefits management approach, not the team plan (book 6.3.2).

7.q:
Which two statements about the issue artifacts in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. The issue register holds a record of the formal issues and their status.
2. The issue report is used to forecast when a stage will exceed its tolerances.
3. The daily log can hold informal issues and required actions.
4. The issue management approach lists each issue raised so far.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
7.w: Statement 1 is true: the issue register captures and maintains formal issues and their status. Statement 3 is true: the daily log records informal issues, required actions and significant events (book Table 11.1, Table 12.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is false: a forecast breach of tolerance is reported in an exception report; an issue report analyses one issue and recommends a decision (book Table 11.1, Table 12.1).
n.2: Both statements are false: forecasting a tolerance breach is the exception report's job, and the issue management approach describes the procedure rather than listing issues (book Table 11.1, Table 12.1).
n.3: Statement 4 is false: the issue management approach describes how issues are captured, reported and controlled; the issues themselves are recorded in the issue register (book Table 11.1).

7.q: During a progress review workshop at an engineering firm, the team shows newly completed features so that users can give acceptance and feedback. Under which topic does this happen?
o: Project highlights
Current risks and issues
Welcome
Product demo
7.w: In the progress review workshop, the product demo topic shows completed features and gathers user acceptance and feedback (book 13.5.4.1, Table 13.10).

n.0: Project highlights reviews the project dashboard metrics, not a demonstration of the product (book Table 13.10).
n.1: Current risks and issues looks at open risks and issues, not at completed features (book Table 13.10).
n.2: The welcome introduces the facilitators, presenters and stakeholders at the start (book Table 13.10).

7.q: Technical debt has grown so large that the remaining Must have features can no longer be delivered within the stage tolerances. Which report should the project manager use?
o: An exception report to the project board
A lessons report to the project board
A highlight report through the project dashboard
An issue report to the change authority
7.w: Technical debt forecast to become too significant causes an exception, and a forecast breach of stage tolerance is escalated to the board in an exception report (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.4.2, Table 12.1).

n.1: A lessons report shares lessons to improve ways of working; it does not escalate a forecast breach (book Table 12.1).
n.2: The project dashboard gives regular status; a forecast breach of tolerance needs an exception report (book Table 12.1).
n.3: An issue report covers one issue's impact and options; a forecast breach of stage tolerance goes to the board as an exception (book 11.3.4, Table 12.1).

7.q: Which statement describes how the 'focus on products' principle supports working in an agile way?
o: Products are fully specified at the start so that delivery teams can build them without change
Product descriptions and quality criteria can be prioritized and decomposed so what is delivered can flex
Products are replaced by activities and tasks, which are easier to timebox in each iteration
Products are approved by the board one at a time, at each stage boundary, before the next starts
7.w: In agile, product descriptions, quality specifications and quality tolerances can be prioritized and decomposed so that what is delivered can flex, making it easier to stay in control and focus on value (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 5.1).

n.0: Agile does not fix every product detail up front; change is embraced and requirements are prioritized so that what is delivered can flex (book Table 5.1, Table 11.1).
n.2: Focus on products means delivering well-defined outputs rather than concentrating on activities, so products are not replaced by tasks (book 5.2.1.6).
n.3: The board authorizes stages, not individual products; products are delivered by teams within each stage (book 5.2.1.4).

7.q: A city museum's agile project has just started, and the team must size about 150 high-level stories for the project backlog quickly. Which estimation technique is intended for this situation?
o: Magic estimation
Card-based estimating of each story in turn
A cumulative flow diagram
Velocity from the last three iterations
7.w: Magic estimation is a quick, collaborative technique used in early planning, for example at project product level, to size many items relative to each other without lengthy discussion (book 8.4.3).

n.1: Card-based estimating discusses and estimates one story at a time, which is too slow for sizing a very large early backlog (book 8.4.3).
n.2: A cumulative flow diagram shows work items in each workflow state over time to reveal bottlenecks; it does not estimate size (book 12.4.2).
n.3: At the very start there are no completed iterations, so there is no velocity yet; velocity also forecasts delivery rather than sizing stories (book 12.4.3).

7.q: At the end of an iteration, a tester suggests a change to the way stories are handed from developers to testing so that less rework is needed next time. Under which topic of the team retrospective workshop does this suggestion belong?
o: The bad
The good
Team building
The learning
7.w: The learning gathers lessons, improvement suggestions and actionable insights for the next iteration, so a proposed process improvement belongs there (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.14).

n.0: The bad identifies the issues and their causes; turning them into a suggestion for improvement is the learning (book Table 13.14).
n.1: The good recognizes and celebrates what went well; it does not hold improvement proposals (book Table 13.14).
n.2: Team building strengthens bonds through a game or food, not through process changes (book Table 13.14).

7.q: Besides the target state, what can a change management approach describe, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The procedure for raising requests for change against the project backlog
The schedule of benefits reviews to be held after the final release
The criteria the CPO uses to prioritize the epics in the project backlog
Any interim states the business passes through on the way to the target
7.w: The change management approach can define the target organizational state and how the business will shift from the current state through any interim states (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1, Table 4.1).

n.0: Raising and handling requests for change is set out in the issue management approach, not the change management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, issues practice).
n.1: The schedule of benefits reviews belongs in the benefits management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 6.1).
n.2: How the CPO prioritizes epics is part of managing the project backlog in the plans practice, not the change management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, plans practice).

7.q: A company renames its project phases 'sprints' and holds daily stand-ups, but managers still decide every task and team members may not change how they work. Why are agile benefits unlikely to follow?
o: Daily stand-ups are too frequent for teams that work in sprints
Managers should run the stand-ups so that tasks are assigned faster
People are not allowed to think and act in an agile way
The team needs a longer planning phase before the first sprint starts
7.w: Calling processes agile means little if people are not allowed to think and act in an agile way; the benefits depend on teams being empowered to self-manage, not on new labels (book 2.3).

n.0: Frequent stand-ups are normal in agile teams; the problem is the lack of empowerment (2.3).
n.1: More direction from managers would deepen the problem; agile relies on teams self-managing (2.3).
n.3: A longer upfront planning phase is a waterfall habit and does not address the missing agile mindset (2.2, 2.3).

7.q: At which level of a PRINCE2 Agile project is a cumulative flow diagram mostly used?
o: Project board level, to approve stage and exception plans
Project level, in place of the burn-up chart on the project dashboard
Team level, to follow how tasks move through the workflow
Organization level, to compare the agile maturity of projects
7.w: The cumulative flow diagram is mostly a team-level technique that follows tasks through workflow states; it is unlikely to be used at project level (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.4.2).

n.0: The board decides on stage and exception plans using the project dashboard and release map, not a cumulative flow diagram (book Table 13.4).
n.1: At project level a burn-up chart forecasts completion; a cumulative flow diagram is unlikely to be used at that level (book 12.4.2, 12.4.3).
n.3: Comparing agile maturity uses agile maturity assessments based on the key metrics for agility, not a cumulative flow diagram (book 12.4.1).

7.q: In PRINCE2 Project Management, what should the project management team do to keep the agreed ways of working aligned with the emerging culture?
o: Fix the ways of working in the PID and treat any deviation as an exception
Ask project assurance to audit compliance at the end of every stage
Replace the team members who do not follow the agreed processes
Gather and act on feedback about how people are actually working
7.w: Feedback should be gathered and acted on so that the defined ways of working stay aligned with how people actually work, as culture keeps evolving (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2.3).

n.0: Exceptions concern forecast breaches of tolerance; freezing the ways of working ignores the evolving culture the method asks teams to respond to (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2.3).
n.1: Audits can show non-compliance, but the method's response is to understand and adapt through feedback, not to rely on stage-end checks (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2.3).
n.2: Non-compliance is treated as a sign that ways of working no longer fit the culture, not as a reason to replace people (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2.3).

7.q: A council is procuring an external agile supplier. Which management product could include a definition of the MVP and its tolerances, so that the contract supports agile delivery?
o: The quality register
The communication management approach
The commercial management approach
The risk register
7.w: The commercial management approach should support agile product development, for example with fixed teams or costs per iteration, a definition of the MVP and possible tolerances, and an agreed Definition of Done (book 7.3.2, Table 7.3).

n.0: The quality register records planned and completed quality activities and their results, not contract terms (book 9.3.2).
n.1: The communication management approach sets the means and frequency of communication and feedback with stakeholders, not procurement or contract form (book 4.4).
n.3: The risk register records identified risks and their status; it does not define what the supplier must deliver (book 10.3.2).

7.q: What does scaling up agile mean in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Raising one team's velocity so that it can deliver more user stories in each iteration
Adopting agile values and principles beyond small teams for multi-team, multi-product work
Giving each team its own separate governance so that teams can act independently
Focusing every team on short-term goals so that releases can be delivered sooner
7.w: Scaling up agile means adopting agile values and principles beyond small teams to support larger multi-team and multi-product environments (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 3.2).

n.0: Scaling is about many teams and products, not one team's output (book 3.2).
n.2: Scaling keeps sufficient governance and control; governance is not re-created for each team (book 3.2).
n.3: Short-term goals are not the focus; scaling aligns teams to shared goals (book 3.2).

7.q: Teams have adopted stand-ups and iterations but follow them by rote. Which statement about 'doing agile' and 'being agile' explains the effect on culture?
o: Doing agile changes the culture; being agile changes the processes and tools
Being agile brings a lasting cultural shift; doing agile alone may give short-term gains
Being agile applies to delivery teams; doing agile applies to the project board
Doing agile builds long-term resilience; being agile brings short-term efficiency
7.w: Being agile is thinking in an agile way and being allowed to apply that mindset; it creates cultural shift and long-term resilience, whereas doing agile on its own may give short-term efficiency without lasting impact (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1).

n.0: This reverses the two: doing agile is applying frameworks, processes and terms, and being agile is the mindset that shifts culture (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1).
n.2: Being and doing agile are not split by level of the project management team; both apply to everyone involved (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1).
n.3: This reverses the contrast: long-term resilience comes from being agile, short-term efficiency from doing agile alone (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1).

7.q: A delivery team forecasts that it cannot finish every planned feature before a fixed release date. Following the PRINCE2 Agile fix and flex defaults, what should normally happen?
o: Extend the release date so that every planned feature can be delivered
Add budget for extra developers so that all the features fit the date
Remove a Must have feature so that the Should haves can be kept
Drop or defer lower-priority Should and Could haves to keep the date
7.w: Time and cost have zero tolerance, while scope is flexed for Should and Could haves, so lower-priority features are dropped or deferred to protect the date (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1, Table 5.1).

n.0: Time has zero tolerance for extra time on all levels of plan, so extending the date breaks the default (book Table 3.1).
n.1: Cost has zero tolerance for extra cost on all levels of plan, so adding budget breaks the default (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Must haves are fixed; it is Should and Could haves that flex (book Table 3.1).

7.q: What does an agile transformation plan typically span?
o: A single iteration of one delivery team within a management stage
One management stage, after which the stage plan replaces it
Several projects or initiatives working towards enterprise-wide agility
The initiation stage of a single project, ending when the PID is approved
7.w: An agile transformation plan typically covers several projects or initiatives, as it aims at enterprise-wide adoption of agility (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.7.1).

n.0: An iteration is a short timebox for one team; a transformation plan covers organization-wide adoption (book 2.7.1).
n.1: A transformation plan is not tied to one stage; it typically spans several projects or initiatives (book 2.7.1).
n.3: The plan is broader than one project's initiation; for a single pilot it may not even be needed (book 2.7.1).

7.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile say a separate product breakdown document is not needed when a story map is used?
o: The project canvas already lists every product and its components
Building the story map already breaks the products into user stories
Products are defined later by each team when it writes its team plan
The product flow diagram already shows the full product hierarchy
7.w: During story mapping the products are broken down into smaller user stories, so a separate product breakdown structure is not needed (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.1.1).

n.0: The project canvas summarizes the business justification (vision, value, options, costs, users, scope, benefits, risks); it is not a product breakdown (book 6.3.2.1).
n.2: Team plans hold task-level detail for the next iteration; they do not define the project's products (book Table 8.1).
n.3: A product flow diagram shows development sequence and dependencies, not the product hierarchy (book 8.4.2).

7.q: Which of the following is an example of the 'responsiveness and innovation' benefit of agile?
o: A team keeps its priorities aligned with strategy during a reorganization
A team reports higher morale after being trusted to plan its own work
A team uses rapid user feedback to find a new way to solve a complex problem
A team agrees a fixed price and fixed scope with its supplier at the outset
7.w: Responsiveness and innovation come from feedback loops and continual improvement that reduce waste and produce innovative solutions to complex problems (book 2.4).

n.0: Staying aligned to organizational objectives through change is resilience and alignment (2.4).
n.1: Higher morale from self-management is the efficient teams and engaged people benefit (2.4).
n.3: A fixed price and scope is a contracting choice, not an example of an agile benefit (2.4).

7.q: Which statement describes the agile coach role in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: A mentor who helps the organization adopt agile and removes blockers across teams
A facilitator who works inside one or two teams to help them manage themselves
An independent reviewer who checks that governance controls are being followed
A team-level leader who owns a delivery team's backlog and its user stories
7.w: The agile coach mentors and facilitates the organization in adopting and sustaining agile, works across teams to remove systemic blockers and supports the board, project assurance and the PM with expert agile knowledge (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: Working closely with one or two specific teams on self-management describes the team coach, not the agile coach.
n.2: Independent checking of governance and agile practices is the role of project assurance.
n.3: Owning a delivery team's product backlog and user stories describes the product owner.

7.q: In the PRINCE2 Agile default approach to fixing and flexing the aspects of project performance, how is the benefits aspect treated?
o: It has zero tolerance on every level of plan, in the same way as time and cost
It is fixed for the Must haves and flexed for the Should haves and Could haves
It is fixed for the minimum criteria and flexed above the minimum criteria
It is fixed for minimum viability and flexed above minimum viability
7.w: Benefits are fixed at the level of minimum viability and may be flexed above that level, so the project must at least deliver a viable level of benefit (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1).

n.0: Zero tolerance at all levels of plan is the default for time and cost, not benefits (book Table 3.1).
n.1: Fixed for Must haves and flexed for Should and Could haves is the default for scope (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Fixed for minimum criteria and flexed above them is the default for sustainability; benefits use minimum viability (book Table 3.1).

7.q: Halfway through an iteration, the team's burn-down chart shows the actual line well above the ideal line. What does this indicate, and what should the team do?
o: The team is behind and should focus on the highest-priority items in the product backlog
The team is ahead and can pull extra stories forward from the next iteration
Scope has grown and the iteration should be extended so that all stories are finished
The team is behind and should send an exception report straight to the project board
7.w: On a burn-down chart, an actual line above the ideal line means less work has been completed than planned; the team will not finish everything at this rate and should concentrate on the highest-priority items in the product backlog (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.4.3).

n.1: Being ahead would put the actual line below the ideal line; above it means more work remains than planned (book 12.4.3).
n.2: Iterations are timeboxes and time has zero tolerance, so the response is to flex what is delivered, not to extend the iteration (book Table 3.1).
n.3: The reading of 'behind' is right, but a slow iteration is handled by the team reprioritizing; exception reports are prepared by the project manager when a stage or project plan is forecast to exceed tolerance (book Table 12.1).

7.q: During a progress review workshop for an airport's baggage-tracking project, the teams show newly completed features to users to gather their acceptance and feedback. Which topic of the progress review workshop is this?
o: Product demo
Project highlights
Current risks and issues
Wrap-up
7.w: The product demo topic shows completed features and gathers user acceptance and feedback (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.10).

n.1: Project highlights reviews the metrics on the project dashboard rather than demonstrating features (book Table 13.10).
n.2: Current risks and issues discusses open risks and issues and how to address them, not completed features (book Table 13.10).
n.3: Wrap-up closes the workshop by summarizing outcomes; it is not where features are demonstrated (book Table 13.10).

7.q: Which of the following is one of the four values of the Agile Manifesto?
o: Processes and tools over individuals and interactions
Comprehensive documentation over working software
Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Following a plan over customer collaboration
7.w: The first Manifesto value prefers individuals and interactions to processes and tools (Agile Manifesto, 2001; book Table 2.1).

n.0: This reverses the value: individuals and interactions are valued more than processes and tools.
n.1: This reverses the value: working software is valued more than comprehensive documentation.
n.3: This mixes two values and reverses the preference; the Manifesto values responding to change over following a plan.

7.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.
In PRINCE2 Agile, the [?] keeps the project backlog refined with input from users and aligned with the product backlogs of the delivery teams.
o: product owner of each team
project manager
chief product owner
project support
7.w: The chief product owner owns the project backlog, keeps it refined with user input and aligns it with the delivery-level product backlogs (book Table B.1).

n.0: Each team's product owner keeps their own product backlog aligned with the project backlog; the project backlog itself is the CPO's.
n.1: The project manager consults on backlogs but does not own or refine the project backlog.
n.3: Project support helps with administration and dashboards; it does not own any backlog.

7.q: In closing a project, the project manager records follow-on action recommendations for unfinished work, open issues and risks, and confirms that the product has been handed over to operations. Which activity is this?
o: Confirm project acceptance
Authorize project closure
Request project closure
Prepare planned closure
7.w: 'Confirm project acceptance' covers follow-on action recommendations for unfinished work, issues and risks, checks that the benefits management approach includes post-project confirmation and confirms handover to operations (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.18).

n.1: 'Authorize project closure' is the board's activity in directing a project, where it approves the end project report and confirms the updated project canvas; the project manager's work described here belongs to closing a project (book Table 13.4, Table 13.18).
n.2: 'Request project closure' asks the board to close, with a performance summary, readiness and concessions for off-specifications (book Table 13.18).
n.3: 'Prepare planned closure' updates the project log and release map with final actuals and drafts the closure notification (book Table 13.18).

7.q: During the project kickoff workshop for a council's waste collection app, each team maps its members' skills to find gaps and overlaps. Which kickoff topic is this?
o: Team delegation matrix
Team values and norms
Team skill matrix
Psychological safety
7.w: The team skill matrix topic maps the team's skills and shows gaps and overlaps (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.8).

n.0: The team delegation matrix simplifies decision-making and empowers self-management by making clear who decides what (book Table 13.8).
n.1: Team values and norms creates an agile culture and manages expectations for working together (book Table 13.8).
n.3: The psychological safety topic assesses how safe people feel to speak up and take part; it does not map skills (book Table 13.8).

7.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. PRINCE2 Agile explains that agile is less about rigid adherence to a [?] and more about collaboration, creativity and adaptability.
o: framework
mindset
user need
timebox
7.w: The book says agile is less about rigidly sticking to a framework and more about collaboration, creativity and adaptability (book 2.3).

n.1: The agile mindset is what the book wants teams to adopt, so it is not what agile is 'less about'.
n.2: Agile is user-focused; the book does not say it is less about meeting user needs.
n.3: Timeboxes are an agile technique, but the sentence in the book contrasts collaboration and adaptability with rigid use of a framework.

7.q: In which workshop topic is MoSCoW used to review and prioritize requirements before an iteration?
o: Effort estimation in the team planning workshop
Team values and norms in the project kickoff workshop
Product backlog refinement in the team planning workshop
Project highlights in the progress review workshop
7.w: The product backlog refinement topic of the team planning workshop reviews and prioritizes requirements using MoSCoW (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.13).

n.0: Effort estimation builds a shared view of the complexity and effort of each story; prioritizing with MoSCoW is backlog refinement (book Table 13.13).
n.1: Team values and norms shape the agile culture and expectations of the team, not the order of requirements (book Table 13.8).
n.3: Project highlights reviews the metrics on the project dashboard; it does not prioritize the backlog (book Table 13.10).

7.q: How do the values in the Agile Onion change a team's focus?
o: From user value towards detailed documentation and fixed plans
From rigid processes towards people, collaboration and user value
From team self-management towards central control of decisions
From short iterations towards a single long delivery phase
7.w: Values, defined by the Agile Manifesto, shift attention from rigid processes to people, collaboration and user value (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.1).

n.0: This reverses the shift; values move focus away from rigid processes towards people and user value (book 2.6.1).
n.2: The agile mindset favours empowerment and self-management, not central control (book 2.6.1, 2.6.2).
n.3: A single long delivery phase describes waterfall, which the values do not promote (book 2.2).

8.q: During initiation of an agile project at an insurance broker, the project manager drafts the artifact that sets out how risk will be managed on the project, including the procedures, techniques and responsibilities to be used. Which artifact is this?
o: Risk register
Agilometer
Issue management approach
Risk management approach
8.w: The risk management approach describes how risk will be managed on the project. It holds the procedure, techniques and responsibilities, not the individual risks (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 10.1; PRINCE2 7 manual chapter 9).

n.0: The risk register records the identified risks with their status and history; it does not describe how risk will be managed (book Table 10.1).
n.1: The Agilometer identifies and monitors the risks of agile working through its sliders; it does not set out the risk procedures and responsibilities (book 10.3.1).
n.2: The issue management approach describes how issues are captured and how baseline changes are controlled, not how risk is managed (book Table 11.1).

8.q: Which feature of agile working does PRINCE2 Agile link MOST directly to the benefit of responsiveness and innovation?
o: Feedback loops and continual improvement
Detailed upfront requirements and sign-off
A fixed scope agreed in the contract
Formal written reports at fixed intervals
8.w: Feedback loops and continual improvement reduce waste and lead to innovative solutions to complex problems (book 2.4).

n.1: Detailed upfront requirements reduce the room to respond to feedback, the opposite of this benefit (2.2, 2.4).
n.2: Fixed contractual scope limits responsiveness; it is not linked to this benefit (2.4).
n.3: Formal reports do not create the feedback loops the book links to innovation (2.4).

8.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of agile as PRINCE2 Agile describes it?
o: Learning from feedback and adapting the work in response
Collaborating closely to create user-focused solutions
Fixing the full solution in detail before any work begins
Being ready to pivot quickly when circumstances change
8.w: Agile favours adaptation, experimentation, feedback and quick pivots. Fixing the whole solution in detail upfront is the linear-sequential (waterfall) way, whose main limitation is a lack of adaptability (book 2.2, 2.3).

n.0: Learning from feedback and adapting is a core feature of agile (2.3).
n.1: Collaboration and user-focused solutions are central to agile (2.3).
n.3: Quick pivots are named among the things agile favours (2.3).

8.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile apply the 'define roles, responsibilities and relationships' principle?
o: Agile roles are added where needed and PRINCE2 roles are tailored carefully to the agile context
PRINCE2 roles are replaced by Scrum roles, so a project board is not needed in agile projects
Roles are left undefined so that self-managing teams can decide among themselves who does what
The project manager takes over the chief product owner's duty of making sure user needs are met
8.w: In agile, additional agile roles may be needed and PRINCE2 Project Management roles should be tailored carefully to the agile context; PRINCE2 Agile V2 has 11 roles, including the chief product owner, product owner, team coach and agile coach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 5.1, Table 7.2).

n.1: PRINCE2 Agile keeps governance roles such as the project executive and project board; it adds agile roles rather than replacing the PRINCE2 roles (book Table 5.1, 7.3.1).
n.2: The principle requires defined and agreed roles; self-management happens within clear roles and boundaries, not in place of them (book 5.2.1.3).
n.3: It is the chief product owner, not the project manager, who makes sure user requirements are met (book 5.2.1.3, Table B.1).

8.q: How is MoSCoW used in the project canvas workshop?
o: To prioritize the scope, set out as epic user stories, under scope definition
To rank each team member's skills when building the team skill matrix
To prioritize the key user groups, ranked first to third, under user group definition
To prioritize the Agilometer sliders that need the most improvement
8.w: In the project canvas workshop, the scope definition topic defines the scope in epic user stories and prioritizes them with MoSCoW, then checks timeline and scope tolerances (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.2).

n.1: The team skill matrix maps skills, gaps and overlaps in the project kickoff workshop (book Table 13.8).
n.2: User group definition ranks one to three key user groups first to third; it does not use MoSCoW (book Table 13.2).
n.3: The Agilometer is assessed in the project initiation workshop and is a risk tool; it is not ranked with MoSCoW (book 10.3.2, Table 13.7).

8.q: What does A/B testing involve in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Writing a unit test for each piece of code before the code itself is written
Comparing two versions of a feature with users and analysing how they respond
Splitting the testing of each story between a developer and a tester
Checking a product against its acceptance criteria before and after refactoring
8.w: A/B testing compares two versions of a product, design or feature with users and analyses their responses to guide decisions (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.4.3).

n.0: Writing tests first at unit level is test-driven development (Glossary).
n.2: Sharing testing between roles is a team arrangement, not A/B testing (book Table 7.2, 9.4.3).
n.3: Refactoring keeps behaviour unchanged, and checking against acceptance criteria is a quality check on one version; A/B testing compares two versions with users (book 9.4.1, 9.4.3).

8.q: In a PRINCE2 Agile project, the project manager is preparing the product backlogs and the management approaches. Who should the project manager consult?
o: The agile coach, who approves the management approaches
Project support, who owns the team product backlogs
The product owners and the relevant stakeholders
The developers, who set the priorities for each team
8.w: The project manager consults the product owners and stakeholders when preparing product backlogs and management approaches (book Table B.1).

n.0: The agile coach advises on agile ways of working, but the management approaches are approved by the project executive.
n.1: Product backlogs are owned by the product owners; project support provides administrative help.
n.3: Developers build the increments; priorities come from the product owner within the team and the CPO across teams.

8.q: At the end of initiation, a project manager shares the final project canvas, the PID and the release map with the project board. Which initiating activity is this, and which board activity normally follows?
o: Request project authorization, followed by 'authorize the project'
Prepare the project plan, followed by 'authorize a stage or exception plan'
Request project authorization, followed by 'authorize initiation'
Establish project controls, followed by 'give ongoing direction'
8.w: In 'request project authorization' the project manager shares the final project canvas, PID and release map with the board; the board then approves the PID, confirms tolerances and commits resources in 'authorize the project' (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.6, Table 13.4).

n.1: 'Prepare the project plan' documents the release map and plans transition to operations; it is not the request to the board, and the board's next step is not a stage authorization (book Table 13.6, Table 13.4).
n.2: The activity is right but 'authorize initiation' happened earlier, when the board approved the project brief and the release map for initiation (book Table 13.4).
n.3: 'Establish project controls' sets stage boundaries, tolerances and escalation procedures; the board's response to the PID is 'authorize the project' (book Table 13.6, Table 13.4).

8.q: Teams at Kestrel Freight follow every event of a new agile framework, yet they resist changing plans when user feedback arrives. Which explanation fits PRINCE2 Agile guidance on the agile mindset?
o: The teams lack the formal processes that tell them when to deliver value to their users
The teams need more framework events, since adaptability grows with each review
The teams have adopted visible practices without a mindset of adaptability and learning
The teams have no approved agile transformation plan from the project board
8.w: Practices are the most visible layer and teams that stop there can look agile without the mindset that fosters adaptability and continual learning (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.1).

n.0: The teams already follow the framework's events and processes; the gap is the mindset, as processes alone do not guarantee agility (book 2.6.1).
n.1: Adding events adds practices; adaptability comes from the mindset, the innermost layer (book 2.6.1).
n.3: An agile transformation plan guides enterprise adoption (book 2.7.1); it does not explain why teams resist adapting to feedback.

8.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, how is the 'manage by exception' principle applied when working in an agile way?
o: Tolerance is allowed on time and cost, while what is delivered is held fixed
Tolerances are replaced by each team's Definition of Done for the iteration
Tolerance is set on team velocity, so teams escalate when story points fall
Tolerance is allowed on what is delivered and restricted on time and cost
8.w: Working in an agile way emphasizes allowing tolerance on what is delivered and restricting tolerance on time and cost (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 5.1; Table 3.1).

n.0: This reverses the agile position: time and cost have zero tolerance by default, while what is delivered is flexed (book Table 3.1, Table 5.1).
n.1: The Definition of Done is a quality artifact setting when an item is complete; it does not replace tolerances set by the board (book 9.3.2.2).
n.2: Velocity is used to forecast empirically; tolerances are set against the seven performance aspects, not against velocity (book 12.4.3, 5.2.1.5).

8.q: In the 'evaluate the project' activity of closing a project, which products does the project manager prepare?
o: The exception report and the issue report
The end stage report and the checkpoint report
The project canvas and the project backlog
The end project report and the lessons report
8.w: Evaluating the project compares it with the original PID and approved changes, and produces the end project report and the lessons report (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.18).

n.0: These products handle forecast tolerance breaches and individual issues during the project, not the evaluation at closure (book Table 12.1, 11.3.4).
n.1: In PRINCE2 Agile these are replaced by the project dashboard and the team dashboard and serve stage and team reporting, not closure (book Table 12.1).
n.2: The project canvas and project backlog are created in starting up; at closure the board confirms the updated project canvas rather than the project manager creating these products (book Table 13.1, Table 13.4).

8.q: A housing association's agile project will deliver an online repairs portal for tenants. Which of these is a benefit, as PRINCE2 Agile defines the term?
o: The online repairs portal released to tenants at the end of stage 2
The release map showing three releases across the first two stages
The project canvas approved by the project executive at the start
A 20% fall in repair calls to the contact centre within one year
8.w: A benefit is a measurable improvement, resulting from an outcome, that the investing organization sees as an advantage and that contributes to its objectives. A measured fall in repair calls fits this (book Glossary).

n.0: The portal is an output, a specialist product the project delivers; an output is not a benefit (book Glossary).
n.1: The release map is a plan, a management artifact; it is not a measurable improvement for the organization (book 8.3.2.5).
n.2: The project canvas is the agile form of the business case that records expected benefits; the approved document is not itself a benefit (book 6.3.2.1).

8.q:
Which two statements about being agile and doing agile are correct?

1. Being agile includes being allowed to apply an agile mindset within suitable levels of self-management.
2. Doing agile covers the use of agile frameworks, techniques and terminology.
3. Adopting an agile framework is enough to bring faster delivery and higher quality.
4. Being agile concerns short-term mechanics, while doing agile creates long-term cultural change.
o: 1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
1 and 2
8.w: Statement 1 is the definition of being agile and statement 2 the definition of doing agile (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3.1). Statement 3 is the misconception the book warns against (book 2.3), and statement 4 reverses the long-term versus short-term contrast.

n.0: Statement 1 is correct, but statement 3 is the classic misconception: a framework does not by itself bring faster delivery or higher quality; the value lies in shifting mindsets and culture (book 2.3).
n.1: Statement 2 is correct, but statement 4 reverses the contrast: being agile brings long-term cultural change and doing agile alone short-term mechanics (book 2.3.1).
n.2: Both are wrong: statement 3 is the framework misconception (book 2.3) and statement 4 reverses the long-term versus short-term contrast (book 2.3.1).

8.q: An organization has years of lessons logs that nobody reads. It uses AI to categorize and prioritize the lessons, make them searchable by role and project stage, and highlight recurring issues and proven solutions. Which principle does this use of AI support?
o: Manage by exception
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Learn from experience
Manage by stages
8.w: AI strengthens learning from experience by turning large volumes of lessons into accessible, prioritized insights tailored to roles or stages, highlighting recurring issues and proven solutions (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.1).

n.0: Manage by exception is about delegating authority through tolerances; the AI use described here works on past lessons (book 5.2.1.5, 15.4.1).
n.1: AI supports defined roles by analysing skills and workload to suggest role assignments, not by organizing lessons (book 15.4.1).
n.3: AI supports manage by stages by adjusting predictions and refining the next stage or iteration plan (book 15.4.1).

8.q: In the scope definition topic of the project canvas workshop, how is the project's scope typically expressed?
o: As detailed tasks estimated in hours for each developer
As user stories for the first iteration, ready for the team plan
As epics prioritized using MoSCoW, with a timeline and tolerance
As product register entries for each specialist product
8.w: Scope definition in the project canvas workshop sets a timeline and tolerance and expresses scope as epics prioritized with MoSCoW (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.2).

n.0: Task-level planning is done only for the next iteration in managing product delivery, not in starting up (book Table 8.1, Table 13.12).
n.1: Detailed user stories for an iteration are prepared in team planning during managing product delivery (book 13.6.4.1).
n.3: The product register records products and their status during the project; scope on the canvas is high-level epics (book Table 9.1, Table 13.2).

8.q: In a PRINCE2 Agile project, what does the project brief outline that reflects the agile way of working?
o: The detailed task-level team plan for each iteration in the first stage
The signed-off list of user stories for the whole of the project
The flexible areas of scope and quality criteria, based on prioritization
The velocity that each delivery team is required to achieve per iteration
8.w: In PRINCE2 Agile the project brief outlines which areas of scope and quality criteria are flexible, based on prioritization, and describes the agile techniques and approaches chosen with their expected benefits (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 6.1).

n.0: Team plans are produced by the delivery team for the next iteration during managing product delivery, not in the project brief (book Table 8.1).
n.1: Agile expects requirements to evolve; a fixed, signed-off list of all stories contradicts the flexible scope the brief describes (book Table 6.1).
n.3: Velocity is measured from the team's actual work and used to forecast; it is not imposed through the brief (book 8.3).

8.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
A change that leaves the project backlog untouched is a detail change and is dealt with informally at [?] level, whereas a change to the project backlog is decided formally.
o: board
executive
stage
team
8.w: Issues that do not affect the agreed baseline are handled informally at team level; issues that do affect it are handled and decided formally at the appropriate management level (book 11.3.2).

n.0: The board, or a delegated change authority, decides baseline changes; detail changes do not need to reach it (book 11.3.2).
n.1: The project executive is part of the board and is involved in formal decisions, not in informal detail changes (book 11.3.2, Table 7.2).
n.2: Stage-level planning is shown in the release map; detail changes are dealt with by the team and product owner within the iterations (book 11.3.2, 8.3.2.5).

8.q:
Which two statements about organizational change management (OCM) in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. OCM is the means of moving an organization from its current state to a target state.
2. OCM is a technique used to control changes to the project backlog.
3. The change management approach can describe how the business moves through interim states.
4. The change management approach is replaced by the release map in agile projects.
o: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
8.w: OCM is the move from current to target state (statement 1), and the change management approach can describe the shift through any interim states (statement 3) (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1, Table 4.1).

n.1: Statement 2 is wrong: controlling changes to the project backlog is change control in the issues practice, not OCM (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 11.3).
n.2: Statements 2 and 4 are both wrong: OCM is not backlog change control, and the release map replaces project and stage plans, not the change management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1).
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: if anything replaces the change management approach it is the agile transformation plan, not the release map (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).

8.q: Which role approves the management approaches, such as the quality management approach, in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Project assurance
The chief product owner
The project executive
The project manager
8.w: The project executive is accountable for the project and approves the project brief, the management approaches and the team structure (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 7.2).

n.0: Project assurance monitors adherence and advises the board and project manager; it does not approve the approaches (book Table 7.2).
n.1: The CPO represents the users and owns the project backlog; approving the management approaches is the executive's responsibility (book Table 7.2).
n.3: The project manager prepares the approaches with product owners and stakeholders, but approval sits with the executive (book Table 7.2, Table 13.6).

8.q: Which statement about the organizational context of a project is correct?
o: It describes whether the project stands alone or forms part of a programme or portfolio
It describes whether the project's suppliers sit inside or outside the sponsoring organization
It describes how formal governance and documentation need to be for the project's size
It describes whether products are built in sequence or through repeated iterations
8.w: The organizational context recognizes that a project may be part of a programme or portfolio, or may be a standalone project introducing a single change into the operational environment (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.4).

n.1: Whether suppliers are external to the sponsoring organization is the commercial context, not the organizational context (book 1.3.4).
n.2: How formal governance and documentation need to be is driven by the scale context (book 1.3.4).
n.3: Whether products are built sequentially or iteratively is the delivery method context (book 1.3.4).

8.q: What does PRINCE2 Agile say about the processes layer of the Agile Onion?
o: Processes are the core of agility, so changing them is the surest way to create lasting change
Processes are defined by the Agile Manifesto values and form the foundation of all other layers
Processes are the specific techniques and events that teams use, such as prioritization
Processes give structure, such as when to deliver value, but do not guarantee agility by themselves
8.w: The formal processes of agile frameworks give structure, guiding when to deliver value and how to manage work, but must be supported by principles and values to allow change and innovation (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.1).

n.0: The core of the onion is the mindset; processes alone do not guarantee agility (book 2.6.1).
n.1: The layer defined by the Manifesto that encompasses all else is values (book 2.6.1).
n.2: Techniques and events such as prioritization and workshops are practices (book 2.6.1).

8.q: At which level of a PRINCE2 Agile project are burn charts a suitable way of showing progress, and why?
o: At every level, because what is delivered is the main aspect that flexes
At team level, because the board tracks spend against budget instead
At project level, because teams report progress in checkpoint reports
At stage level, because time tolerance is the main measure of progress
8.w: Flexibility in what is delivered is the aspect of performance of most interest to the whole project management team, so showing it in a burn chart suits every level of the project (book 12.3.1).

n.1: Cost has zero tolerance on all levels of plan in PRINCE2 Agile, so tracking spend against budget adds little; the board also benefits from burn charts (book 12.3.1, Table 3.1).
n.2: Checkpoint reports are replaced by team dashboards, and burn charts are used at team level as well as project level (book Table 12.1, 12.3.1).
n.3: Time also has zero tolerance on all levels of plan, so time tolerance is not the progress measure; scope delivered is (book 12.3.1, Table 3.1).

8.q: What distinguishes iterative-incremental delivery from linear-sequential delivery?
o: The whole product is designed in full before any part of it is built, tested or released to users
The product is delivered in one handover once every requirement is complete
The product is built in repeated cycles, with usable parts delivered and reviewed along the way
The scope is fixed and the timeboxes are extended until all of it is complete
8.w: Iterative-incremental delivery builds the product in repeated timeboxed cycles, so parts are delivered early and feedback shapes what follows; linear-sequential delivery completes each phase before the next (book 1.3.4, 2.2).

n.0: Designing everything before building is the linear-sequential (waterfall) pattern (2.2).
n.1: A single final handover is typical of linear-sequential delivery, not iterative-incremental (2.2).
n.3: In agile delivery time is fixed and lower-priority scope flexes, not the reverse (Table 3.1).

8.q: A PRINCE2 Agile project has teams in two cities. The project manager wants to document how the remote teams will work together, including the tools they will use for transparency and rich communication. In which product should this be described?
o: Role descriptions
Project management team structure
Commercial management approach
Team delegation matrix
8.w: The project management team structure sets out who is involved, how they relate and how they work together, including arrangements for co-located or remote teams and the tools used for transparency and rich communication (book 7.3.2, Table 7.3).

n.0: Role descriptions set out each role's specific responsibilities, not team working arrangements across locations.
n.2: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracts, not how remote teams collaborate.
n.3: A delegation matrix shows who decides and who is involved per decision area; working arrangements and tools for remote teams belong in the team structure.

8.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes organizational change management (OCM) from change control in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: OCM is handled by the issues practice; change control by the change management approach
OCM moves the organization to a target state; change control manages changes to baselines
OCM covers user groups outside the project; change control covers supplier contracts
OCM is used in traditional projects; change control is used in agile projects
8.w: OCM is about the organization's transition from current to target state, supported by the change management approach; change control handles changes to approved baselines through the issues practice (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1, 11.3).

n.0: This reverses the two: change control sits in the issues practice, while the change management approach supports OCM (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1).
n.2: OCM covers everyone affected by the change, and change control covers changes to baselines, not supplier contracts (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1, 4.2.2).
n.3: Both apply in agile projects; PRINCE2 Agile uses OCM for people's transition and the issues practice for controlling baseline changes (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1).

8.q: A rail infrastructure project uses delivery teams from two companies and several external advisers. According to PRINCE2 Agile, what helps people work effectively across these organizational and cultural boundaries?
o: Placing every external adviser under the direct authority of the product owner
Setting clear boundaries within which people are free to flex
Asking each company to keep following its own decision-making rules
Holding all decisions at project board level until trust has been built
8.w: When working across organizations and cultures, PRINCE2 Agile recommends clear boundaries within which people can flex, for example a delegation matrix showing what advisers decide or advise on (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.1).

n.0: The product owner has direct authority over delivery team members; the guidance for advisers is to clarify what they decide or advise on, not to place them under the PO (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.1, 7.3.1).
n.2: Separate decision-making rules in each company leave people unclear about who decides what; the book asks for shared, clear boundaries (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.1).
n.3: Holding decisions at board level runs against local decision-making and the freedom to flex within agreed boundaries (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.1).

8.q: PRINCE2 Agile attaches named workshops to each of its processes. How does it describe a workshop?
o: An informal daily meeting where each member reports progress
A training course run by the agile coach for the project board
A facilitated session with a set purpose, agenda and outputs
A formal meeting at which the board authorizes the next stage
8.w: A workshop is a facilitated, collaborative session with a defined purpose, participants, agenda topics and outputs; PRINCE2 Agile V2 names workshops for every process (book 5.6.3.1).

n.0: A short daily progress meeting is the daily stand-up, which the project manager may attend only with the team's agreement; it is not a workshop with a set agenda and outputs (book Table 12.1, 5.6.3.1).
n.1: Training and coaching raise agile maturity, but a workshop is a working session with its own agenda and outputs, not a course (book 2.7.3, 5.6.3.1).
n.3: Authorizing a stage is a board decision in directing a project; it does not describe what a workshop is (book 5.6.3.1).

8.q: A delivery team at an energy supplier is working on its part of a customer portal project. Which two named workshops support the 'managing product delivery' process in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The progress review workshop and the project retrospective workshop
The release planning workshop and the agile enablement workshop
The team planning workshop and the team retrospective workshop
The project initiation workshop and the project kickoff workshop
8.w: Managing product delivery is supported by the team planning workshop, which prepares the next iteration, and the team retrospective workshop, which reflects on the last one (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.6.4.1, 13.6.4.2).

n.0: The progress review and project retrospective workshops support controlling a stage (book 13.5.4.1, Table 13.11).
n.1: The release planning workshop supports managing a stage boundary and the agile enablement workshop supports directing a project (book 13.7.4.1, 13.3.3).
n.3: The project initiation and project kickoff workshops support initiating a project (book 13.4.4.1, 13.4.4.2).

8.q: In a PRINCE2 Agile project with two delivery teams, between which two roles is each team's work package description agreed?
o: The project executive and the project manager
The chief product owner and the product owner
The project manager and the product owner
The team coach and the developers
8.w: The project manager and the product owner agree work as work package descriptions expressed as sets of user stories, within the tolerances and management approaches (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.3.1).

n.0: The executive and project manager agree stage-level matters such as tolerances, not team work packages (book Table 7.2).
n.1: The CPO works closely with product owners on priorities, but work packages are agreed with the project manager (book 7.3.1).
n.3: The team coach helps the team self-manage; work packages are agreed between the PM and PO (book Table 7.2, 7.3.1).

8.q: Why are personas useful when developing the business case for a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: They give a clear overview of each team member's skills, strengths and gaps so training can be planned
They help identify and articulate the specific benefits the project can deliver to its users and stakeholders
They set out how much authority the board delegates to the teams for each type of key decision
They track the total level of risk exposure across iterations so that trends can be monitored
8.w: Personas help a project identify and articulate the specific benefits it can deliver to users, customers and stakeholders, which is why they sit in the business case practice (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.0: An overview of team skills, strengths and gaps is the team skill matrix in the organization practice (book 7.4.1).
n.2: Agreeing levels of delegated authority for decisions is done with delegation poker and the delegation matrix (book 7.4.3).
n.3: Tracking total risk exposure across iterations is the cumulative risk burn-down chart in the risk practice (book 10.4.2).

8.q: Which list correctly names benefits of agile described in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Resilience and alignment; fixed scope and budget; responsiveness and innovation
Predictability and control; efficient, engaged teams; responsiveness and innovation
Resilience and alignment; efficient, engaged teams; responsiveness and innovation
Resilience and alignment; efficient, engaged teams; a reduced need for governance
8.w: The book describes organizational resilience and alignment, more efficient teams and engaged people, and responsiveness and innovation among the benefits of agile (book 2.4).

n.0: Fixed scope is not an agile benefit; scope below the Must haves flexes in PRINCE2 Agile (2.4, Table 3.1).
n.1: Predictability and control are not named agile benefits; resilience and alignment is (2.4).
n.3: Agile does not reduce the need for governance; PRINCE2 Agile keeps governance and control throughout (3.1).

8.q: A project manager forecasts that the current stage plan will exceed its tolerances. Which product informs the project board of this, setting out options and a recommendation?
o: Issue report
Project dashboard
Lessons report
Exception report
8.w: The exception report tells the project board when a stage plan or project plan is forecast to exceed tolerance and offers options and recommendations for how to proceed (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1).

n.0: An issue report describes one issue's impact on the baseline with options for resolving it; a forecast tolerance breach on a plan calls for an exception report (book 11.3.4, Table 12.1).
n.1: The project dashboard gives the board regular status in place of the highlight report; it is not the product for escalating a forecast breach (book Table 12.1).
n.2: The lessons report shares lessons and triggers actions to embed them; it does not escalate a forecast breach (book Table 12.1).

8.q: Which estimating technique gives a quick, collaborative way to size the relative size or complexity of many items in early planning, such as at project product level, without lengthy discussion?
o: Delegation poker
Magic estimation
Product flow diagram
MoSCoW prioritization
8.w: Magic estimation is a quick, collaborative technique used in early planning, for example at project product level, to estimate the relative size or complexity of many pieces of work without lengthy discussion (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.4.3).

n.0: Delegation poker is an organization practice technique for agreeing decision-making levels, not for sizing work (book 7.4.2).
n.2: A product flow diagram shows the sequence and dependencies of products; it does not estimate size (book 8.4.2).
n.3: MoSCoW sets priority (Must, Should, Could, Won't), for example in product backlog refinement, not relative size or complexity (book Table 13.13).

8.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile differ from PRINCE2 Project Management in relation to the delivery method context?
o: PRINCE2 Agile can host any delivery method, while PRINCE2 Project Management is designed for linear delivery
Both are designed for linear-sequential delivery, with agile techniques added during the delivery stages
PRINCE2 Agile is designed for hybrid delivery, mixing linear and iterative work within each delivery stage
PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative-incremental delivery; PRINCE2 Project Management can host any method
8.w: PRINCE2 Project Management is configured so a project can use any chosen delivery method, whereas PRINCE2 Agile is specifically designed for projects using iterative and incremental (agile) delivery (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.4).

n.0: This reverses the position: it is PRINCE2 Project Management that can host any delivery method, while PRINCE2 Agile is designed for iterative-incremental delivery (book 1.3.4).
n.1: PRINCE2 Agile is specifically designed for iterative and incremental delivery, not for linear-sequential delivery with agile add-ons (book 1.3.4).
n.2: PRINCE2 Agile is described as designed for iterative and incremental (agile) delivery, not as a hybrid method (book 1.3.4).

8.q: A project manager is setting up the agile enablement workshop for a university's student records project. Which group of participants is this workshop intended for?
o: The delivery team, its product owner and its team coach for the coming iteration
The project board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives
The project manager, project support and the developers working in each team
The chief product owner, the developers and the users who will accept the product
8.w: The agile enablement workshop is a special workshop for the project board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives, held to review agile maturity and agile risks (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.3.3, Table 13.5).

n.0: A delivery team with its product owner and team coach describes the team planning or team retrospective workshops in managing product delivery (book 13.6.4).
n.2: The project manager, project support and developers are not the audience the book gives; the enablement workshop centres on the board with agile coaches and business representatives (book 13.3.3).
n.3: The CPO, developers and accepting users fit a product demo; the enablement workshop is a board-level session on agile maturity and risk (book 13.3.3).

8.q:
Which two statements about tolerances and exceptions in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?

1. Scope is fixed for Must-have features and flexed for Should-have and Could-have features.
2. An exception may be triggered by an updated burn chart at iteration or release level.
3. Benefits may fall below minimum viability so that the release date can be kept.
4. An exception arises each time a team's velocity falls below its average.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
8.w: Scope is fixed for Must-haves and flexed for lower priorities (statement 1), and an updated burn chart at iteration or release level can reveal a forecast breach and trigger an exception (statement 2) (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1, Table 12.1).

n.1: Statement 3 is wrong: benefits are fixed at minimum viability and flexed above it (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Statement 4 is wrong: a dip in velocity is ordinary variation; an exception needs a forecast breach of tolerance (book Table 12.1).
n.3: Both are wrong: benefits are fixed at minimum viability, and a dip in velocity is not in itself an exception (book Table 3.1, Table 12.1).

8.q: Which of the following is NOT a use of the team skill matrix in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Identifying the training needs of team members
Spotting skill gaps and overlaps in the team
Recording which person decides each decision area
Helping to assign the right people to the tasks
8.w: Recording who decides in each decision area is the purpose of the delegation matrix (book 7.4.3). The other three are uses of the team skill matrix (book 7.4.1).

n.0: Identifying training needs is a stated use of the team skill matrix.
n.1: Mapping skills to spot gaps and overlaps is what the team does with the matrix in the kickoff workshop.
n.3: Helping to assign the right people to tasks is a stated use of the team skill matrix.

8.q: Which statement correctly describes how the release map is used across the PRINCE2 Agile processes?
o: It is first created in closing a project, when the end project report compares planned and actual releases
It is produced by each delivery team in accept a work package as the plan for the next iteration
The board approves a release map for initiation, and the PM documents the project release map in initiation
It is owned by the chief product owner and replaces the project product description for the board
8.w: Starting up produces a high-level release map for initiation, which the board approves when authorizing initiation; in initiating a project the project manager documents the release map while preparing the project plan (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Tables 13.1, 13.4, 13.6).

n.0: The release map exists from starting up onwards; closing a project does not create it (book Tables 13.1, 13.6).
n.1: Accepting a work package produces a team plan, not the release map (book Table 13.12).
n.3: The CPO owns the project backlog, which is what replaces the project product description (book 8.3.2.1, Table 7.2).

8.q: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate use of trading in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Absorbing a new requirement by removing a lower-priority item of similar effort
Keeping the workload of an iteration balanced when the priorities change
Resolving a technical blocker that has stopped progress on a story
Responding to a detail change that is more valuable than an existing story
8.w: Trading handles emerging change by swapping items of similar effort; it is not a way of resolving blockers. Blockers are tackled by swarming and escalated if the team cannot resolve them (book 11.4.1, 11.4.2).

n.0: This is an appropriate use: trading replaces a lower-priority item with the new requirement of similar effort (book 11.4.1).
n.1: This is an appropriate use: trading keeps the workload balanced instead of adding tasks on top (book 11.4.1).
n.3: This is an appropriate use: detail changes should be prioritized and traded if more valuable than existing work (book 11.3.2, 11.4.1).

8.q: Which key characteristic of the agile mindset involves working closely with team members, stakeholders and users, with shared ownership and co-creation of solutions?
o: Collaboration
Respect
Empowerment
Transparency and rich communication
8.w: Collaboration means working closely with the team, stakeholders and users in a culture of shared ownership, mutual support and co-created solutions (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.2).

n.1: Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness, valuing all voices (book 2.6.2).
n.2: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management (book 2.6.2).
n.3: Transparency concerns open, rich information flow rather than co-creation (book 2.6.2).

9.q: A project manager agrees 'a set of user stories' with a product owner before the team starts an iteration. Which PRINCE2 management product does this set of user stories represent?
o: Product description
Work package description
Team plan
Project product description
9.w: In PRINCE2 Agile the work package description is expressed as a set of user stories agreed between the project manager and the product owner (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 8.1, 7.3.1).

n.0: Product descriptions are tailored into the team product backlog, which the product owner owns; the agreed set of stories is the work package (book 8.3.2.1, Table 8.1).
n.2: The team plan is the delivery team's detailed task plan for the iteration, produced when it accepts the work package (book Table 8.1).
n.3: The project product description describes the overall project product and is tailored into the project backlog, which the CPO owns; it is not the agreed work for one team (book 8.3.2.1).

9.q: PRINCE2 Agile Version 2 builds on PRINCE2 Project Management. Which list gives the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 Project Management?
o: Principles, themes, processes, roles and tailoring
Principles, practices, processes, products and tolerances
Principles, people, practices, processes and performance targets
Principles, people, practices, processes and the project context
