11.w: Product-based planning keeps its product focus in PRINCE2 Agile (statement 1), and the budget step covers product costs (people, equipment, materials, facilities) plus project management costs (statement 2) (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.1, 8.3.1.5).

n.0: Statement 3 is wrong: the task-level plan for the next iteration is the team plan, not the story map (book Table 8.1).
n.1: Statement 4 is wrong: the story map is recommended to replace the product breakdown structure, not feed it (book 8.3.1.1).
n.2: Both are wrong: the story map is neither the team plan nor an input to a PBS it is meant to replace (book Table 8.1, 8.3.1.1).

11.q: Why does unpaid technical debt matter to a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: It requires a fresh Agilometer assessment at every stage boundary
It reduces the minimum viable benefits figure recorded in the project canvas
It increases the number of Won't have items recorded in the backlog
It raises disorder and lowers quality, so later changes become harder and costlier
11.w: Unpaid technical debt accumulates interest: it increases disorder, lowers quality and makes later change harder (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.4.2).

n.0: The Agilometer assesses the risks of agile working; it is not triggered by technical debt (book 10.3.2, 9.4.2).
n.1: Technical debt affects the quality and changeability of products; it does not alter the benefits figures in the canvas (book 9.4.2, 6.3.2).
n.2: Won't have items are an agreed scope decision, not a consequence of technical debt (book 9.3.2, 9.4.2).

11.q:
Which two statements about the quality practice in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?

1. Product descriptions, quality specifications and quality tolerances can be prioritized and decomposed so that what is delivered can flex.
2. Testing is grouped at the end of each release so that the iterations can focus on building features.
3. Products are aligned with the quality management approach through quality planning, quality control and product acceptance.
4. An organization's own testing procedures are set aside in favour of those in the quality register.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
11.w: Statement 1 is how agile keeps the focus on products while letting what is delivered flex (book Table 5.1); statement 3 is the quality cycle (book 9.3.1). Statement 2 is wrong because testing is done first or as you go inside iterations (9.4.3); statement 4 is wrong because own procedures may be used and recorded in the PID, and the quality register records activities, not procedures (9.3.1, Table 9.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is false: agile tests first or as you go within iterations rather than grouping testing at the end of a release (book 9.4.3).
n.2: Both statements are false: testing is not deferred to the end of a release (9.4.3), and an organization's own procedures may be kept, with the quality register recording activities rather than procedures (9.3.1, Table 9.1).
n.3: Statement 4 is false: an organization's own procedures may be used as a tailoring decision recorded in the PID (book 9.3.1).

11.q: A team coach at a logistics firm puts a burn-down chart on the team dashboard. What does a burn-down chart show?
o: Completed work rising towards a total scope line across stages
The number of work items in each workflow state over time
Outstanding work falling over time, often across an iteration
Total risk exposure falling as risk responses take effect
11.w: A burn-down chart is a run chart of outstanding work over time, typically used at team level to show story points remaining over the days of an iteration (book 12.4.3).

n.0: Completed work rising against a scope line over stages describes a burn-up chart, usually used at project or product level (book 12.4.3).
n.1: Items in each workflow state over time is a cumulative flow diagram, used to reveal bottlenecks (book 12.4.2).
n.3: Falling total risk exposure is shown by a cumulative risk burn-down chart, a risk technique, not a progress burn-down (book 10.4.2).

11.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, which action is MOST LIKELY to build social cohesion in a hybrid team whose members are spread across several cities?
o: Requiring all team members to work from the same office every day
Running all online meetings to a strict, formal agenda
Replacing face-to-face workshops with written status updates
Arranging synchronized co-location days for key people and teams
11.w: For remote and hybrid teams, PRINCE2 Agile suggests synchronized co-location days for key people and teams, plus time for less structured conversation online, to build social cohesion (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.3).

n.0: Mandating full-time co-location is not the book's answer; it suggests planned, synchronized co-location days for key people (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.3).
n.1: Strict formal agendas leave no room for the less structured conversation that helps remote people build cohesion (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.3).
n.2: Written updates reduce contact between people; social cohesion grows when people meet purposefully and regularly (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.3.3).

11.q: Apart from resolving a blocker, in which other situation does PRINCE2 Agile say swarming can be useful?
o: To speed up the completion of time-sensitive work
To replace low-priority stories with new ones of equal effort
To assess how suitable the environment is for agile working
To track the total risk exposure from one iteration to the next
11.w: Swarming can be applied in various contexts, such as accelerating task completion or responding to time-sensitive requirements, though it is especially effective for resolving blockers (book 11.4.2).

n.1: Replacing stories with others of similar effort is trading, not swarming (book 11.4.1).
n.2: Assessing suitability for agile working is the purpose of the Agilometer (book 10.3.1).
n.3: Tracking total risk exposure across iterations is done with the cumulative risk burn-down chart (book 10.4.2).

11.q: A city council hires an external software company to build its new parking permit app, while council staff act as the users. Which project context does PRINCE2 say must be taken into account because of this arrangement?
o: Commercial
Organizational
Scale
Delivery method
11.w: The commercial context recognizes that the suppliers of a project's products may be external to the sponsoring organization, as with the software company here (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.4).

n.1: The organizational context is about whether the project is standalone or part of a programme or portfolio, not about external suppliers (book 1.3.4).
n.2: Scale is about how simple or complex the project is and how formal its governance must be, not about who supplies the products (book 1.3.4).
n.3: The delivery method context is about how the work is delivered, for example linear-sequential or iterative-incremental, not about external suppliers (book 1.3.4).

11.q: Which statement best explains how epics and user stories relate to each other in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Epics sit in each team's product backlog, while user stories sit in the project backlog
Epics are written after the user stories are finished, to summarize what was delivered
Epics are high level and often vague, so they are broken down into detailed user stories
Epics replace user stories when the project uses a linear, waterfall delivery method
11.w: Requirements often start large or vague; these epics are high-level stories that are broken down into more detailed user stories as work approaches (book 8.3.2.2). The project backlog holds mostly epics, and team product backlogs hold the detailed stories (book 8.3.2.1).

n.0: This reverses the levels: the project backlog holds mostly epics and each team's product backlog holds detailed user stories (book 8.3.2.1).
n.1: Epics come first, as broad requirements, and are decomposed into stories; they are not written afterwards as a summary (book 8.3.2.2).
n.3: Epics and user stories are agile requirement formats used for iterative delivery; they are not a substitute format for waterfall projects (book 8.3.2.2).

11.q: In the 'prepare the next stage plan' activity of managing a stage boundary, what does the project manager update in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: The release map for the next stage, applying lessons and updating PID components
The team plan for each iteration of the next stage, on behalf of the teams
The team dashboards, so that each team reports in the same standard format
The project canvas workshop outputs, by repeating the workshop with the executive
11.w: Preparing the next stage plan reviews and updates PID components, applies lessons and updates the release map for the next stage, since the release map is the agile form of the stage plan (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.15, ch 8).

n.1: Team plans are produced by the delivery teams in managing product delivery; the stage boundary works at release map level (book Table 13.12).
n.2: Team dashboards are co-created and updated by each team; imposing one format conflicts with self-management (book Table 13.8).
n.3: The project canvas workshop belongs to starting up a project; it is not repeated to prepare the next stage plan (book 13.2.4.1).

11.q: At the start of a new project, the project manager reviews lessons from similar past projects and talks to people who have delivered comparable work elsewhere. Which principle is being applied?
o: Learn from experience
Ensure continued business justification
Manage by stages
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
11.w: Learn from experience: lessons from previous projects are sought at the start and applied throughout, especially when the work is new to the organization (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 5.2; PRINCE2 7 manual 2.2; 'assess previous lessons' in starting up, book Table 13.1).

n.1: Ensure continued business justification is about the project remaining worthwhile, not about reviewing lessons from earlier projects (book 5.2.1.1).
n.2: Manage by stages is about stage-by-stage authorization and control, not about gathering lessons (book 5.2.1.4).
n.3: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships is about clear roles and stakeholder engagement; consulting others here is to gather lessons (book 5.2.1.3).

11.q: A project board wants regular, visual information on stage progress instead of written reports. Which agile artifact replaces both the highlight report and the end stage report?
o: Team dashboard
Release map
Project dashboard
Cumulative flow diagram
11.w: The project dashboard replaces the highlight report and the end stage report; it is updated and reviewed in progress review workshops so the board can pull the information it needs (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1).

n.0: The team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report and reports from the team to the project manager (book Table 12.1).
n.1: The release map replaces the project and stage plans; it is a plan, not a progress report (book 8.3.2.5).
n.3: A cumulative flow diagram is a mostly team-level technique showing tasks in each workflow state; it does not replace either report (book 12.4.2).

11.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.

If technical debt is not paid back, it builds up [?], making later changes harder and more costly.
o: tolerance
contingency
interest
velocity
11.w: Like financial debt, unpaid technical debt accumulates interest, making future change harder, raising disorder and lowering quality (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.4.2).

n.0: Tolerances may be set for technical debt, but tolerance is a permitted limit, not what unpaid debt accumulates (book 9.4.2).
n.1: Contingency is room kept in reserve, such as Could haves; it is not what unpaid technical debt accumulates (book 9.4.2).
n.3: Velocity is the rate at which a team delivers story points; debt tends to slow work rather than build velocity (book 12.4.3, 9.4.2).

11.q: A delivery team has used delegation poker to agree the levels at which its members make decisions. Which statement about the outcome is correct?
o: The agreed levels replace the tolerances set by the project board
The agreed levels are approved by the senior supplier each iteration
The agreed levels apply to the project board's decisions as well
The team still works within tolerances and escalates beyond them
11.w: Self-management in PRINCE2 Agile operates inside agreed boundaries: teams know the limits of self-management and when decisions must be escalated, and product owners deliver within tolerances agreed with the PM (book 4.5, Table 7.2).

n.0: Delegation within a team does not override the tolerances set through the governance levels.
n.1: Delegation levels are a team agreement; the senior supplier does not approve them each iteration.
n.2: Delegation poker defines decision-making within teams; it does not change the board's decisions.

11.q: Which statement correctly contrasts a project with business as usual (BAU)?
o: A project is repetitive, while BAU work is unique and temporary
A project has no fixed end, while BAU work has a start and an end
A project avoids change, while BAU work introduces the change
A project is unique, while BAU work is repetitive and ongoing
11.w: A project is unique (a different team, customer, product, location or timeframe), whereas BAU is repetitive and ongoing (book 1.3.1).

n.0: This reverses the contrast: BAU is repetitive and ongoing, and projects are unique and temporary (1.3.1).
n.1: Projects are temporary with a start and an end; BAU is ongoing (1.3.1).
n.2: Projects introduce change; BAU identifies the need for it and adopts it afterwards (1.3.1).

11.q: What is the central aim of Lean thinking, one of the agile-related approaches recognized in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Removing waste so that the flow of value to the customer is maximised
Limiting each sprint to one month or less to keep feedback frequent
Testing a minimum viable product with early users to validate ideas
Writing tests before writing code to improve technical quality
11.w: Lean is about eliminating waste to maximise the flow of value to the customer (book Glossary; Lean Enterprise Institute).

n.1: Sprint length limits belong to Scrum, not Lean.
n.2: Testing an MVP to validate ideas is the hallmark of Lean Startup, which builds on Lean but is a separate approach.
n.3: Test-first programming comes from eXtreme Programming (XP) (Glossary).

11.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, how can AI support communication within an agile project?
o: By automating routine information updates so leaders can focus on high-impact communication
By replacing face-to-face conversations with stakeholders on the progress of the project
By deciding which stakeholder messages the project board needs to approve before release
By removing the need to agree a communication management approach for the project
11.w: AI supports communication by automating the collection and dissemination of information and answering common questions through a project chatbot, freeing leaders for strategic, high-impact communication; it does not remove the need to communicate with stakeholders (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.2).

n.1: AI supports communication, but the need for people to communicate with stakeholders remains (book 15.4.2).
n.2: The book does not give AI a role in deciding which messages the board approves; communication decisions stay with people (book 15.4.2).
n.3: The communication management approach remains a PRINCE2 Agile product; AI helps carry out communication, it does not remove the approach (book 15.4.2).

11.q: Which project context has the most direct influence on how formal a project's governance, documentation, project structure and tolerances need to be?
o: Commercial
Organizational
Delivery method
Scale
11.w: Scale: projects range from relatively simple to large and complex, and the scale influences how the project is managed and controlled, including the formality of governance, documentation, structure and tolerances (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.4).

n.0: The commercial context concerns suppliers that may be external to the sponsoring organization; the book links formality of control to scale (book 1.3.4).
n.1: The organizational context concerns whether the project is standalone or part of a programme or portfolio; the book links formality of control to scale (book 1.3.4).
n.2: The delivery method context concerns linear-sequential or iterative-incremental work; the book links formality of control to scale (book 1.3.4).

11.q: In a team planning workshop at a hospital trust, the team added a response to a supplier-delay risk to its backlog. During the next iteration, the developers carry out that response as part of their normal work. Which step of the risk technique is this, and where does PRINCE2 Agile place it?
o: Implement, which is part of the continuous iteration cycles
Plan, which is completed in the agile enablement workshop by the board
Assess, which is carried out when the team plan is produced
Communicate, which is handled by updating the project dashboard
11.w: Carrying out planned risk responses is the implement step, which PRINCE2 Agile makes part of the continuous iteration cycles (book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).

n.1: Planning the response happened when the team added it to the backlog; the agile enablement workshop deals with risks to agile adoption, not team-level responses (book 10.3.1, Table 13.5).
n.2: Assessing means estimating and evaluating the risk; carrying out a response that is already planned is implementation (book 10.3.1).
n.3: Carrying out the response is implement, not communicate; communicating uses the established procedures and feedback loops, and nothing is being reported here (book 10.3.1).

11.q: During the project closure workshop, participants bring the PID, the logs, the project dashboard and the Agilometer up to date. Which topic of the project closure workshop is this?
o: Lessons report
Progress review
Project lessons
Final handover planning
11.w: In the project closure workshop, the progress review topic updates the PID, logs, project dashboard and Agilometer (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.19).

n.0: The lessons report topic uses these updates to produce actionable lessons; it is not where the PID, logs and dashboard are updated (book Table 13.19).
n.2: Project lessons shares insights gained during the project, rather than updating the project's records (book Table 13.19).
n.3: Final handover planning agrees support responsibilities, operational requirements and benefits actions (book Table 13.19).

11.q: In a complex environment, why does PRINCE2 Agile favour an agile mindset over searching for a perfect solution?
o: Complex work needs a fixed, detailed plan agreed before delivery so that change can be avoided
Complexity removes the need for governance, so teams can make every decision themselves
Perfect solutions can be found by doing more detailed upfront analysis in each stage
Complexity brings ambiguity, so staying adaptable and able to pivot is worth more than perfection
11.w: Because complexity creates ambiguity, there is rarely one perfect answer; it is better to stay adaptable and able to pivot quickly than to chase perfection (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.4).

n.0: A fixed plan that avoids change is the opposite of the agile response to complexity (book 2.4).
n.1: PRINCE2 Agile keeps governance and control; self-management works within agreed tolerances (book 3.1).
n.2: The book says there is rarely one perfect solution in complex work, so more upfront analysis does not find one (book 2.4).

11.q: One of the principles behind the Agile Manifesto concerns sustainable development. What does it say sponsors, developers and users should be able to do?
o: Increase their pace in every iteration
Maintain a constant pace indefinitely
Work extra hours before each release
Match the pace of the fastest team
11.w: The Agile Manifesto principles state that agile processes promote sustainable development, with sponsors, developers and users able to keep a constant pace indefinitely (agilemanifesto.org/principles). This supports agility that lasts rather than short bursts.

n.0: The principle asks for a pace that can be kept up, not one that keeps rising (agilemanifesto.org/principles).
n.2: Bursts of overtime before releases are the opposite of a sustainable, constant pace (agilemanifesto.org/principles).
n.3: Each team works at a pace it can sustain; matching another team's pace is not the principle (agilemanifesto.org/principles).

11.q: Which statement about the commercial management approach in a PRINCE2 Agile project is correct?
o: It sets out how each supplier's delivery team will run its iterations
It replaces the role descriptions when external suppliers are involved
It can define fixed teams and cost per iteration and an agreed DoD
It mainly records the skill levels of the supplier's team members
11.w: The commercial management approach makes procurement and contracts support agile delivery, for example through fixed delivery teams and costs per iteration, a defined MVP and tolerances, and an agreed Definition of Done (book 7.3.2, Table 7.3).

n.0: The approach covers selecting and contracting suppliers, not the supplier's own internal ways of working.
n.1: Role descriptions remain a separate product; the commercial approach does not replace them.
n.3: Skill levels are mapped in the team skill matrix, not in the commercial management approach.

11.q: When an agile project's product is transferred to the operations team, PRINCE2 Agile recommends handing over the project's agile artifacts and tools. What is the main purpose of doing this?
o: To give end users a quick-start guide to the main features of the new product
To define the service levels and maintenance schedules for the support teams
To set out the contacts and timelines for resolving operational issues quickly
To keep the ways of working aligned with agile practices after the transition
11.w: Handing over agile artifacts and tools effectively ensures continuity and alignment with agile practices once the product is in operations (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 14.2.1).

n.0: Quick-start guides, manuals and videos support user adoption alongside training; they are not the purpose of handing over agile artifacts (book 14.2.1).
n.1: Service levels and maintenance schedules belong in the step-by-step operational procedures, a separate part of the transition (book 14.2.1).
n.2: Contacts and timelines for issue resolution are the escalation pathways, which help knowledge transfer but are a separate measure (book 14.2.1).

11.q: When the business case is tailored into a project canvas, which scenarios should the canvas outline?
o: Best-case, worst-case and expected-case scenarios
Must have, Should have and Could have scenarios
Current-state, transition-state and target-state scenarios
Threat, opportunity and secondary-risk scenarios
11.w: PRINCE2 Agile tailors the business case into the project canvas, which should outline best-case, worst-case and expected-case scenarios (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 5.2).

n.1: Must, Should and Could are MoSCoW priorities used for scope, not business case scenarios (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Current and target states describe organizational change in OCM, not business case scenarios (book 4.2.1).
n.3: Threats and opportunities are risk categories recorded through the risk practice, not canvas scenarios (book 10.1, Table 13.3).

11.q: When does the confirm step of the business case technique mostly take place, and why can part of it happen earlier in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: Before initiation, because the project mandate already states the expected benefits in full
Mostly after closure, but releasing products iteratively can realize some benefits during the project
At each daily stand-up, because every completed user story carries a benefit that can be confirmed
At the end of initiation, because the full project canvas is approved by the board at that point
11.w: Confirming benefits mostly happens after the project closes, but because agile releases products iteratively, some benefits may be realized and confirmed during the project (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.3.1).

n.0: Benefits cannot be confirmed before anything is delivered; the mandate only triggers starting up (book 6.3.1, Table 13.1).
n.2: Stand-ups coordinate daily work; benefits are measurable improvements from outcomes and are confirmed through benefits reviews, not story by story (book 6.3.1, Table 6.1).
n.3: Approving the full project canvas authorizes the project; it confirms the justification, not that benefits have been realized (book Table 13.4, 6.3.1).

11.q:
Identify the missing words in the following sentence.

During the project initiation workshop, the team may decide that the [?] should replace the change management approach when the organization's move to agile working needs it.
o: project canvas
agile transformation plan
communication management approach
release map
11.w: When the management approaches are co-created in the project initiation workshop, the agile transformation plan can replace the change management approach if needed (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).

n.0: The project canvas summarizes the project and its business case; it is refined in initiation but does not replace the change management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).
n.2: The communication management approach is a separate approach agreed alongside the change management approach, not a replacement for it (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.6).
n.3: The release map replaces the project and stage plans, not the change management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, plans practice).

11.q: A project manager says the communication management approach must give a controlled, bidirectional flow of information. What does PRINCE2 Agile mean by describing communication in this way?
o: Listening and gathering feedback matter as much as sending information out
The project manager and the CPO share responsibility for sending messages
Each message is sent twice, once in writing and once in a meeting
Users and suppliers receive the same messages at the same time
11.w: Bidirectional communication is as much about listening as about broadcasting: it gathers feedback and concerns as well as sending information (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).

n.1: Bidirectional refers to information flowing both out to and back from stakeholders, not to two senders sharing the work (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).
n.2: Repeating a message in two formats is still one-way broadcasting; bidirectional means receiving feedback too (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).
n.3: Sending identical messages to all groups is generic messaging, which the book says is rarely effective (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).

11.q: While initiating an agile project at a port authority, the project manager writes the artifact that describes how issues will be captured and reported, and how changes to the project baseline will be assessed and controlled. Which artifact is this?
o: Issue register
Issue report
Risk management approach
Issue management approach
11.w: The issue management approach describes how issues will be captured and reported and how changes to the project baseline will be assessed and controlled (book Table 11.1).

n.0: The issue register records the formal issues themselves and their status; it does not describe the procedure (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 11.1).
n.1: An issue report describes one issue's impact on the baseline, the options and a recommendation; it does not set out the overall procedure (book Table 11.1).
n.2: The risk management approach describes how risk will be managed, not how issues and baseline changes will be handled (book Table 10.1).

11.q: A project at Calder Rail has four delivery teams. Which arrangement fits PRINCE2 Agile guidance on scaling?
o: A project manager for each team, each reporting to a separate project board
One product owner across all the teams, with a chief product owner inside each team
One team coach for all four teams, taking over the work of the product owners
One project manager, a chief product owner across the teams and a product owner per team
11.w: With multiple teams there is one project manager, possibly several product owners (one per team) and one chief product owner prioritizing across the teams (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.3.1, Figure 7.2).

n.0: Scaling keeps one project manager and one set of governance; it does not create a project and board per team (book 3.2, 7.3.1).
n.1: This reverses the roles: the chief product owner works across teams and each team has its own product owner (book 7.3.1).
n.2: A team coach works with one or two teams and does not replace product owners (book Table 7.2).

11.q: Which approach was originally developed for creating and managing start-up companies but is now applied by many kinds of business to get products to customers quickly?
o: Lean
eXtreme Programming (XP)
Lean Startup
Kanban
11.w: The Glossary describes Lean Startup as originally intended for creating and managing start-ups and now used by any business to deliver products to customers quickly (book Glossary).

n.0: Lean focuses on removing waste and improving flow; the start-up origin belongs to Lean Startup.
n.1: XP is a set of engineering practices such as test-first programming, not a start-up method (Glossary).
n.3: Kanban is a flow method using WIP limits, not a start-up method (Glossary).

11.q: Story mapping is used to define and break down the work needed to build a product that meets user needs. Under which PRINCE2 Agile practice is the story map described as an artifact?
o: Plans
Quality
Business case
Progress
11.w: The story map is a plans practice artifact: it supports product-based planning by breaking products into user stories (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.4).

n.1: The quality practice covers acceptance criteria, the Definition of Ready and Definition of Done, not the story map (book 9.3.2).
n.2: The business case practice uses the project canvas, not the story map (book 6.3.2.1).
n.3: The progress practice uses dashboards, burn charts and reports, not the story map (book 12.3.2).

11.q: A product owner asks when a situation in a PRINCE2 Agile project becomes an exception. Which answer is correct?
o: When a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded
When a team's velocity drops in one iteration
When the product owner reorders the product backlog
When a user story fails the team's Definition of Done
11.w: An exception is a situation where tolerances are forecast to be exceeded; agile teams flex what is delivered within tolerance, so ordinary variation does not cause one (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1).

n.1: A dip in velocity is ordinary variation handled by the team; an exception needs a forecast breach of tolerance (book Table 12.1).
n.2: Reprioritizing the product backlog is normal product owner work within tolerance, not an exception (book 8.3.2.1).
n.3: A story that is not done is reworked or stays in the backlog; failing the Definition of Done is a quality matter, not an exception (book 9.3.2.2).

11.q: Which pairing of a PRINCE2 management product with the agile artifact used for it in PRINCE2 Agile is correct?
o: Checkpoint report and team dashboard
Highlight report and team dashboard
Product description and project backlog
Work package description and release map
11.w: The team dashboard is used in place of the checkpoint report; the PM pulls team progress from it (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1).

n.1: The highlight report pairs with the project dashboard, not the team dashboard (book Table 12.1).
n.2: The project backlog tailors the project product description; product descriptions pair with the team product backlog (book 8.3.2.1).
n.3: A work package description in agile is a set of user stories; the release map pairs with the project and stage plans (book Table 8.1).

11.q: A delivery team has completed 16, 20 and 24 story points in its first three iterations, and 120 story points remain in the release. Using the team's velocity, how many more iterations should the project manager forecast?
o: 4 more iterations
5 more iterations
6 more iterations
7 more iterations
11.w: Velocity is the average rate: (16 + 20 + 24) / 3 = 20 points per iteration, so 120 / 20 = 6 more iterations, assuming conditions stay the same (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3, 12.4.3).

n.0: Four iterations would need 30 points per iteration, faster than the team has achieved in any iteration so far.
n.1: Five iterations uses the best single iteration (24 points) instead of the average rate of 20 points.
n.3: Seven iterations implies about 17 points per iteration, below the team's measured average of 20.

11.q: In which PRINCE2 Agile workshop is a psychological safety assessment one of the agenda topics?
o: Team planning workshop
Release planning workshop
Project canvas workshop
Project kickoff workshop
11.w: The project kickoff workshop includes a psychological safety assessment alongside team introductions, team values and norms, the skill matrix and dashboards (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.4.4.2, Table 13.8).

n.0: The team planning workshop covers backlog refinement, user story refinement, estimation and iteration planning (Table 13.13).
n.1: The release planning workshop covers OKR definition and release planning at a stage boundary (13.7.4.1, Table 13.16).
n.2: The project canvas workshop builds the one-page business justification in starting up (13.2.4.1, Table 13.2).

11.q:
Which two statements about the team skill matrix in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. It is owned by the project executive and approved at each stage boundary.
2. It can show current skills and the expertise planned for the future.
3. It helps assign the right people to tasks and identify training needs.
4. It replaces the role descriptions for members of a delivery team.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 3
1 and 4
3 and 4
11.w: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the skill matrix shows current and planned skills and helps assign people and identify training needs (book 7.4.1, 4.5).

n.0: Statement 1 is wrong: the team builds the matrix collaboratively; it is not an executive-approved product.
n.2: Both are wrong: the matrix is the team's own tool, and role descriptions remain a separate product.
n.3: Statement 4 is wrong: role descriptions remain a separate organization product.

12.q: At the end of an iteration, a developer describes a user story as 'almost done'. How does PRINCE2 Agile treat this story against the Definition of Done?
o: It counts as done if most of its acceptance criteria have passed
It counts as done if the product owner agrees that it is close
It counts as half done and earns half of its story points
It is not done, as an item is either done or not done
12.w: Against the Definition of Done an item is either done or not done; there is no 'almost done' in agile (book 9.3.2.2).

n.0: Meeting most criteria is not meeting the DoD; any criterion still unmet means the item is not done (book 9.3.2.2).
n.1: The DoD is a shared, fixed set of criteria; a product owner's view that work is close does not change whether it is done (book 9.3.2.2).
n.2: There is no partial credit for a story; the finished part can be split off, and the rest returns to the backlog (book 9.3.2.2).

12.q: In the quality practice, what is the Definition of Ready?
o: A shared agreement on the criteria an item must meet to be considered complete
A checklist the project board uses before authorizing the next stage
A shared agreement on the criteria an item must meet before work on it begins
A list of the finished products and their approval and acceptance dates
12.w: The DoR is a shared team agreement on the criteria a task, deliverable or user story must meet before work begins, so the item is fully prepared (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 9.3.2.1).

n.0: Criteria for an item to count as complete form the Definition of Done, not the Definition of Ready (book 9.3.2.2).
n.1: Authorizing a stage is a board decision in directing a project; the DoR is a team-level agreement about work items (book 9.3.2.1).
n.3: Products with their status and acceptance dates are recorded in the product register (book Table 9.1).

12.q: A product team faces shifting customer needs in a market that changes from month to month. Which response does PRINCE2 Agile favour?
o: Spend longer on analysis so that a perfect solution can be specified upfront
Fix the full scope early so that the changing market cannot disrupt the plan
Stay adaptable and ready to pivot quickly rather than search for a perfect solution
Pause the work until the market settles and the requirements become stable
12.w: In complex, ambiguous situations the book favours staying adaptable and able to pivot quickly over trying to find the perfect solution upfront (book 2.4).

n.0: Hunting for a perfect solution upfront is what the book advises against in complex situations (2.4).
n.1: Fixing all scope early removes the flexibility needed to respond to change; only Must haves are fixed by default (Table 3.1).
n.3: Waiting for stability delays value; the book's response to complexity is to stay adaptable (2.4).

12.q: Which agile approach is a lightweight, iterative framework in which work is organized into short, timeboxed sprints to tackle complex problems?
o: Kanban
Scrum
Lean
Lean Startup
12.w: Scrum is an iterative, timeboxed approach to product delivery; the Scrum Guide describes it as a lightweight framework for generating value through adaptive solutions to complex problems, using sprints (book Glossary).

n.0: Kanban focuses on flow and WIP limits; iterations are optional rather than built around sprints (Glossary).
n.2: Lean is a way of thinking about removing waste, not a sprint-based framework.
n.3: Lean Startup is about quickly getting products to customers and learning, not sprint timeboxes (Glossary).

12.q: An updated release-level burn chart shows that the Must-have stories cannot all be delivered by the fixed release date. According to the progress practice, what should happen first?
o: Extend the release by one iteration so that every Must-have story is delivered
Ask the board to raise cost tolerance so that more developers can join the team
Hold an immediate project meeting to discuss options before escalating to the board
Ask the team to swarm and record the shortfall in the lessons log for later review
12.w: An updated burn chart at iteration or release level can trigger an exception; the progress practice suggests an immediate project meeting to discuss the options before the matter is escalated to the project board (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1).

n.0: Time has zero tolerance on all levels of plan, so extending the release is not the agile response (book Table 3.1).
n.1: Cost has zero tolerance on all levels of plan, and options are discussed in a project meeting before anything goes to the board (book Table 3.1, Table 12.1).
n.3: Swarming suits a stuck task or blocker, not a forecast shortfall in Must-haves, and the lessons log records lessons rather than escalating a breach (book 11.4.2, Table 12.1).

12.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, who normally defines a delivery team's OKRs, and in which workshop?
o: The project board, which hands them to teams in the agile enablement workshop
The agile coach, who sets them for each team at the project kickoff workshop
Project assurance, which uses them to audit each team at the progress review
The team itself, with other teams and the PM, in the release planning workshop
12.w: Teams define their own OKRs in a workshop with other teams and the project manager during managing a stage boundary, which is the release planning workshop (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.3.2.3, Table 13.16).

n.0: The agile enablement workshop is where the board reviews Agilometer assessments; it does not hand OKRs to teams (book Table 13.5).
n.1: The agile coach supports agile adoption across the organization; OKR definition is not a kickoff topic, and teams set their own OKRs (book Table 13.8, Table 13.16).
n.2: Project assurance monitors adherence to principles and practices; it does not define team OKRs, and the progress review looks at the project dashboard (book Table 7.2, 13.5.4.1).

12.q:
Which two statements about the risk technique in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. Risks can be raised at any point in the project, as well as in planning sessions and retrospectives.
2. The 'assess' step is where risks are first gathered and documented.
3. The 'plan' step is addressed by planning the necessary risk responses.
4. The 'communicate' step takes place once, when the stage is closed.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
12.w: Statement 1 is true: planning sessions and retrospectives are the fixed points for identifying risks, but risks can surface at any time and in any workshop. Statement 3 is true: the plan step plans the necessary risk responses (book 10.3.1, Figure 10.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is false: risks are gathered and documented in the identify step; assess is where they are estimated and evaluated (book 10.3.1).
n.2: Both statements are false: gathering risks belongs to identify, and communicate is part of the continuous feedback loops in every iteration and stage, not a one-off at stage close (book 10.3.1).
n.3: Statement 4 is false: communicating risks happens through the established communication procedures and feedback loops throughout each iteration (book 10.3.1).

12.q: A bank is piloting agile working on one project and asks whether it needs an agile transformation plan yet. What does PRINCE2 Agile suggest?
o: Write an agile transformation plan before the pilot's initiation stage begins
Record the transition steps in the project canvas instead of a separate product
Update the change management approach, as a plan may not be needed for one pilot
Ask the agile coach to replace the communication management approach with a plan
12.w: An agile transformation plan typically spans several projects for organization-wide adoption; for a single pilot it may not be needed yet, and the change management approach can be updated instead (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.7.1).

n.0: The book suggests a transformation plan may not be needed for a single pilot, so writing one first is not its suggestion (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.7.1).
n.1: The project canvas summarizes the project and its business case; the transition is described in the change management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1).
n.3: Where a transformation plan is used, it can replace the change management approach, not the communication management approach (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).

12.q: Which statement describes the authority of the project manager in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: They set priorities across all delivery teams on behalf of the users
They approve the tolerances for agile decision-making on the project
They direct the daily work of each developer and tester in the teams
They run the project day to day for the board within agreed tolerances
12.w: The project manager has authority to run the project on a day-to-day basis on behalf of the board, within the tolerances and constraints the board has agreed (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.0: Setting priorities across teams on behalf of users is the chief product owner's responsibility.
n.1: Approving tolerances for agile decision-making is the project executive's responsibility.
n.2: Delivery team members are led by their product owner and manage their own work; the PM does not direct them individually.

12.q: In card-based story point estimating, every team member picks a value privately on a pre-numbered card and all the cards are revealed at the same moment. Why is this done?
o: So that the product owner can adopt the highest card as the final value
So that each person gives an independent view without being swayed by others
So that the estimate can be turned straight into hours for the team plan
So that the project manager can log each member's estimate on the dashboard
12.w: Agile estimation draws on the whole team so everyone contributes without being swayed by others; revealing simultaneously keeps each estimate independent before differences are discussed (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.4.3).

n.0: The team discusses differences and agrees a shared value; the product owner does not simply take the highest card (book 8.4.3).
n.2: Story points stay relative estimates; they are not converted to hours (book 8.4.3).
n.3: The aim is unbiased team estimates; individual estimates are not dashboard content (book 8.4.3, Table 12.1).

12.q: How should communication for a remote team differ from that for a co-located team, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
o: It can rely on information being shared organically between colleagues
It is handed over to project support to reduce the load on the team
It is limited to the written reports defined in the project initiation documentation
It needs a more deliberate, structured approach, including how information flows
12.w: Remote teams need a more deliberate and structured approach: clarity on how information flows, suitable formats, key relationships identified, and agreed structured and unstructured time together (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).

n.0: Organic sharing is what co-located teams benefit from; remote teams need deliberate methods instead (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4, PRINCE2 7 manual 3.3.3).
n.1: Project support helps with administration, but communication for remote teams needs agreed structure involving the team itself (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).
n.2: Relying on written reports alone is not enough, and the book asks for both structured and unstructured time together (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4).

12.q: What does the product register record in a PRINCE2 Agile project?
o: All the products required by a plan and their current status
All the user stories selected for the coming iteration
All planned and completed quality activities and their results
All the lessons learned about product quality so far
12.w: The product register lists all products required by a plan with their status, identifiers, approval and acceptance dates and references (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 9.1).

n.1: Stories selected for an iteration form the team plan agreed in the team planning workshop (book Table 13.13).
n.2: Planned and completed quality activities with results are the content of the quality register (book Table 9.1).
n.3: Lessons are recorded in the lessons log, part of the project log (book Table 12.1).

12.q: A project manager at a rail operator is explaining the issues practice to new product owners. In PRINCE2 Agile, when is a change to a requirement treated as a change to the project baseline?
o: When the change is estimated to take the team more than one iteration to build
When a developer and a tester disagree about a story's acceptance criteria
When the new or changed requirement means the project backlog has to change
When the product owner reorders the user stories in the team's product backlog
12.w: If a new or changed requirement means the project backlog needs to change, it is a change to the project baseline and must be handled formally (book 11.3.2).

n.0: The size of the work does not decide the route; what matters is whether the project backlog, the project baseline, must change (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 11.3.2).
n.1: A disagreement over acceptance criteria inside a story is team-level detail and does not by itself alter the project backlog (book 11.3.2).
n.3: Reordering a team's product backlog is normal prioritization at team level; it does not change the project backlog (book 11.3.2, 8.3.2.1).

12.q: In which process does the detailed estimation of user stories normally take place in PRINCE2 Agile, and in which part of it?
o: Directing a project, when the board reviews the release map in the agile enablement workshop
Closing a project, when actual effort is compared with the original estimates for each release
Starting up a project, when the project canvas workshop agrees the cost definition for the project
Managing product delivery, in the effort estimation topic of the team planning workshop
12.w: Estimation of work is part of the plans practice and takes place during managing product delivery; the team planning workshop includes an effort estimation topic to reach a shared view of each story's effort (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.13).

n.0: The agile enablement workshop reviews Agilometer assessments and agile adoption risks, not story estimates (book Table 13.5).
n.1: Closing a project reviews performance and confirms acceptance; estimating stories happens before they are built (book Table 13.13).
n.2: Cost definition in the project canvas workshop sets out the project's costs at a high level, not detailed story estimates (book Table 13.2).

12.q: A tester finds that a finished feature does not meet the acceptance criteria that were agreed for it. Which practice provides the means to capture and assess this and to control any resulting change to the project's baseline?
o: Issues
Quality
Risk
Progress
12.w: A product that deviates from what was agreed is an issue. The issues practice collects and assesses issues and controls changes to the baseline, answering 'what now, when a product deviates from what was agreed?' (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 11.1, Table 5.2).

n.1: Quality documents users' requirements and how they will be met; once a product has deviated from what was agreed, capturing it and controlling baseline change is the issues purpose (book 9.1, 11.1).
n.2: Risk deals with uncertain events that may happen; this deviation has already happened, so it is an issue (book 10.1, 11.1).
n.3: Progress compares actual achievement with plan and handles deviations that cause an exception, not the assessment of an individual off-specification (book 11.1, 12.1).

12.q: What is the purpose of the release planning workshop in the 'managing a stage boundary' process?
o: To prepare a delivery team for its next iteration by refining, estimating and selecting stories
To build shared understanding of objectives, align teams with the vision and plan the next stage
To assess agile maturity and agile risks with the board, agile coaches and business representatives
To formally conclude the project, confirm the final product and prepare for handover to operations
12.w: The release planning workshop builds shared understanding of objectives, aligns teams with the vision and plans the next stage, reviewing the project canvas, project backlog and release map (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.7.4.1).

n.0: Preparing the next iteration is the purpose of the team planning workshop in managing product delivery (book 13.6.4.1).
n.2: Assessing agile maturity and risks with the board is the purpose of the agile enablement workshop in directing a project (book 13.3.3).
n.3: Formally concluding the project is the purpose of the project closure workshop (book 13.8.4).

12.q: A transport authority uses AI to analyse historical and real-time project data, forecasting whether the expected benefits will still line up with the timelines and budget and warning early of cost overruns. Which PRINCE2 principle does PRINCE2 Agile say this use of AI supports?
o: Learn from experience
Ensure continued business justification
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Tailor to suit the project
12.w: AI supports ensuring continued business justification by using predictive analytics to forecast whether anticipated benefits will align with projected timelines and budgets, and by flagging early signs of overruns (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 15.4.1).

n.0: AI supports learning from experience by turning large volumes of lessons into searchable, prioritized insights, not by forecasting viability (book 15.4.1).
n.2: AI supports defined roles, responsibilities and relationships by analysing skills and workload to suggest role assignments, not by forecasting viability (book 15.4.1).
n.3: AI supports tailoring by spotting similarities with past projects and suggesting how to adapt the method (book 15.4.1).

12.q: Which pairing of a performance aspect with its PRINCE2 Agile default is correct?
o: Sustainability: fixed for minimum criteria, flexed above them
Time: fixed for Must haves, flexed for Should and Could haves
Benefits: zero tolerance on all levels of plan
Scope: fixed for minimum viability, flexed above it
12.w: Sustainability is fixed for the minimum criteria and flexed for anything above them (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1).

n.1: Time has zero tolerance for extra time on all levels of plan; the Must, Should and Could split is the scope default (book Table 3.1).
n.2: Benefits are fixed for minimum viability and flexed above it; zero tolerance on all levels applies to time and cost (book Table 3.1).
n.3: Scope is fixed for Must haves and flexed for Should and Could haves; minimum viability is the benefits default (book Table 3.1).

12.q: Which statement reflects the agile mindset described in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Agile is less about strict adherence to a framework and more about collaboration and adaptability
Agile is mainly about choosing one framework and applying its rules consistently in every team
Agile is about finding the one perfect solution through detailed analysis before work starts
Agile is mainly about reducing documentation so that teams can spend more time building
12.w: PRINCE2 Agile describes agile as less about rigid adherence to a framework and more about collaboration, creativity and adaptability (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.3).

n.1: The book stresses that agile is less about rigid adherence to a framework (book 2.3).
n.2: Complexity creates ambiguity, so there is rarely one perfect solution; staying adaptable is preferred (book 2.4).
n.3: Reduced paperwork is not what the book identifies as the heart of agile; it emphasizes collaboration, creativity and adaptability (book 2.3).

12.q:
Which two statements about the activities of the 'controlling a stage' process are correct?

1. In 'escalate issues and risks', the project manager recommends options to the board in an exception report.
2. Every activity of the process needs its own dedicated agile workshop.
3. In 'receive completed work package', the board confirms the set of user stories was delivered.
4. In 'evaluate work package status', the project manager pulls progress from the team dashboard.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 3
3 and 4
1 and 4
12.w: Statement 1 describes 'escalate issues and risks' and statement 4 describes 'evaluate work package status' (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.9).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the book places 'evaluate stage status' in a progress review and says activities such as authorizing a work package or taking corrective action need no dedicated agile event (book Table 13.9).
n.1: Both are wrong: activities such as authorizing a work package need no dedicated agile event, and it is the project manager, not the board, who receives completed work packages (book Table 13.9).
n.2: Statement 3 is wrong: 'receive completed work package' is a project manager activity in controlling a stage, not a board decision (book Table 13.9).

12.q: Which statement describes the developer role in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: Designs, develops and maintains product increments and resolves technical issues
Designs and runs tests, then checks products against the team Definition of Done
Facilitates the team's workshops and helps the team to write its user stories
Agrees the work package descriptions for the team with the project manager
12.w: The developer designs, develops and maintains increments of the products, resolves technical issues and keeps improving the outputs (book Table 7.2, Table B.1).

n.1: Designing and running tests against the team DoD describes the tester.
n.2: Facilitating team workshops and helping write user stories describes the team coach.
n.3: Agreeing work package descriptions with the PM is a product owner responsibility.

12.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
When a project buys in some of its products from a company outside the organization paying for the project, its [?] context must be taken into account.
o: organizational
commercial
scale
delivery method
12.w: The commercial context applies when the project's products come from suppliers outside the sponsoring organization (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.4).

n.0: The organizational context concerns whether the project is standalone or part of a programme or portfolio (book 1.3.4).
n.2: The scale context concerns how simple or complex the project is and therefore how formally it is controlled (book 1.3.4).
n.3: The delivery method context concerns whether work is linear-sequential or iterative-incremental (book 1.3.4).

12.q: When the change management approach is used to guide an agile transformation, what does PRINCE2 Agile say it should consider so that the change lasts?
o: The evolving culture and how to stop changes being rolled back afterwards
Financial rewards for the teams that adopt the new agile framework the fastest
Strict compliance checks on any team that departs from the new agile processes
A single announcement explaining the change to all of the affected staff
12.w: In deciding the detail of the change management approach, PRINCE2 Agile asks for consideration of the evolving culture and of how to ensure changes are not reversed once the transformation ends (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.1).

n.1: Rewards are not what the book names; it asks for the evolving culture to be considered (book 4.2.1).
n.2: Compliance checks do not make change stick; the book points to culture and preventing roll-back (book 4.2.1).
n.3: One-off communication is not enough; people need training, coaching and a culture that sustains the change (book 2.7.3, 4.2.1).

12.q: A team coach wants a chart that shows how many tasks sit in each workflow state over time, so that bottlenecks become visible. Which technique fits this need?
o: A burn-up chart
A cumulative flow diagram
A cumulative risk burn-down chart
A release map
12.w: A cumulative flow diagram shows the number of tasks in each workflow state over time and reveals bottlenecks; it is mostly used at team level (book 12.4.2).

n.0: A burn-up chart shows completed work against a deadline, not the spread of tasks across workflow states (book 12.4.3).
n.2: A cumulative risk burn-down chart tracks total risk exposure across iterations, not workflow states (book 10.4.2).
n.3: A release map is a plan of releases and their features; it does not chart work in progress over time (book 8.3.2.5).

12.q: Where is the team Definition of Done included or linked in PRINCE2 Agile?
o: In the project backlog
In the project canvas
In the release map
In the product backlog
12.w: A product backlog should include or link to the team Definition of Done; it is used at team level by the product owner (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 8.3.2.1).

n.0: The project backlog shows or links to the project-level DoR and DoD, not each team's DoD (book 8.3.2.1).
n.1: The project canvas records the business justification, not team quality criteria (book 6.3.2).
n.2: The release map shows releases, their timing and features; it does not hold the team DoD (book 8.3.2).

12.q:
Which two statements about the types of issue in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. A business opportunity is an issue with an immediate and negative impact on the project.
2. A request for change is a proposal for a change to a baseline.
3. An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications.
4. A problem is an issue that represents unanticipated positive consequences for the project.
o: 1 and 2
1 and 4
2 and 3
3 and 4
12.w: Statement 2 is true: a request for change proposes a change to a baseline. Statement 3 is true: an off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications (book 11.3.1).

n.0: Statement 1 is false: an immediate and negative impact describes a problem; a business opportunity brings unanticipated positive consequences (book 11.3.1).
n.1: Both statements are false: they swap the definitions of a business opportunity and a problem (book 11.3.1).
n.3: Statement 4 is false: unanticipated positive consequences describe a business opportunity; a problem has an immediate negative impact (book 11.3.1).

12.q: Which benefit to organizational change management does PRINCE2 Agile link to progress reviews that include demos?
o: They give the project board a formal point to approve the next stage
They replace retrospectives as the place to agree process improvements
They engage users and help to speed up adoption of the change
They set the time and cost tolerances for the next iteration
12.w: Progress reviews, including demos, enable user engagement and improve the speed of adoption (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).

n.0: Approval of the next stage is a project board decision in directing a project after managing a stage boundary, not the purpose of a progress review (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book, processes).
n.1: Retrospectives are the separate enabler for learning lessons and improving adoption; demos do not replace them (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.2.4).
n.3: Time and cost have zero tolerance at every level of plan in PRINCE2 Agile, and tolerances are not set in progress reviews (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 3.1).

12.q: A team coach is preparing a team planning workshop in the 'managing product delivery' process. What is the purpose of this workshop?
o: To prepare the next iteration and agree a realistic team plan
To review the project dashboard with the project board
To agree the project canvas before the project is initiated
To confirm the final product is ready for handover to users
12.w: The team planning workshop prepares the next iteration through backlog refinement, user story refinement, effort estimation and iteration planning, ending with a realistic team plan (book 13.6.4.1, Table 13.13).

n.1: Reviewing project dashboard metrics belongs to the progress review workshop in controlling a stage (book Table 13.10).
n.2: The project canvas is built in the project canvas workshop when the project is being started up (book 6.3.2.1).
n.3: Confirming the final product is ready for handover happens in the project closure workshop (book Table 13.19).

12.q:
Which two statements about projects and business as usual (BAU) are correct?
1. BAU identifies a need for change and a project is the means of introducing it.
2. A project continues until the product it delivers is retired from use.
3. Project teams normally sit within one functional department of BAU.
4. When a project ends, BAU adopts the change, which leads to the expected benefits.
o: 1 and 2
2 and 3
3 and 4
1 and 4
12.w: Statement 1 is the 'change' characteristic and statement 4 the 'temporary' characteristic: a project has a start and an end, after which BAU adopts the change and the expected benefits follow (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.1).

n.0: Statement 2 is wrong: a project is temporary and ends once the change is handed to BAU; running the product until retirement is BAU (book 1.3.1).
n.1: Both statements are wrong: projects end when the change is adopted, and project teams are cross-functional, working across BAU's functional divisions (book 1.3.1).
n.2: Statement 3 is wrong: project teams are cross-functional, working across functional divisions and sometimes across organizations (book 1.3.1).

12.q: How does PRINCE2 Agile keep a project governed while still giving delivery teams room to decide how they do their work?
o: Tolerances restrict what is delivered but allow flexibility in time and cost
Tolerances restrict time and cost but allow flexibility in what is delivered
The board approves each iteration plan before the team starts work on it
Tolerances are removed so that teams can agree changes directly with users
12.w: Manage by exception is at the heart of letting people self-manage while staying in control: in agile, tolerance is allowed on what is delivered and restricted on time and cost (book Table 5.1, Table 3.1).

n.0: This is the reverse: time and cost have zero tolerance by default, while scope below the Musts can flex (Table 3.1).
n.2: The board authorizes stages; iterations are planned by the teams themselves within the stage (5.2.1.4).
n.3: Tolerances are not removed; manage by exception still applies and is how the board stays in control (Table 5.1).

12.q: Which Agile Onion layer is defined by the Agile Manifesto and described as the foundation that encompasses all else?
o: Values
Practices
Processes
Mindset
12.w: Values are defined by the Agile Manifesto and form the foundation of agile, shifting focus from rigid processes to people, collaboration and user value (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.1).

n.1: Practices are techniques and activities, the most visible layer, not the foundation (book 2.6.1).
n.2: Processes give structure to agile implementations but do not guarantee agility (book 2.6.1).
n.3: The mindset is the innermost way of thinking; the layer defined by the Manifesto as the foundation is values (book 2.6.1).

12.q: PRINCE2 Agile recognizes three levels of timebox in a project. Which list names them?
o: Iteration, release and stage
Sprint, epic and project
Iteration, increment and phase
Release, work package and stage
12.w: The Glossary defines three levels of timebox: iteration, release and stage. A release usually contains two to four iterations, and in agile a stage contains timeboxed releases and iterations (book Glossary, 8.3.2.5, 5.2.1.4).

n.1: An epic is a large user story, not a timebox, and 'sprint' is the Scrum word for an iteration (Glossary).
n.2: An increment is a product output, not a timebox, and 'phase' is not one of the named levels (Glossary).
n.3: A work package is a set of work agreed between project manager and product owner, not a timebox level (Glossary).

12.q: In which agile workshop is persona definition one of the topics?
o: Project canvas workshop
Project kickoff workshop
Project initiation workshop
Release planning workshop
12.w: Persona definition, identifying and defining key user personas, is a topic of the project initiation workshop in initiating a project (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 13.7).

n.0: The project canvas workshop includes user group definition (one to three key groups), but persona definition is a project initiation workshop topic (book Table 13.2, Table 13.7).
n.1: The kickoff workshop covers team topics such as psychological safety, values and norms, the skill matrix and dashboards (book Table 13.8).
n.3: The release planning workshop, at a stage boundary, covers introduction, OKR definition, release planning and wrap-up (book Table 13.16).

12.q: In which situation can a PRINCE2 Agile project reasonably use a set of more than five personas?
o: When the organization's agile maturity is high
When the project has more than five delivery teams
When the project is a pilot of agile ways of working
When the users come from many demographic groups
12.w: The persona set can be enlarged when agile maturity is high; above five is not recommended for agile pilots or new products (see PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 6.4.1).

n.1: The number of teams is not the criterion; the book links a larger persona set to high agile maturity (book 6.4.1).
n.2: Pilots are exactly where more than five personas is not recommended (book 6.4.1).
n.3: Personas are based on needs, not demographics, so demographic variety does not justify more personas (book 6.4.1).

12.q: A project manager is documenting how the people on a PRINCE2 Agile project will work together, including team working practices, how performance reviews will run and how members gain access to project systems. Which product should hold this?
o: Role descriptions
Commercial management approach
Team skill matrix
Project management team structure
12.w: The project management team structure includes a section on working practices and arrangements, which is where performance reviews and access to project systems are described, alongside the structure chart and summary of authority (book Table 7.3).

n.0: Role descriptions set out each role's specific responsibilities; working practices and arrangements sit in the team structure.
n.1: The commercial management approach covers procurement and contracts, not internal working practices.
n.2: The team skill matrix maps capabilities and gaps; it does not hold working practices or system access.

12.q: A product owner reviews the draft OKRs for her team. Which statement correctly describes a key result?
o: An aspirational statement of what the team hopes to achieve next
A specific, measurable outcome that indicates progress to the objective
A user story that has been accepted against the team's Definition of Done
A feature shown to users in the final product demonstration
12.w: Key results are specific, measurable outcomes that indicate progress towards the objective; the objective itself is the clear, aspirational goal (PRINCE2 Agile V2 Glossary, book 12.3.2.3).

n.0: An aspirational goal is the objective, not a key result (Glossary).
n.2: A story meeting the Definition of Done is a completed piece of work, not a measurable outcome set as part of an OKR (book 9.3.2.2).
n.3: Demonstrating features gathers user acceptance at a demo; it is not how a key result is defined (book Table 13.19).

12.q: What is the purpose of the progress review workshop in the 'controlling a stage' process?
o: To prepare for the next iteration by refining, estimating and selecting user stories
To build shared understanding of objectives and plan the next stage with team OKRs
To assess the project's current status, celebrate achievements and address any challenges
To confirm the final product meets requirements and prepare for handover to operations
12.w: The progress review workshop assesses current status, celebrates achievements and addresses challenges using metrics, accomplishments and open risks (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 13.5.4.1).

n.0: Preparing the next iteration is the purpose of the team planning workshop in managing product delivery (book 13.6.4.1).
n.1: Planning the next stage with OKRs is the purpose of the release planning workshop at a stage boundary (book 13.7.4.1).
n.3: Confirming the final product and preparing handover is the purpose of the project closure workshop (book 13.8.4).

12.q: A product owner maintains her team's product backlog. What should she keep it aligned with?
o: The other teams' product backlogs, prioritized by her across teams
The senior supplier's resource plan, which orders the stories
The project backlog, business justification and tolerances
The team plan, which fixes stories for all remaining releases
12.w: The product owner owns the product backlog and keeps it aligned with the project backlog, continued business justification and tolerances, working closely with the CPO (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 7.2).

n.0: Prioritizing across teams is the chief product owner's job, not a product owner's (book Table 7.2).
n.1: The senior supplier represents those who design and build the products; the order of a team's stories is set by priority in its product backlog (book Table 7.2, Glossary).
n.3: The team plan covers the next iteration at task level, not all remaining releases (book Table 8.1).

12.q: Which key characteristic of the agile mindset is about fostering autonomy and self-management within teams?
o: Respect
Adaptability
Empowerment
Transparency and rich communication
12.w: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management within teams (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 2.6.2).

n.0: Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness, not autonomy (book 2.6.2).
n.1: Adaptability concerns inspection and adaptation in response to change (book 2.6.2).
n.3: Transparency concerns open, rich information flow, not freedom to decide (book 2.6.2).

12.q: A project board asks for a clear statement of which features the new online booking system will include and which it will not include. Which performance target does this statement relate to?
o: Quality
Benefits
Scope
Time
12.w: Scope is the performance target describing what the project will deliver and what it will not deliver (out of scope) (PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 1.3.2).

n.0: Quality is about the characteristics that make products fit for purpose, not which features are in or out of the project (book 1.3.2).
n.1: Benefits are the measurable improvements expected from the change, not a list of included and excluded features (book 1.3.2).
n.3: Time concerns when the project and its products will be delivered, not which features are in or out (book 1.3.2).
